topics.label: Trinity
topics.ask: Why it is not a Bible teaching

thoughts.text: I and the Father are one.”

This line is often quoted as if Jesus were claiming to be the Father, or to be one person of a Trinity. The verse does not say that. He has just spoken of his own hand and the Father’s hand. He is the Son the Father sent, and both of them guard the sheep.
The oneness is purpose and action.

The Greek word rendered one is neuter. It means one thing, a unity, not one male person. A masculine form would have been the way to say one person. John uses the same neuter when Jesus prays that his disciples may be one just as he and the Father are one.

AKS reads “I and the Father are one.” It does not read “one God,” “one person,” or “one being.” Two verses later the charge is that he made himself a god, and he answers that he said, “I am God’s Son.”
so that they may all be one, just as You, Father, are in union with Me and I am in union with You, that they also may be in union with Us, so that the world may believe that You sent Me.
The cross-reference. Jesus prays that his followers may all be one just as the Father is in union with him. If “one” here meant one Almighty, the disciples would be that Almighty too.
I will no longer be in the world, but they are in the world, and I am coming to You. Holy Father, protect them by Your name, the name You gave Me, so that they may be one as We are one.
He asks that they may be one just as we are one. The same word, the same kind of unity.
“We are not stoning you for a fine work,” the Jews answered, “but for blasphemy, because you, although being a man, make yourself a god.”
The listeners heard a man making himself a god, not the Father.
then what about the One whom the Father made holy and sent into the world? How then can you accuse Me of blasphemy for stating that I am God’s Son?
Jesus says the statement they attacked was “I am God’s Son.”
You heard Me say, ‘I am going away, and I am coming back to you.’ If you loved Me, you would rejoice that I am going to the Father, because the Father is greater than I.
The Father is greater than I. The two are not the same person and not equal.
Now this is everlasting life, that they may know You, the only true God, and Jesus Christ, whom You have sent.
The Father is the only true God. Jesus is the one he sent.
Listen, O Israel: Jehovah our God is one Jehovah.
Jehovah our God is one Jehovah. One, not three persons in one God.
yet for us there is but one God, the Father, from whom all things came and for whom we exist. And there is but one Lord, Jesus Christ, through whom all things came and through whom we exist.
One God, the Father, and one Lord, Jesus Christ. The verse keeps them distinct.
In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was a god.

John opens by introducing a person called the Word, already existing in the beginning, beside God, and himself divine. The Word is not a saying or a plan. The title with the article presents someone who can be with God and also be spoken of as godlike.

The next lines continue that distinction: the Word was with God, and through him creation took place. Later John says the Word became flesh. The verse is therefore about identity and origin, not only about a message.
AKS’s “a god” is meant to preserve both truths the Greek holds together: the Word is not the Almighty God he was with, and the Word is not a mere creature without divine status.

The Greek wording is built from en arche (“in the beginning”), ho logos (“the Word,” with the article), the verb en (“was”), pros ton theon (“with the God”), and a closing clause, theos en ho logos, where theos has no article and stands before the verb.

The article on the first theos identifies the one the Word was with. The second theos, without the article in this position, describes a quality of the Word. It does not say the Word is the same person as that God.

AKS reads “the Word was a god.” The indefinite article is required by English, not by a Greek article that is missing. The clause keeps the Word distinct from God, which the verse has already said the Word was with, and it still calls the Word divine.
Other renderings say “divine” or “the Word was God.” AKS does not treat those as the same statement. “God” with a capital, in this sentence, would identify the Word as the God he was with.
He was with God in the beginning.
Repeats that the Word was with God, which would be pointless if the Word were that God.
All things came into existence through him, and apart from him not even one thing came into existence.
All things came into existence through the Word, the one who was with God.
The Word became flesh and made His dwelling among us. We have seen His glory, the glory of the only-fathered Son from the Father, full of undeserved kindness and truth.
The Word became flesh, a person who came to dwell among people.
Now this is everlasting life, that they may know You, the only true God, and Jesus Christ, whom You have sent.
Jesus speaks of the Father as the only true God and of himself as the one sent.
The Son is the image of the invisible God, the firstborn of all creation.
The Son is the image of the invisible God and the firstborn of all creation.
To the angel of the congregation in Laodicea write: These are the words of the Amen, the faithful and true Witness, the beginning of the creation by God.
Jesus calls himself the beginning of the creation by God.
Jesus replied, “This is the most important: ‘Hear, O Israel, Jehovah our God is one Jehovah.
This verse quotes or closely cites Deuteronomy 6:4, where the divine name appears. AKS keeps Jehovah in the quotation so the reader can see who is being spoken of in the Hebrew passage.
The name is a translation decision about the quotation, not a claim that every later Greek copy still prints the Hebrew letters.

The Hebrew passage uses the divine name. Later copies of the Christian Greek Scriptures generally use a word meaning Lord (kyrios) where a translator must decide whether the quotation still refers to that name.

AKS uses Jehovah in this quotation because the Hebrew passage being quoted contains the divine name, and the speaker or writer is citing that passage. This note does not claim that a surviving Greek copy of this verse still shows the four letters of the name. It records why the name is restored in the quotation.
Listen, O Israel: Jehovah our God is one Jehovah.
The Shema names Jehovah as the one God of Israel.
In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was a god.
Greek did not use an indefinite article. English still has to show whether the writer is naming the Almighty or describing someone as divine. AKS makes that difference visible.
Theos means god. With the article, in this verse, it identifies the God the Word was with. Without the article, in the predicate before the verb, it describes the Word’s divine quality.
AKS capitalizes God for the one the Word was with, and says “a god” for the Word. See the fuller note on John 1:1.
Now this is everlasting life, that they may know You, the only true God, and Jesus Christ, whom You have sent.
The Father is called the only true God.
In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was a god.
Reducing the title to an idea loses the one who became flesh. The article and the actions John lists mark a person, God’s spokesman, not a floating concept.
Logos can mean a word, a message, or reason. With the article, and with what John says next, it is a title for a person who was with God and later became flesh.
AKS translates the title Word, not Message or Reason. The person can be with God, make things, and dwell among humans.
The Word became flesh and made His dwelling among us. We have seen His glory, the glory of the only-fathered Son from the Father, full of undeserved kindness and truth.
The Word became flesh.
All things came into existence through him, and apart from him not even one thing came into existence.

John has already said the Word was with God. This line says creation happened through him. He is the agent, not the God he was with, and not one of the things that came into existence apart from him. The later letter to the Colossians makes that limit explicit.
The verb describes things coming into existence, not the Word creating himself. He is already present with God in the lines before this one.

AKS says all things came into existence through him, and apart from him not even one thing came into existence. Colossians says the same work with the words all other things, so the Word is not counted among the things made through him.
In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was a god.
The Word was with God before anything is said to have come into existence through him.

For by means of Him all other things were created in the heavens and on the earth, the things visible and the things invisible, whether thrones or lordships or governments or authorities. All other things have been created through Him and for Him.
All other things were created by means of him.
No one has ever seen God. The only-fathered god, who is at the Father's side, is the one who has made Him known.

John has already called the Word a god and said that the Word was with God. This line uses god again for the Son, and it keeps the Father as the God no human has seen. The Son is not a second Almighty. He is the only one who came directly from the Father and then made him known.
The title uses theos, god. The earliest copies read only-begotten god. Some later copies read only-begotten Son. The word only-begotten marks a unique origin, the one produced directly by God.
AKS says the only-begotten god, who is at the Father’s side, is the one who has made God known. No one has seen God. The Son can explain him because he was with him.
In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was a god.
The Word was with God, and the Word was a god.
Now this is everlasting life, that they may know You, the only true God, and Jesus Christ, whom You have sent.
The Father is the only true God, and Jesus is the one he sent.
The Son is the image of the invisible God, the firstborn of all creation.
The Son is the firstborn of all creation.
“Most truly I say to you,” Jesus said, “before Abraham came into existence, I have been.”

The crowd said Jesus was not yet fifty and asked how he had seen Abraham. His answer is about existence before Abraham’s birth. He has just said that the Father is the one who glorifies him, and that the Father is their God. The sentence distinguishes him from that God.

The Greek verb is present in form, but the action started before Abraham came into existence and was still going on. That is why AKS uses I have been. The same verb is rendered I have been when Jesus tells Philip that he has been with them for a long time.
AKS does not turn this sentence into a claim that Jesus is the one who spoke to Moses. It keeps a life that began before Abraham and had not ended.
Jesus answered, “If I glorify Myself, My glory means nothing. The One who glorifies Me is My Father, of whom you say, ‘He is our God.’
The Father, whom they call God, is the one who glorifies Jesus.
Jesus replied, “Philip, I have been with you all this time, and still you do not know Me? Anyone who has seen Me has seen the Father. How can you say, ‘Show us the Father’?
The same verb is rendered I have been with you all this time.
God said to Moses: “I Will Become What I Choose to Become.” And he added: “This is what you are to say to the Israelites, ‘I Will Become has sent me to you.’”
What was spoken to Moses is a different statement, about the one who sent Moses.
who, although he was existing in God’s form, gave no consideration to trying to be equal to God.

Paul is teaching humility. The example is someone who had a high place and did not grasp for a higher one. Equality with God was not his to keep. He emptied himself, became a man, and died on a torture stake. God afterward exalted him.
The order is downward obedience, then a gift of honor from God.

The Greek noun means something to be seized or snatched. It is not a word for holding on to a thing already possessed. If he gave no consideration to seizing equality with God, he was not already that equal.
AKS says that although he was existing in God’s form, he gave no consideration to trying to be equal to God. God’s form means a spirit existence with God, not identity as the Almighty.
More than that, when he came as a man, he humbled himself and became obedient to the point of death, yes, death on a torture stake.
He became obedient as far as death on a torture stake.
For this very reason God exalted him to a superior position and kindly gave him the name that is above every other name,
God exalted him. The higher name was given, not already his as Almighty.
You heard Me say, ‘I am going away, and I am coming back to you.’ If you loved Me, you would rejoice that I am going to the Father, because the Father is greater than I.
Jesus says the Father is greater than he is.
Keep watch over yourselves and the entire flock of which the holy spirit has made you overseers. Be shepherds of the congregation of God, which He purchased with the blood of His own Son.

The overseers shepherd a congregation that God purchased. The price is the blood of his own Son. That keeps the Father as the buyer and the Son as the one who died. The same distinction is in the ransom sayings, where the Son gives his life.

The Greek says through the blood of the own one. It can be read as his own blood or as the blood of his own. The verse has already called the flock God’s. The blood that purchased it is the blood of the Son who belongs to God.
AKS says the congregation of God, which he purchased with the blood of his own Son. It does not say that God himself died.
just as the Son of man did not come to be served, but to serve, and to give his life as a ransom in exchange for many.”
The Son of man gives his life as a ransom.
For God so loved the world that He gave His only-fathered Son, that everyone exercising faith in Him must not perish but have everlasting life.
God gave his only-begotten Son.

For by means of Him all other things were created in the heavens and on the earth, the things visible and the things invisible, whether thrones or lordships or governments or authorities. All other things have been created through Him and for Him.

The Son is the first creation, the agent through whom the rest were made. He is before those other things, and they hold together by means of him. He is also the firstborn from the dead, first of another group.
Firstborn in both places is about being first, not about being the uncreated God.

A bare rendering of the Greek is all things. Left alone, that wording can be heard as if the Son created every thing including himself. The verse before it has already called him the firstborn of all creation.
AKS says by means of him all other things were created, and he is before all other things. Other is required by the context, not by an extra Greek word sitting in the line.
The Son is the image of the invisible God, the firstborn of all creation.
He is the firstborn of all creation.
Also, He is before all other things, and by means of Him all other things were made to exist.
He is before all other things.
All things came into existence through him, and apart from him not even one thing came into existence.
All things came into existence through him.
To the angel of the congregation in Laodicea write: These are the words of the Amen, the faithful and true Witness, the beginning of the creation by God.
He is the beginning of the creation by God.
To the angel of the congregation in Laodicea write: These are the words of the Amen, the faithful and true Witness, the beginning of the creation by God.

Jesus is the Amen, the faithful witness, and the beginning of what God created. That title fits a first creation, not a second Almighty. Proverbs speaks of wisdom produced as the beginning of Jehovah’s way. Colossians calls the Son the firstborn of all creation.
The three lines belong together.
The title is beginning, the start of what God created. AKS does not call him the Originator in the sense of the one who created all things including himself.
AKS reads the beginning of the creation by God. The same person is the firstborn of all creation, and wisdom is described as produced at the start of Jehovah’s way.
The Son is the image of the invisible God, the firstborn of all creation.
The firstborn of all creation.
Jehovah produced me as the beginning of his way, the earliest of his achievements of long ago.
Jehovah produced wisdom as the beginning of his way.
In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was a god.
The Word was with God in the beginning.
Jehovah produced me as the beginning of his way, the earliest of his achievements of long ago.

Wisdom was there before the rest of Jehovah’s works because Jehovah produced wisdom first. That is the same pattern as a Son who is the beginning of the creation by God and the agent of what came after. The speaker is not the everlasting God. Jehovah is the one who produced him.
The Hebrew verb is one the Scriptures also use when a person is brought into existence. Wisdom is speaking as someone Jehovah produced, not as Jehovah himself.
AKS says Jehovah produced me as the beginning of his way, the earliest of his achievements of long ago. Produced replaces a vague first course. The line is about origin.
To the angel of the congregation in Laodicea write: These are the words of the Amen, the faithful and true Witness, the beginning of the creation by God.
The beginning of the creation by God.
The Son is the image of the invisible God, the firstborn of all creation.
The firstborn of all creation.
who gave himself as a corresponding ransom for all—this is to be witnessed to at the proper time.

There is one God, and one mediator, the man Christ Jesus. The ransom is not God paying himself. It is the man Jesus giving a life that corresponds to what was lost. That is why the mediator is called a man, and why the one God and the mediator are not the same person.
The word appears only here. It joins ransom with a prefix meaning in exchange for, or corresponding to. Jesus’ perfect life answers the perfect life Adam lost.
AKS says he gave himself as a corresponding ransom for all. Where Jesus speaks of a ransom in exchange for many, the simpler word for ransom is used. Here Paul uses the fuller word.
For there is one God, and there is one mediator between God and men, a man, Christ Jesus,
One God, and one mediator, the man Christ Jesus.
just as the Son of man did not come to be served, but to serve, and to give his life as a ransom in exchange for many.”
The simpler word, a ransom for many.
So it is written: “The first man Adam became a living soul”; the last Adam a life-giving spirit.
Adam became a living soul. The last Adam is a life-giving spirit.

And we know that the Son of God has come, and he has given us understanding so that we may know the one who is true. And we are in union with the one who is true by means of his Son, Jesus Christ. This is the true God and everlasting life.

An earlier wording could be heard as if the Son were the true God. The line does the opposite. The Son came to make the true one known. Jesus himself called the Father the only true God. This verse agrees with that.

The sentence names the Son, then the one who is true, then says we are in union with that one by means of his Son. This is the true God points back to the one who is true, not to the Son who is the means.
AKS says the Son has given us understanding so that we may know the one who is true, and that we are in union with the one who is true by means of his Son. This is the true God and everlasting life.
Now this is everlasting life, that they may know You, the only true God, and Jesus Christ, whom You have sent.
The Father is the only true God, and Jesus is the one he sent.
But about the Son he says: “God is your throne forever and ever, and the scepter of your kingdom is the scepter of uprightness.”

The psalm was first spoken to a human king whom God appointed. As a prophecy it points to the Messiah, whom God also appoints. Calling the Son God in the sense of addressing the Almighty would ignore the next breath, where his God anoints him above his companions.
The Greek can be read as your throne, O God, or as God is your throne. The next line says God, your God, anointed you. The one addressed has a God. He is not the Almighty.
AKS reads God is your throne forever and ever. Jehovah is the source of the Son’s royal authority. The same decision is used in the psalm being quoted.
You have loved righteousness and hated wickedness; therefore God, Your God, has anointed You above Your companions with the oil of joy.”
God, your God, anointed you.
God is your throne forever and ever, and justice is the scepter of your kingdom.
The psalm says God is your throne.
He will be great and will be called the Son of the Most High. Jehovah God will give Him the throne of His father David,
The throne is given by God.
Now the earth was formless and empty, and darkness was over the surface of the deep. And God’s active force was moving over the surface of the waters.

Scripture speaks of this spirit as God’s breath, his hands, or his fingers, and compares it to water poured out. A craftsman’s hands do not act apart from him. Stephen, full of holy spirit, saw God’s glory and Jesus at God’s right hand, two persons, not three.
The spirit has no personal name.
The Hebrew word can mean breath, wind, or spirit. Here it is God’s own force at work over the waters, not a third person beside him.
AKS says God’s active force was moving over the surface of the waters. Spirit remains a true sense of the word. Person is not.
So if you who are evil know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more will your Father in heaven give the holy spirit to those who ask Him!”
The Father gives holy spirit to those who ask.
But Stephen, full of the holy spirit, looked intently into heaven and saw the glory of God and Jesus standing at the right hand of God.
Stephen saw God and Jesus, not a third person.

“The spirit of Jehovah is on Me, because He has anointed Me to preach good news to the poor. He has sent Me to proclaim liberty to the captives and recovery of sight to the blind, to release the oppressed,
The spirit of Jehovah is Jehovah’s power on the one he sends.
so that they may all be one, just as You, Father, are in union with Me and I am in union with You, that they also may be in union with Us, so that the world may believe that You sent Me.

Read this prayer beside John 10:30. Jesus wants his followers to be one just as he and the Father are one. He even asks that they be in union with the Father and the Son. That cannot mean the disciples become Jehovah, and it cannot mean they join a three-person God.

It means the same oneness he already claimed for himself and the Father: purpose, love, and work. John 10:30, taken alone, is sometimes treated as a Trinity text. This prayer shows what kind of oneness he meant, and it includes humans.

The Greek for one is again neuter, a unity of thing or purpose, not one person. AKS says the Father is in union with the Son, and that the disciples are to be in union with them. Union is shared life and will. It is not fusion into one being.
AKS reads that they may all be one, just as the Father is in union with Jesus and Jesus is in union with the Father, and that they also may be in union with them. The same “one” is asked for humans.
I and the Father are one.”
The line people quote for the Trinity. This prayer defines the oneness.
Now this is everlasting life, that they may know You, the only true God, and Jesus Christ, whom You have sent.
The Father remains the only true God. The Son is the one sent.
I have given them the glory You gave Me, so that they may be one as We are one—
He repeats that they may be one just as we are one.
“We are not stoning you for a fine work,” the Jews answered, “but for blasphemy, because you, although being a man, make yourself a god.”

The crowd’s accusation is not that Jesus said “I and the Father are the same person.” They heard a man speaking as a god. Jesus answers from Psalm 82, where human judges are called gods, and then says the Father sanctified him and sent him.
His own words for the claim are “I am God’s Son.” The verse distinguishes a god from the God who sent him.
The Greek theos here has no article. In this sentence it is “a god,” not “the God,” the Father. Capitalizing God turns the charge into a claim Jesus did not make.
AKS reads that they wanted to stone him because he, although a man, made himself a god. It does not say he made himself God.
I and the Father are one.”
The line that prompted the charge.
then what about the One whom the Father made holy and sent into the world? How then can you accuse Me of blasphemy for stating that I am God’s Son?
He identifies the claim as “I am God’s Son.”
In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was a god.
The Word was a god, and the Word was with God.
I have said, ‘You are gods; you are all sons of the Most High.’
The scripture he quotes, where men are called gods.
You heard Me say, ‘I am going away, and I am coming back to you.’ If you loved Me, you would rejoice that I am going to the Father, because the Father is greater than I.

Jesus tells his disciples to rejoice that he is going to the Father, because the Father is greater. A Trinity that makes the Son equal to the Father in godship has to explain this line away. AKS leaves it as a real comparison.
The Son can be divine, and the Word was a god, without being the God he was with.
Greater compares two persons. Jesus says the Father is greater than he is. That sentence cannot stand if they are the same Almighty, equal in every sense.
AKS reads “the Father is greater than I.” It does not soften the comparison.
I and the Father are one.”
Oneness of purpose is not equality of person.
who, although he was existing in God’s form, gave no consideration to trying to be equal to God.
He did not try to be equal to God.
But I want you to understand that the head of every man is Christ, and the head of the woman is man, and the head of Christ is God.
The head of Christ is God.
Thomas replied, “My Lord and my God!”
A week earlier Jesus had said he was going to his Father and their Father, to his God and their God. Thomas had heard him call the Father the only true God.

“My God” here fits a divine one who represents the true God, the same sense as “the Word was a god,” or the way some Hebrew accounts answer an angelic messenger with words aimed at the God who sent him. It does not undo John 17:3.
John closes the chapter by saying these things were written so that readers would believe Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God, not that he is the only true God.
Thomas speaks to Jesus and says “My Lord and my God.” The words are addressed to him. They still have to be read with what Jesus had just sent them: he was ascending to his Father and his God.
AKS keeps Thomas’s words, “My Lord and my God!” It does not add a claim that Thomas thought Jesus was the Almighty.
“Do not cling to Me,” Jesus said, “for I have not yet ascended to the Father. But go and tell My brothers, ‘I am ascending to My Father and your Father, to My God and your God.’”
Jesus calls the Father “my God and your God.”
Now this is everlasting life, that they may know You, the only true God, and Jesus Christ, whom You have sent.
The Father is the only true God.
But these are written so that you may believe that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God, and that by believing you may have life in His name.
The chapter’s aim is faith that Jesus is the Son of God.
In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was a god.
A god, with God, not the God he was with.
Therefore go and make disciples of all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the holy spirit,

The Trinity is sometimes rested on this commission. The line does not say the three are one God. Elsewhere people are baptized in the name of Jesus, and the spirit is what the Father gives. The Father and the Son are persons. The spirit is God’s active force.
One authority over baptism is not a statement that three persons are the same God.
The verse names the Father, the Son, and the holy spirit under one name, that is, one authority. Naming three together does not make them one being, and the holy spirit is not given a personal name.
AKS says disciples are baptized in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the holy spirit. Spirit is not capitalized as a personal title.
Peter replied, “Repent and be baptized, every one of you, in the name of Jesus Christ for the forgiveness of your sins, and you will receive the gift of the holy spirit.
Baptism is also described as in the name of Jesus Christ.
Now the earth was formless and empty, and darkness was over the surface of the deep. And God’s active force was moving over the surface of the waters.
God’s active force, not a third person.
So if you who are evil know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more will your Father in heaven give the holy spirit to those who ask Him!”
The Father gives holy spirit to those who ask.
yet for us there is but one God, the Father, from whom all things came and for whom we exist. And there is but one Lord, Jesus Christ, through whom all things came and through whom we exist.

If the Trinity were the Bible’s definition of God, this would have been the place to say one God in three persons. Paul says the opposite shape: one God, the Father, and a Lord who is distinct from him and the agent of creation. Jesus is not omitted. He is not called the one God.
Paul says there is one God, and he identifies that one as the Father. He then names one Lord, Jesus Christ, through whom all things came. The two titles are not stacked on one person.
AKS reads one God, the Father, from whom all things came, and one Lord, Jesus Christ, through whom all things came.
Listen, O Israel: Jehovah our God is one Jehovah.
Jehovah our God is one Jehovah.
Now this is everlasting life, that they may know You, the only true God, and Jesus Christ, whom You have sent.
The only true God, and the one he sent.
For there is one God, and there is one mediator between God and men, a man, Christ Jesus,
One God, and one mediator, the man Christ Jesus.
Listen, O Israel: Jehovah our God is one Jehovah.
The word Trinity never appears in Scripture. This is the confession Jesus himself calls the greatest commandment’s opening. Jehovah is one. He is not described here as three coequal persons.
Later lines that are asked to carry that idea, including “I and the Father are one,” have to be read so they do not cancel this sentence.
The confession uses the divine name and the word one. It identifies one person, Jehovah, not a group of persons sharing a title.
AKS reads “Hear, O Israel: Jehovah our God is one Jehovah.” The name is kept, and one is not expanded into three.
Jesus replied, “This is the most important: ‘Hear, O Israel, Jehovah our God is one Jehovah.
Jesus quotes this confession as the first command.
I and the Father are one.”
A different kind of oneness, tested by John 17:21.
May people know that you, whose name is Jehovah, You alone are the Most High over all the earth.
Jehovah alone is the Most High.

Then God said, “Let Us make man in Our image, after Our likeness, to rule over the fish of the sea and the birds of the air, over the livestock, and over all the earth itself and every creature that crawls upon it.”

The plural is real. It is not proof of three persons. Jehovah is speaking to the one who was with him in the beginning, the Son through whom all other things were made. Proverbs speaks of wisdom produced as the beginning of Jehovah’s way, beside him as a master worker.
No third person is addressed. The spirit in the previous verses is God’s active force over the waters, not a consultant in the conversation.
The Hebrew verb is plural, “let us make.” A plural of address can be a speaker talking with another person. It does not, by itself, count how many persons God is.
AKS reads “Let Us make man in Our image.” The next verse returns to singular action: God created.
In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was a god.
The Word was with God in the beginning.
The Son is the image of the invisible God, the firstborn of all creation.
The Son is the firstborn of all creation.
Jehovah produced me as the beginning of his way, the earliest of his achievements of long ago.
Jehovah produced wisdom at the start of his way.
Now the earth was formless and empty, and darkness was over the surface of the deep. And God’s active force was moving over the surface of the waters.
God’s active force, not a third speaker.
For to us a child is born, to us a son is given, and the government will be upon His shoulders. And He will be called Wonderful Counselor, Mighty God, Eternal Father, Prince of Peace.

The child who is born receives titles. Mighty God fits the one who is a god and who rules with real power. It does not make the child the same person as Jehovah. Eternal Father means he becomes a lasting father to the subjects of his government.
Jesus himself prayed to the Father as the only true God. A title in a prophecy does not erase that prayer.

The Hebrew title is Mighty God, a divine title, not the title Almighty. Eternal Father describes the ruler’s future care of his people. It is not the personal name of Jehovah, whom the same book still calls the Father of the Messiah in a different sense: the one who sends him.
AKS says he will be called Wonderful Counselor, Mighty God, Eternal Father, Prince of Peace. It does not say Almighty God.
Now this is everlasting life, that they may know You, the only true God, and Jesus Christ, whom You have sent.
The Father is the only true God.
In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was a god.
The Word was a god.
He will be great and will be called the Son of the Most High. Jehovah God will give Him the throne of His father David,
Jehovah gives him David’s throne. The Son of the Most High is not the Most High.
For there are three that testify:

A line that sounds like a definition of the Trinity was written into some later manuscripts of this letter and then into older English Bibles. It is not part of the letter. AKS follows the text that does not contain it.
Nothing in the real sentence says the Father, the Son, and the spirit are one God. The witnesses agree. Witnesses that agree are not one person.

Some later copies insert a sentence about the Father, the Word, and the holy spirit, and about those three being one. Those words are not in the early text. The three that testify in this passage are the spirit, the water, and the blood.
AKS reads “there are three that testify,” and the next verse names the spirit, the water, and the blood. It does not print a Trinity formula here.
the spirit, the water, and the blood—and these three are in agreement.
The three are the spirit, the water, and the blood.
Now this is everlasting life, that they may know You, the only true God, and Jesus Christ, whom You have sent.
The only true God is the Father.

topics.label: Hellfire
topics.ask: Why the penalty is death, not torment

thoughts.text: For the living know that they will die, but the dead know nothing. They have no further reward, because the memory of them is forgotten.

The teaching of a burning hell, where the wicked stay alive in pain forever, is not in this text or in the words the Bible actually uses for the dead. The wage sin pays is death, not endless life in misery. Faithful people expected to go to the Grave.

Jesus was in the Grave until he was raised. A place that holds the righteous and the Christ is not a chamber of fire. Gehenna and the lake of fire are a different picture: destruction, the second death, not a life that never ends.
Sheol, the place of the dead, is the Grave. The dead are not described as conscious, and a conscious torment cannot be read into a verse that says they know nothing.
AKS says the dead know nothing, and in the Grave there is no work or planning or knowledge or wisdom. It does not call that place a fire.
Whatever you find to do with your hands, do it with all your might, for in the Grave, where you are going, there is no work or planning or knowledge or wisdom.
No knowledge or wisdom in the Grave.
Look, every soul belongs to Me; both father and son are Mine. The soul who sins is the one who will die.
The soul that sins will die.
For the wages sin pays is death, but the gift God gives is everlasting life by Christ Jesus our Lord.
The wages of sin is death.
Foreseeing this, David spoke about the resurrection of the Christ, that He was not abandoned to the Grave, nor did His body see decay.
The Christ was not abandoned to the Grave.
Do not be afraid of those who kill the body but cannot kill the soul. Instead, fear the One who can destroy both soul and body in Gehenna.
God can destroy both soul and body in Gehenna.
Then Death and the Grave were thrown into the lake of fire. This is the second death—the lake of fire.
The lake of fire is the second death.
They have built high places to Baal on which to burn their children in the fire as offerings to Baal—something I never commanded or mentioned, nor had it even come into My heart.
Burning children in the fire never came into God’s heart.

But I tell you that anyone who is angry with his brother will be subject to judgment. Again, anyone who says to his brother, ‘Raca,’ will be subject to the Sanhedrin. But anyone who says, ‘You fool!’ will be subject to the fire of Gehenna.
Jesus warns that angry contempt can lead to Gehenna. Because AKS uses Grave for the common grave of the dead, this stronger word stays in place. The two must not be translated as if they were one.
Gehenna names the valley used as a picture of destruction. It is a different word from Hades.
AKS keeps Gehenna, so it is not confused with Grave. The warning is judgment that destroys, not life in another world.
Then Death and the Grave were thrown into the lake of fire. This is the second death—the lake of fire.
The lake of fire is called the second death, destruction rather than preservation.
And Jesus said to him: “Truly I tell you today, you will be with me in Paradise.”

Jesus had said he would be killed and raised on the third day. On the day he was raised he said he had not yet ascended to the Father. The criminal could not be with him in Paradise on the day of the execution.

Today belongs with the moment Jesus gave his word, the way solemn promises in the Hebrew Scriptures use today. The Paradise he promised is the restored earth, the home of the great crowd, not heaven that afternoon.
The Greek word for today can stand with the promise or with the day the promise was spoken. The written text had no comma. AKS places the pause after today.
AKS reads, Truly I tell you today, you will be with me in Paradise. The man was not told that he would be in Paradise that same afternoon.
“The Son of man must suffer many things,” He said. “He must be rejected by the elders, chief priests, and scribes, and He must be killed and on the third day be raised to life.”
Jesus said he would be raised on the third day.
“Do not cling to Me,” Jesus said, “for I have not yet ascended to the Father. But go and tell My brothers, ‘I am ascending to My Father and your Father, to My God and your God.’”
After his death he had not yet ascended to the Father.
For the living know that they will die, but the dead know nothing. They have no further reward, because the memory of them is forgotten.
The dead know nothing, so the man was not alive in Paradise that day.
And these will go away into everlasting cutting-off, but the righteous into everlasting life.

The goats go to a cutting-off from which there is no resurrection. The sheep receive life that does not end. The verse is not a picture of an immortal soul suffering forever. Death is the loss. Life is the gift.
The Greek word is used of pruning, cutting off what is taken away. It is not a word for keeping a person alive in pain. Everlasting describes the result. The person is cut off from life.
AKS says everlasting cutting-off, and everlasting life for the righteous. The two outcomes are opposites. One ends life. The other continues it.
For God so loved the world that He gave His only-fathered Son, that everyone exercising faith in Him must not perish but have everlasting life.
The alternative to perishing is everlasting life.
For the wages sin pays is death, but the gift God gives is everlasting life by Christ Jesus our Lord.
The wages of sin is death. The gift is everlasting life.
Do not be afraid of those who kill the body but cannot kill the soul. Instead, fear the One who can destroy both soul and body in Gehenna.
If the soul could not die, this warning would be empty. Jesus says the soul can be destroyed. That is the opposite of a hell where a deathless soul is kept alive to suffer.
Gehenna stays in AKS as its own word so it is not confused with the Grave, and so it is not turned into a fire that never finishes its work.
Gehenna is not the common grave. The warning is that God can destroy soul and body there. Destroy is the end of the person, not the preservation of the person in pain.
AKS says fear the One who can destroy both soul and body in Gehenna. The soul is not said to survive the destruction.
Look, every soul belongs to Me; both father and son are Mine. The soul who sins is the one who will die.
The soul that sins will die.

But I tell you that anyone who is angry with his brother will be subject to judgment. Again, anyone who says to his brother, ‘Raca,’ will be subject to the Sanhedrin. But anyone who says, ‘You fool!’ will be subject to the fire of Gehenna.
Gehenna is kept distinct from the Grave.
Then Death and the Grave were thrown into the lake of fire. This is the second death—the lake of fire.
The lake of fire is the second death.
They have built high places to Baal on which to burn their children in the fire as offerings to Baal—something I never commanded or mentioned, nor had it even come into My heart.
That kind of fire never came into God’s heart.
Then Death and the Grave were thrown into the lake of fire. This is the second death—the lake of fire.

Hellfire, as a never-ending burning of living souls, cannot be this lake. The Grave itself is ended here. The explanation supplied in the verse is death, a second death, not a second life. People who were dead are not pictured as moving into an immortal suffering.
Death is removed.
The verse explains its own symbol. Death and the Grave are thrown into the lake of fire, and “this is the second death.” A grave that can be destroyed is not a place of eternal life in torment.
AKS says Death and the Grave were thrown into the lake of fire. This is the second death, the lake of fire.
For the living know that they will die, but the dead know nothing. They have no further reward, because the memory of them is forgotten.
The dead know nothing.
For the wages sin pays is death, but the gift God gives is everlasting life by Christ Jesus our Lord.
Death is the wage. Life is the gift.
And these will go away into everlasting cutting-off, but the righteous into everlasting life.
Everlasting cutting-off, the opposite of everlasting life.
In the Grave, where he was in torment, he looked up and saw Abraham from afar, with Lazarus by his side.

The rich man and Lazarus are not two men reporting from the other side of death. The dead know nothing, and in the Grave there is no knowledge. Jesus is answering people who would not listen. The rich man stands for the proud religious leaders.
Lazarus stands for the lowly ones who did listen. The last line is the point. If they will not hear Moses and the Prophets, they will not be persuaded even if someone rises from the dead.

The word for Grave is Hades, the common grave of mankind. It is not a region where the dead stay awake. The torment is inside the story. The same Bible says the dead know nothing, so the story cannot be a report of their condition.
AKS says in the Grave, where he was in torment. It does not say the dead are conscious. The line belongs to an illustration.
For the living know that they will die, but the dead know nothing. They have no further reward, because the memory of them is forgotten.
The dead know nothing. A conscious rich man would undo that.
Whatever you find to do with your hands, do it with all your might, for in the Grave, where you are going, there is no work or planning or knowledge or wisdom.
In the Grave there is no work, knowledge, or planning.
Then Abraham said to him, ‘If they do not listen to Moses and the Prophets, they will not be persuaded even if someone rises from the dead.’”
The illustration ends on refusing Moses and the Prophets.
They have built high places to Baal on which to burn their children in the fire as offerings to Baal—something I never commanded or mentioned, nor had it even come into My heart.
Hellfire says God keeps people alive in fire. Jehovah says the burning of children as offerings never came into his heart. He had not commanded it and he had not spoken of it.
The valley where that was done later stood for slaughter and for the dead, not for a life inside the flames. Gehenna destroys. It does not carry out a thought God says never entered his heart.
The Hebrew says this never came up into the heart. Heart is desire and intention. The sentence is about what God would not think of doing, not about a place he prepared.
AKS says they burned their children in the fire as offerings to Baal, something Jehovah never commanded, nor had it even come into My heart. Jeremiah 7:31 and 32:35 say the same thing.
They have built the high places of Topheth in the Valley of Ben-hinnom so they could burn their sons and daughters in the fire—something I never commanded, nor had it even come into My heart.
The same words: burning sons and daughters never came into his heart.

They have built the high places of Baal in the Valley of Ben-hinnom to make their sons and daughters pass through the fire to Molech—something I never commanded them, nor had it ever come into My heart, that they should commit such a detestable thing and cause Judah to sin.
Passing children through the fire never entered his heart.
For the living know that they will die, but the dead know nothing. They have no further reward, because the memory of them is forgotten.
The dead know nothing, so they are not alive in the fire.
Do not be afraid of those who kill the body but cannot kill the soul. Instead, fear the One who can destroy both soul and body in Gehenna.
Gehenna is destruction of soul and body.
It is not the dead who praise Jah, nor any who descend into silence.
If the dead were alive in another place, this line would be false. They do not praise. They go down into silence. Hellfire needs the dead to be awake. The psalm says they are not.
Praise and silence are the contrast. The dead do not praise. Those who go down are in silence, not in a conscious torment where they could still cry out.
AKS says it is not the dead who praise Jah, nor any who descend into silence. Silence is the state. Jah is the short form of the divine name, and AKS keeps it.
For the living know that they will die, but the dead know nothing. They have no further reward, because the memory of them is forgotten.
The dead know nothing.
When his spirit departs, he returns to the ground; on that very day his plans perish.
His plans perish the day he dies.
Whatever you find to do with your hands, do it with all your might, for in the Grave, where you are going, there is no work or planning or knowledge or wisdom.

The writer tells the living to work with all their might because the place they are going has none of that activity. A conscious afterlife, whether of pleasure or of pain, would still be a kind of knowing. This verse says the Grave has none.
Sheol is the common grave. The list that follows is work, planning, knowledge, and wisdom. All four are absent there.
AKS says in the Grave, where you are going, there is no work or planning or knowledge or wisdom. Grave is Sheol. It is not rendered as a fiery hell.
For the living know that they will die, but the dead know nothing. They have no further reward, because the memory of them is forgotten.
The dead know nothing at all.
It is not the dead who praise Jah, nor any who descend into silence.
They descend into silence.
For the wages sin pays is death, but the gift God gives is everlasting life by Christ Jesus our Lord.

Sin does not pay a person by keeping him alive to suffer. It pays death. Life that does not end is a gift, and the verse says where that gift is found: by Christ Jesus. An immortal soul would already be drawing wages the verse does not offer.
Wages are what the work pays. The pay for sin is death, not life in another form. The opposite gift is everlasting life, and it comes by Christ Jesus, not from a soul that already had it.
AKS says the wages sin pays is death, but the gift God gives is everlasting life by Christ Jesus our Lord. Death and life are the two outcomes. The life is given through him, not absorbed into him.
Look, every soul belongs to Me; both father and son are Mine. The soul who sins is the one who will die.
The soul who sins will die.
By the sweat of your face you will eat bread until you return to the ground, for out of it you were taken. For dust you are and to dust you will return.”
The sentence on Adam was a return to dust.

“For look! the day is coming, burning like a furnace, when all the arrogant and every evildoer will be stubble; the day is coming when I will set them ablaze,” says Jehovah of armies. “Not a root or branch will be left to them.”
The wicked become like chaff that is burned up. Stubble does not burn forever. It is consumed.
Yet a little while, and the wicked will be no more; though you look for them, they will not be found.
Look for the wicked and they are gone. They are not preserved alive in order to be punished without end.

topics.label: Soul
topics.ask: Why the soul is not immortal

thoughts.text: Look, every soul belongs to Me; both father and son are Mine. The soul who sins is the one who will die.

Genesis does not say God put a soul into Adam. The man became a living soul. Ezekiel says that soul can die. The dead know nothing, and on the day a person dies his plans perish. Immortality is not the human condition.

It is something the mortal must be clothed with, a gift tied to the resurrection, not a possession brought out of Eden. The teaching that everyone already has a deathless soul is what makes hellfire seem possible. The Bible removes the premise. The soul dies.
Life after death is a resurrection, not a soul that never left.
Nephesh, soul, is the person. This verse says the soul that sins will die. A soul that dies is not an immortal part that leaves the body and cannot die.
AKS says every soul belongs to God, and the soul who sins is the one who will die. Soul is not changed into “immortal soul.”
Then Jehovah God formed the man from the dust of the ground and blew the breath of life into his nostrils, and the man became a living soul.
The man became a living soul.
For the living know that they will die, but the dead know nothing. They have no further reward, because the memory of them is forgotten.
The dead know nothing.
When his spirit departs, he returns to the ground; on that very day his plans perish.
His spirit departs, and that day his plans perish.
For the wages sin pays is death, but the gift God gives is everlasting life by Christ Jesus our Lord.
The wage is death. Life is a gift.
For the perishable must be clothed with the imperishable, and the mortal with immortality.
The mortal puts on immortality. He does not already have it.
Do not be amazed at this, for the hour is coming in which all those in the memorial tombs will hear his voice
Those in the memorial tombs will hear his voice.
And Jesus said to him: “Truly I tell you today, you will be with me in Paradise.”

Jesus had said he would be killed and raised on the third day. On the day he was raised he said he had not yet ascended to the Father. The criminal could not be with him in Paradise on the day of the execution.

The Greek word for today can stand with the promise or with the day the promise was spoken. The written text had no comma. AKS places the pause after today.
AKS reads, Truly I tell you today, you will be with me in Paradise. The man was not told that he would be in Paradise that same afternoon.
“The Son of man must suffer many things,” He said. “He must be rejected by the elders, chief priests, and scribes, and He must be killed and on the third day be raised to life.”
Jesus said he would be raised on the third day.
“Do not cling to Me,” Jesus said, “for I have not yet ascended to the Father. But go and tell My brothers, ‘I am ascending to My Father and your Father, to My God and your God.’”
After his death he had not yet ascended to the Father.
For the living know that they will die, but the dead know nothing. They have no further reward, because the memory of them is forgotten.
The dead know nothing, so the man was not alive in Paradise that day.
And these will go away into everlasting cutting-off, but the righteous into everlasting life.

The goats go to a cutting-off from which there is no resurrection. The sheep receive life that does not end. The verse is not a picture of an immortal soul suffering forever. Death is the loss. Life is the gift.
The Greek word is used of pruning, cutting off what is taken away. It is not a word for keeping a person alive in pain. Everlasting describes the result. The person is cut off from life.
AKS says everlasting cutting-off, and everlasting life for the righteous. The two outcomes are opposites. One ends life. The other continues it.
For God so loved the world that He gave His only-fathered Son, that everyone exercising faith in Him must not perish but have everlasting life.
The alternative to perishing is everlasting life.
For the wages sin pays is death, but the gift God gives is everlasting life by Christ Jesus our Lord.
The wages of sin is death. The gift is everlasting life.
For the living know that they will die, but the dead know nothing. They have no further reward, because the memory of them is forgotten.

The teaching of a burning hell, where the wicked stay alive in pain forever, is not in this text or in the words the Bible actually uses for the dead. The wage sin pays is death, not endless life in misery. Faithful people expected to go to the Grave.

Jesus was in the Grave until he was raised. A place that holds the righteous and the Christ is not a chamber of fire. Gehenna and the lake of fire are a different picture: destruction, the second death, not a life that never ends.
Sheol, the place of the dead, is the Grave. The dead are not described as conscious, and a conscious torment cannot be read into a verse that says they know nothing.
AKS says the dead know nothing, and in the Grave there is no work or planning or knowledge or wisdom. It does not call that place a fire.
Whatever you find to do with your hands, do it with all your might, for in the Grave, where you are going, there is no work or planning or knowledge or wisdom.
No knowledge or wisdom in the Grave.
Look, every soul belongs to Me; both father and son are Mine. The soul who sins is the one who will die.
The soul that sins will die.
For the wages sin pays is death, but the gift God gives is everlasting life by Christ Jesus our Lord.
The wages of sin is death.
Foreseeing this, David spoke about the resurrection of the Christ, that He was not abandoned to the Grave, nor did His body see decay.
The Christ was not abandoned to the Grave.
Do not be afraid of those who kill the body but cannot kill the soul. Instead, fear the One who can destroy both soul and body in Gehenna.
God can destroy both soul and body in Gehenna.
Then Death and the Grave were thrown into the lake of fire. This is the second death—the lake of fire.
The lake of fire is the second death.
They have built high places to Baal on which to burn their children in the fire as offerings to Baal—something I never commanded or mentioned, nor had it even come into My heart.
Burning children in the fire never came into God’s heart.
For the perishable must be clothed with the imperishable, and the mortal with immortality.

Paul is talking about a change at the resurrection, not about a person who is already deathless inside a body. If humans were born immortal, there would be nothing to put on. Death is swallowed up when that clothing is given, which means death was real until then.
The mortal puts immortality on. The wording is clothing received, not a soul uncovered at death.
AKS says the mortal must be clothed with immortality. It does not say the soul is released into immortality.
Look, every soul belongs to Me; both father and son are Mine. The soul who sins is the one who will die.
The soul who sins will die.
Then Jehovah God formed the man from the dust of the ground and blew the breath of life into his nostrils, and the man became a living soul.
A living soul, not an immortal soul placed in a body.
When his spirit departs, he returns to the ground; on that very day his plans perish.

Death here is a return to the ground and the end of thought. It is not the start of another life in heaven, hell, or a spirit world. The hope the Bible offers the dead is that they will live again, not that they never really died.
The spirit that departs is the life-breath. The same verse says that on that day his plans perish. A conscious person traveling on would still have plans.
AKS says his spirit departs, he returns to the ground, and on that very day his plans perish.
For the living know that they will die, but the dead know nothing. They have no further reward, because the memory of them is forgotten.
The dead know nothing.
Then Jehovah God formed the man from the dust of the ground and blew the breath of life into his nostrils, and the man became a living soul.
Life began when God gave breath.
Do not be amazed at this, for the hour is coming in which all those in the memorial tombs will hear his voice
The dead in the graves hear his voice.
Do not be amazed at this, for the hour is coming in which all those in the memorial tombs will hear his voice

Resurrection is the Bible’s hope for the dead, because death is real. Those who did good come out to a resurrection of life. Those who did evil come out to a resurrection of judgment. Paul told a court that he hoped for a resurrection of both the righteous and the unrighteous.
If the soul had never died, there would be no one in the memorial tombs to call. Jesus told Martha, before he called Lazarus out of a tomb, that he is the resurrection and the life.
The dead are in the memorial tombs. They hear his voice there. They are not described as already alive somewhere else, waiting to be improved.
AKS says the hour is coming when all who are in the memorial tombs will hear his voice and come out.
and come out—those who have done good to the resurrection of life, and those who have done evil to the resurrection of judgment.
A resurrection of life and a resurrection of judgment.
and I have the same hope in God that they themselves cherish, that there will be a resurrection of both the righteous and the wicked.
Both the righteous and the wicked.
Jesus said to her, “I am the resurrection and the life. Whoever exercises faith in Me will live, even though he dies.
Jesus is the resurrection and the life.
For the living know that they will die, but the dead know nothing. They have no further reward, because the memory of them is forgotten.
Until that call, the dead know nothing.
Your dead will live; their bodies will rise. Awake and sing, you who dwell in the dust! For your dew is like the dew of the morning, and the earth will bring forth her dead.
The dead will live. Those in the dust will awake.
It is not the dead who praise Jah, nor any who descend into silence.
If the dead were alive in another place, this line would be false. They do not praise. They go down into silence. Hellfire needs the dead to be awake. The psalm says they are not.
Praise and silence are the contrast. The dead do not praise. Those who go down are in silence, not in a conscious torment where they could still cry out.
AKS says it is not the dead who praise Jah, nor any who descend into silence. Silence is the state. Jah is the short form of the divine name, and AKS keeps it.
For the living know that they will die, but the dead know nothing. They have no further reward, because the memory of them is forgotten.
The dead know nothing.
When his spirit departs, he returns to the ground; on that very day his plans perish.
His plans perish the day he dies.
For the wages sin pays is death, but the gift God gives is everlasting life by Christ Jesus our Lord.

Sin does not pay a person by keeping him alive to suffer. It pays death. Life that does not end is a gift, and the verse says where that gift is found: by Christ Jesus. An immortal soul would already be drawing wages the verse does not offer.
Wages are what the work pays. The pay for sin is death, not life in another form. The opposite gift is everlasting life, and it comes by Christ Jesus, not from a soul that already had it.
AKS says the wages sin pays is death, but the gift God gives is everlasting life by Christ Jesus our Lord. Death and life are the two outcomes. The life is given through him, not absorbed into him.
Look, every soul belongs to Me; both father and son are Mine. The soul who sins is the one who will die.
The soul who sins will die.
By the sweat of your face you will eat bread until you return to the ground, for out of it you were taken. For dust you are and to dust you will return.”
The sentence on Adam was a return to dust.
Then Jehovah God formed the man from the dust of the ground and blew the breath of life into his nostrils, and the man became a living soul.

A soul can die. Ezekiel says the soul who sins is the one who will die. A translation that says “immortal soul” adds a doctrine the words do not carry. You are a soul. You do not possess a second self that leaves at death and keeps on living.
The Hebrew נֶפֶשׁ (nephesh) is a living person or a life that can die. The Greek ψυχή (psyche) carries the same range. Neither word names an immortal wisp living inside a body.
AKS reads “the man became a living soul.” Became is the sentence. It does not say the man was given a soul. He is the soul, formed from dust, made alive by breath.
Look, every soul belongs to Me; both father and son are Mine. The soul who sins is the one who will die.
The soul who sins is the one who will die. The soul is not deathless.
For the living know that they will die, but the dead know nothing. They have no further reward, because the memory of them is forgotten.
The dead know nothing. A soul that has died is not awake somewhere else.
Do not be afraid of those who kill the body but cannot kill the soul. Instead, fear the One who can destroy both soul and body in Gehenna.
God can destroy both soul and body in Gehenna.

The soul who sins is the one who will die. A son will not bear the wrongdoing of his father, and a father will not bear the wrongdoing of his son. The righteousness of the righteous man will fall upon him, and the wickedness of the wicked man will fall upon him.
The soul who sins is the one who dies. The person is the soul. The person dies.
He alone is immortal and dwells in unapproachable light. No one has ever seen Him, nor can anyone see Him. To Him be honor and eternal dominion! Amen.
God alone has immortality. It is not a possession every human already carries.

topics.label: Spirit
topics.ask: God’s active force, not a person

thoughts.text: the spirit of truth. The world cannot receive it, because it neither sees it nor knows it. But you do know it, for it abides with you and will be in you.

The holy spirit is God’s active force, not a third person beside the Father and the Son. A person is not poured out, and a person is not extinguished. The helper teaches and reminds, the way a force sent by the Father does that work.
Stephen, full of holy spirit, looked into heaven and saw God and Jesus. He did not see a third person. The spirit has no personal name.
Pneuma, spirit, is neuter. In this verse the pronouns that follow are neuter too. English often says he, because helper sounds like a person. The Greek says it.
AKS says the world cannot receive it, because it neither sees it nor knows it. The helper is the spirit of truth, and the spirit is it.
Now the earth was formless and empty, and darkness was over the surface of the deep. And God’s active force was moving over the surface of the waters.
God’s active force was moving over the waters.
However, when the spirit of truth comes, it will guide you into all truth. For it will not speak of its own initiative, but it will speak what it hears, and it will declare to you what is to come.
When the spirit of truth comes, it guides. It does not speak of its own initiative.
‘In the last days, God says, I will pour out my spirit on all people. Your sons and daughters will prophesy, your young men will see visions, your old men will dream dreams.
God pours out his spirit. Persons are not poured out.
Do not extinguish the spirit.
Do not extinguish the spirit.
But Stephen, full of the holy spirit, looked intently into heaven and saw the glory of God and Jesus standing at the right hand of God.
Stephen saw God and Jesus, two persons.
Now the earth was formless and empty, and darkness was over the surface of the deep. And God’s active force was moving over the surface of the waters.

Scripture speaks of this spirit as God’s breath, his hands, or his fingers, and compares it to water poured out. A craftsman’s hands do not act apart from him. Stephen, full of holy spirit, saw God’s glory and Jesus at God’s right hand, two persons, not three.
The spirit has no personal name.
The Hebrew word can mean breath, wind, or spirit. Here it is God’s own force at work over the waters, not a third person beside him.
AKS says God’s active force was moving over the surface of the waters. Spirit remains a true sense of the word. Person is not.
So if you who are evil know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more will your Father in heaven give the holy spirit to those who ask Him!”
The Father gives holy spirit to those who ask.
But Stephen, full of the holy spirit, looked intently into heaven and saw the glory of God and Jesus standing at the right hand of God.
Stephen saw God and Jesus, not a third person.

“The spirit of Jehovah is on Me, because He has anointed Me to preach good news to the poor. He has sent Me to proclaim liberty to the captives and recovery of sight to the blind, to release the oppressed,
The spirit of Jehovah is Jehovah’s power on the one he sends.
As soon as Jesus was baptized, He went up out of the water. Suddenly the heavens were opened, and He saw the spirit of God descending like a dove and resting on Him.
At the baptism the reader can count the persons who speak and are seen as persons: Jesus in the water, and the Father whose voice comes from heaven. The spirit is what descends on the Son.
It is compared to a bird, the way Scripture compares God’s power to breath, wind, or something poured out. That picture is not a third Almighty.

The spirit is compared to a dove that descends and rests. A person is not described as arriving and taking a seat beside the Father. The one in the water is Jesus. The voice that follows is the Father’s.
AKS says the spirit of God descending like a dove and resting on Him. Spirit is not capitalized as a personal name. He went up out of the water, which is what immersion looks like.
Now the earth was formless and empty, and darkness was over the surface of the deep. And God’s active force was moving over the surface of the waters.
God’s active force, not a third person.
the spirit of truth. The world cannot receive it, because it neither sees it nor knows it. But you do know it, for it abides with you and will be in you.
The helper is called it.
And they were all filled with the holy spirit and began to speak in other tongues as the spirit enabled them.

What the disciples receive at Pentecost is holy spirit, and it fills them. Filling is what you say of a force or a gift that takes hold of a person. You do not fill a room with a person in that sense and then say the person enabled the speaking.
The gift is from the Father, through the Son.
Filled with is the language of something people receive and are enabled by. They speak as the spirit enables them. The spirit is not introduced here as a person who sits down and talks beside them.
AKS says they were filled with the holy spirit and began to speak in other tongues as the spirit enabled them. Spirit stays lowercase. Enabled keeps the spirit as the power behind the speech.
So if you who are evil know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more will your Father in heaven give the holy spirit to those who ask Him!”
The Father gives holy spirit to those who ask.
Peter replied, “Repent and be baptized, every one of you, in the name of Jesus Christ for the forgiveness of your sins, and you will receive the gift of the holy spirit.
The gift of the holy spirit follows baptism.
As soon as Jesus came up out of the water, He saw the heavens breaking open and the spirit descending on Him like a dove.

Jesus’ own baptism was in the Jordan, and he came up out of the water. That is the act later commanded for disciples. The spirit descends on him. The Father is the one who speaks in the matching account. Two persons, and the spirit as what comes upon the Son.

Came up out of the water means he had been in it. Immediately the spirit descends like a dove. The baptism of Jesus is the pattern of immersion, and the spirit is again compared to a bird resting, not introduced as a third speaker.
AKS says as soon as Jesus came up out of the water, he saw the heavens breaking open and the spirit descending on Him like a dove. Out of the water is the immersion. Spirit is lowercase.
As soon as Jesus was baptized, He went up out of the water. Suddenly the heavens were opened, and He saw the spirit of God descending like a dove and resting on Him.
He went up out of the water, and the spirit descended like a dove.
He gave orders to stop the chariot. Then both Philip and the eunuch went down into the water, and Philip baptized him.
Philip and the eunuch go down into the water.
For prophecy was at no time brought by man’s will, but men spoke from God as they were moved by holy spirit.
Peter denies that prophecy is a human project. The men spoke, so the books have human writers, languages, and styles. They spoke from God, moved by holy spirit, so the result is inspired of God.
The spirit here is the force that moved them, not another God dictating in his own name.

No prophecy was brought by man’s will. Men spoke from God as they were moved by holy spirit. The will that produced it is God’s. The speakers are men. The spirit is what moved them, which fits spirit as God’s active force rather than a third author sitting beside the Father.

AKS says prophecy was at no time brought by man’s will, but men spoke from God as they were moved by holy spirit. Moved keeps the sense of being carried. Holy spirit is lowercase, God’s power moving the speakers.
All Scripture is inspired of God and beneficial for teaching, for reproving, for setting things straight, for disciplining in righteousness,
All Scripture is inspired of God.
Now the earth was formless and empty, and darkness was over the surface of the deep. And God’s active force was moving over the surface of the waters.
God’s active force at work.
God is a Spirit, and His worshipers must worship Him in spirit and in truth.”

Jesus has said the Father is seeking worshipers. Then he says why location does not matter. God is a Spirit. You do not worship a spirit by bowing to a carving or by insisting on one mountain. You worship the Father in spirit and truth. The holy spirit remains his active force.
This verse is about what God is, not about a third person replacing the Father.

Pneuma here describes God’s kind of being. He is not flesh that must be approached on one mountain. An indefinite article in English marks a classification: he is spirit in nature. It does not identify God as the holy spirit, the force he sends. The holy spirit is God’s, upon people.
God himself is the Father Jesus has just named.

AKS says “God is a Spirit, and His worshipers must worship Him in spirit and in truth.” A Spirit classifies his nature. Capitalizing Spirit does not install a personal name. Him is the Father. Worship in spirit is worship that fits a God who is not an image and not confined to a place.
But a time is coming and has now come when the true worshipers will worship the Father in spirit and in truth, for the Father is seeking such as these to worship Him.
The Father is the one who is worshiped.
I am Jehovah; that is My name! I will not yield My glory to another or My praise to idols.
He does not give his praise to idols.
And I will ask the Father, and He will give you another helper to be with you forever—
The helper is holy spirit, which Jesus asks the Father to send. It is given. It is not a person who sends himself.
The angel replied, “The holy spirit will come upon you, and the power of the Most High will overshadow you. So the Holy One to be born will be called the Son of God.
Holy spirit comes upon Mary and the power of the Most High overshadows her. Power is the parallel. A person is not.
For there are three that testify:
The witness is the spirit, the water, and the blood. The three agree. Water and blood are not persons, and the spirit is grouped with them.

topics.label: Death
topics.ask: Why death is not a door to another life

thoughts.text: By the sweat of your face you will eat bread until you return to the ground, for out of it you were taken. For dust you are and to dust you will return.”

Christendom treats death as a doorway, the soul departing to heaven, hell, or a place of cleansing. God told Adam he would go back to the ground. The dead know nothing. Jesus called Lazarus asleep, then said plainly that he was dead.
The hope that follows is a resurrection from the graves, not a life the dead are already living.
The sentence returns the man to the ground he was taken from. Dust does not describe a conscious person leaving for another world.
AKS says dust you are, and to dust you shall return. The penalty stated to Adam is death, not torment and not heaven.
For the living know that they will die, but the dead know nothing. They have no further reward, because the memory of them is forgotten.
The dead know nothing.
Whatever you find to do with your hands, do it with all your might, for in the Grave, where you are going, there is no work or planning or knowledge or wisdom.
In the Grave there is no knowledge or planning.
When his spirit departs, he returns to the ground; on that very day his plans perish.
His thoughts perish the day he returns to the ground.
After He had said this, He told them, “Our friend Lazarus has fallen asleep, but I am going there to wake him up.”
Jesus calls that death sleep.
So Jesus told them plainly, “Lazarus is dead,
He then says plainly that Lazarus is dead.
And many who sleep in the dust of the earth will awake, some to everlasting life, but others to shame and everlasting contempt.
Those asleep in the dust awake. They were not already awake.
And Jesus said to him: “Truly I tell you today, you will be with me in Paradise.”

Jesus had said he would be killed and raised on the third day. On the day he was raised he said he had not yet ascended to the Father. The criminal could not be with him in Paradise on the day of the execution.

Today belongs with the moment Jesus gave his word, the way solemn promises in the Hebrew Scriptures use today. The Paradise he promised is the restored earth, the home of the great crowd, not heaven that afternoon.
The Greek word for today can stand with the promise or with the day the promise was spoken. The written text had no comma. AKS places the pause after today.
AKS reads, Truly I tell you today, you will be with me in Paradise. The man was not told that he would be in Paradise that same afternoon.
“The Son of man must suffer many things,” He said. “He must be rejected by the elders, chief priests, and scribes, and He must be killed and on the third day be raised to life.”
Jesus said he would be raised on the third day.
“Do not cling to Me,” Jesus said, “for I have not yet ascended to the Father. But go and tell My brothers, ‘I am ascending to My Father and your Father, to My God and your God.’”
After his death he had not yet ascended to the Father.
For the living know that they will die, but the dead know nothing. They have no further reward, because the memory of them is forgotten.
The dead know nothing, so the man was not alive in Paradise that day.
For the living know that they will die, but the dead know nothing. They have no further reward, because the memory of them is forgotten.

The teaching of a burning hell, where the wicked stay alive in pain forever, is not in this text or in the words the Bible actually uses for the dead. The wage sin pays is death, not endless life in misery. Faithful people expected to go to the Grave.

Jesus was in the Grave until he was raised. A place that holds the righteous and the Christ is not a chamber of fire. Gehenna and the lake of fire are a different picture: destruction, the second death, not a life that never ends.
Sheol, the place of the dead, is the Grave. The dead are not described as conscious, and a conscious torment cannot be read into a verse that says they know nothing.
AKS says the dead know nothing, and in the Grave there is no work or planning or knowledge or wisdom. It does not call that place a fire.
Whatever you find to do with your hands, do it with all your might, for in the Grave, where you are going, there is no work or planning or knowledge or wisdom.
No knowledge or wisdom in the Grave.
Look, every soul belongs to Me; both father and son are Mine. The soul who sins is the one who will die.
The soul that sins will die.
For the wages sin pays is death, but the gift God gives is everlasting life by Christ Jesus our Lord.
The wages of sin is death.
Foreseeing this, David spoke about the resurrection of the Christ, that He was not abandoned to the Grave, nor did His body see decay.
The Christ was not abandoned to the Grave.
Do not be afraid of those who kill the body but cannot kill the soul. Instead, fear the One who can destroy both soul and body in Gehenna.
God can destroy both soul and body in Gehenna.
Then Death and the Grave were thrown into the lake of fire. This is the second death—the lake of fire.
The lake of fire is the second death.
They have built high places to Baal on which to burn their children in the fire as offerings to Baal—something I never commanded or mentioned, nor had it even come into My heart.
Burning children in the fire never came into God’s heart.
Do not be amazed at this, for the hour is coming in which all those in the memorial tombs will hear his voice
