Resurrection is the Bible’s hope for the dead, because death is real. Those who did good come out to a resurrection of life. Those who did evil come out to a resurrection of judgment. Paul told a court that he hoped for a resurrection of both the righteous and the unrighteous.
If the soul had never died, there would be no one in the memorial tombs to call. Jesus told Martha, before he called Lazarus out of a tomb, that he is the resurrection and the life.
The dead are in the memorial tombs. They hear his voice there. They are not described as already alive somewhere else, waiting to be improved.
AKS says the hour is coming when all who are in the memorial tombs will hear his voice and come out.
and come out—those who have done good to the resurrection of life, and those who have done evil to the resurrection of judgment.
A resurrection of life and a resurrection of judgment.
and I have the same hope in God that they themselves cherish, that there will be a resurrection of both the righteous and the wicked.
Both the righteous and the wicked.
Jesus said to her, “I am the resurrection and the life. Whoever exercises faith in Me will live, even though he dies.
Jesus is the resurrection and the life.
For the living know that they will die, but the dead know nothing. They have no further reward, because the memory of them is forgotten.
Until that call, the dead know nothing.
Your dead will live; their bodies will rise. Awake and sing, you who dwell in the dust! For your dew is like the dew of the morning, and the earth will bring forth her dead.
The dead will live. Those in the dust will awake.
After He had said this, He told them, “Our friend Lazarus has fallen asleep, but I am going there to wake him up.”

A sleeper is not conscious. Jesus did not say Lazarus was in heaven or in pain. He went to wake him, which he did by calling him out of the tomb. If Lazarus had been living a better life, bringing him back would undo it.
The account records no report from Lazarus of another world.
Sleep is Jesus’ own comparison. He explains it in the next lines so no one is left thinking Lazarus is awake somewhere else.
AKS says Lazarus has fallen asleep, and then, Lazarus is dead. The two sentences are one fact.
So Jesus told them plainly, “Lazarus is dead,
Asleep means dead.
For the living know that they will die, but the dead know nothing. They have no further reward, because the memory of them is forgotten.
The dead know nothing.
And many who sleep in the dust of the earth will awake, some to everlasting life, but others to shame and everlasting contempt.
Many sleep in the dust until they awake.
before the dust returns to the ground from which it came and the spirit returns to God who gave it.

This line is quoted as if the dead were alive with God. The same book says the dead know nothing, and that in the Grave there is no knowledge. The spirit that returns is what God gave to make the dust live. When he takes it back, the person is dead.
Psalm 146 says the spirit departs, the man returns to the ground, and his plans perish that day.

Ruach here is the breath or life force, the same family of words as wind and breath. The verse sends the dust back to the ground and the spirit back to the God who gave it. It does not send a conscious person.
AKS says the dust returns to the ground and the spirit returns to God who gave it. It does not say the person goes to heaven.
For the living know that they will die, but the dead know nothing. They have no further reward, because the memory of them is forgotten.
The dead know nothing. This book does not contradict itself.
When his spirit departs, he returns to the ground; on that very day his plans perish.
The spirit departs and the plans perish.
Then Jehovah God formed the man from the dust of the ground and blew the breath of life into his nostrils, and the man became a living soul.
Life began when God gave breath. Death undoes that.
By the sweat of your face you will eat bread until you return to the ground, for out of it you were taken. For dust you are and to dust you will return.”
The person returns to dust.
casts spells, consults a medium or spirit medium, or inquires of the dead.

Christendom has often prayed to the dead, or tried to hear from them. The dead know nothing, so they cannot answer. At Endor a figure spoke as Samuel after God had refused to speak to Saul. That was not Samuel raised. A wicked spirit can imitate a dead person.
Spiritism sits with idolatry among the works of the flesh. Isaiah tells people to consult their God, not the dead, on behalf of the living.
The verse names a medium, a spiritist, and the one who inquires of the dead. Those are practices, not a metaphor for ordinary grief.
AKS says not to consult a medium or a spiritist, or to inquire of the dead. Whoever does these things is detestable to Jehovah.
For whoever does these things is detestable to Jehovah. And because of these detestable things, Jehovah your God is driving out the nations before you.
These practices are detestable to Jehovah.
You must not turn to mediums or spirit mediums; do not seek them out, or you will be defiled by them. I am Jehovah your God.
Do not turn to mediums or spiritists.
When men tell you to consult mediums and spirit mediums who whisper and mutter, shouldn’t a people consult their God instead? Why consult the dead on behalf of the living?
Why consult the dead on behalf of the living?
For the living know that they will die, but the dead know nothing. They have no further reward, because the memory of them is forgotten.
The dead know nothing, so they cannot send a message.

Then Samuel said to Saul, “Why have you disturbed me by bringing me up?” “I am deeply distressed,” replied Saul. “The Philistines are fighting against me, and God has turned away from me. He no longer answers me, either by prophets or by dreams. So I have called on you to tell me what to do.”
The figure at Endor was not Samuel. God had already refused Saul.
idolatry and spiritism; hatred, discord, jealousy, and rage; rivalries, divisions, factions,
Spiritism is listed with idolatry among the works of the flesh.
In the Grave, where he was in torment, he looked up and saw Abraham from afar, with Lazarus by his side.

The rich man and Lazarus are not two men reporting from the other side of death. The dead know nothing, and in the Grave there is no knowledge. Jesus is answering people who would not listen. The rich man stands for the proud religious leaders.
Lazarus stands for the lowly ones who did listen. The last line is the point. If they will not hear Moses and the Prophets, they will not be persuaded even if someone rises from the dead.

The word for Grave is Hades, the common grave of mankind. It is not a region where the dead stay awake. The torment is inside the story. The same Bible says the dead know nothing, so the story cannot be a report of their condition.
AKS says in the Grave, where he was in torment. It does not say the dead are conscious. The line belongs to an illustration.
For the living know that they will die, but the dead know nothing. They have no further reward, because the memory of them is forgotten.
The dead know nothing. A conscious rich man would undo that.
Whatever you find to do with your hands, do it with all your might, for in the Grave, where you are going, there is no work or planning or knowledge or wisdom.
In the Grave there is no work, knowledge, or planning.
Then Abraham said to him, ‘If they do not listen to Moses and the Prophets, they will not be persuaded even if someone rises from the dead.’”
The illustration ends on refusing Moses and the Prophets.
It is not the dead who praise Jah, nor any who descend into silence.
If the dead were alive in another place, this line would be false. They do not praise. They go down into silence. Hellfire needs the dead to be awake. The psalm says they are not.
Praise and silence are the contrast. The dead do not praise. Those who go down are in silence, not in a conscious torment where they could still cry out.
AKS says it is not the dead who praise Jah, nor any who descend into silence. Silence is the state. Jah is the short form of the divine name, and AKS keeps it.
For the living know that they will die, but the dead know nothing. They have no further reward, because the memory of them is forgotten.
The dead know nothing.
When his spirit departs, he returns to the ground; on that very day his plans perish.
His plans perish the day he dies.
Whatever you find to do with your hands, do it with all your might, for in the Grave, where you are going, there is no work or planning or knowledge or wisdom.

The writer tells the living to work with all their might because the place they are going has none of that activity. A conscious afterlife, whether of pleasure or of pain, would still be a kind of knowing. This verse says the Grave has none.
Sheol is the common grave. The list that follows is work, planning, knowledge, and wisdom. All four are absent there.
AKS says in the Grave, where you are going, there is no work or planning or knowledge or wisdom. Grave is Sheol. It is not rendered as a fiery hell.
For the living know that they will die, but the dead know nothing. They have no further reward, because the memory of them is forgotten.
The dead know nothing at all.
It is not the dead who praise Jah, nor any who descend into silence.
They descend into silence.
For the wages sin pays is death, but the gift God gives is everlasting life by Christ Jesus our Lord.

Sin does not pay a person by keeping him alive to suffer. It pays death. Life that does not end is a gift, and the verse says where that gift is found: by Christ Jesus. An immortal soul would already be drawing wages the verse does not offer.
Wages are what the work pays. The pay for sin is death, not life in another form. The opposite gift is everlasting life, and it comes by Christ Jesus, not from a soul that already had it.
AKS says the wages sin pays is death, but the gift God gives is everlasting life by Christ Jesus our Lord. Death and life are the two outcomes. The life is given through him, not absorbed into him.
Look, every soul belongs to Me; both father and son are Mine. The soul who sins is the one who will die.
The soul who sins will die.
By the sweat of your face you will eat bread until you return to the ground, for out of it you were taken. For dust you are and to dust you will return.”
The sentence on Adam was a return to dust.
and I have the same hope in God that they themselves cherish, that there will be a resurrection of both the righteous and the wicked.

Paul’s hope is a future rising, not a present life of the dead. The wicked are included, which means resurrection is not only a reward for the righteous. Judgment comes after they live again, not while they are still in the Grave.
Resurrection is a rising again of people who died. The hope covers two groups, the righteous and the wicked. Both are dead until that rising.
AKS says there will be a resurrection of both the righteous and the wicked. It does not say both are already alive somewhere else.
Do not be amazed at this, for the hour is coming in which all those in the memorial tombs will hear his voice
All in the memorial tombs will hear his voice and come out.
The sea gave up its dead, and Death and the Grave gave up their dead, and each one was judged according to his deeds.
Death and the Grave give up the dead.
The sea gave up its dead, and Death and the Grave gave up their dead, and each one was judged according to his deeds.
Judgment in this vision happens when the dead are given up. They are not sentenced while already conscious in the Grave. The Grave releases them. That is resurrection, and then the deeds are weighed.
The sea, Death, and the Grave each give up the dead. Giving up the dead means the dead were held there, not living on inside those places.
AKS says Death and the Grave gave up their dead, and each one was judged according to his deeds. Grave is Hades, the common grave, not a chamber of torment.
Do not be amazed at this, for the hour is coming in which all those in the memorial tombs will hear his voice
Those in the graves come out.
and I have the same hope in God that they themselves cherish, that there will be a resurrection of both the righteous and the wicked.
Both the righteous and the wicked rise.
Jesus said to her, “I am the resurrection and the life. Whoever exercises faith in Me will live, even though he dies.

Martha is standing at her brother’s grave. Jesus does not say Lazarus is already alive in another world. He says he himself is the resurrection, and then he calls Lazarus out of the tomb. The hope is a person brought back, not a soul that never left.
The resurrection and the life are titles Jesus takes for himself in front of a tomb. The life he offers is for the one who exercises faith, including the one who dies.
AKS says “I am the resurrection and the life. Whoever exercises faith in Me will live, even though he dies.” Exercises faith is the ongoing verb, not a single past moment that cannot be lost.
After He had said this, He told them, “Our friend Lazarus has fallen asleep, but I am going there to wake him up.”
He first calls that death sleep, then says Lazarus is dead.
Do not be amazed at this, for the hour is coming in which all those in the memorial tombs will hear his voice
The dead in the graves hear his voice.
For David did not ascend into heaven, but he himself says: ‘Jehovah said to my Lord, “Sit at My right hand

If every good man went to heaven at death, Peter could not have said this. David was a man after God’s heart, and Peter says he did not ascend. The Christ is the one exalted. David’s hope was still ahead of him.
Did not ascend is a plain denial. David died, was buried, and his tomb was still there. Peter uses that fact before he quotes the psalm.

AKS says David did not ascend into heaven. The next line is the psalm, “Jehovah said to my Lord,” so the divine name is kept in the quotation and David is not moved to heaven to make the argument easier.
No one has ascended into heaven except the One who descended from heaven—the Son of man.
No one has ascended into heaven except the Son of man.
A Psalm of David. Jehovah said to my Lord: “Sit at My right hand until I make Your enemies a footstool for Your feet.”
The psalm Peter quotes, Jehovah speaking to David’s Lord.
You must not turn to mediums or spirit mediums; do not seek them out, or you will be defiled by them. I am Jehovah your God.

The dead are silent. Asking them for guidance is asking people who know nothing. This law says the contact itself defiles, whether or not the medium seems kind. The one to consult is Jehovah, who names himself in the same verse.
Mediums and spiritists are people who claim contact with the dead or with spirits. Turning to them defiles. The verse ends by naming Jehovah as the one who speaks the ban.
AKS says you must not turn to mediums or spiritists, or you will be defiled by them. I am Jehovah your God. The name is kept. Spiritists is the practice, not a metaphor for bad advice.
casts spells, consults a medium or spirit medium, or inquires of the dead.
No medium, no spiritist, no inquiry of the dead.
For the living know that they will die, but the dead know nothing. They have no further reward, because the memory of them is forgotten.
The dead know nothing to tell.
When men tell you to consult mediums and spirit mediums who whisper and mutter, shouldn’t a people consult their God instead? Why consult the dead on behalf of the living?
Isaiah does not treat the dead as helpers who can still speak if the rite is done properly. He treats the consultation as absurd. The living ask God. The dead have nothing to give the living.
The prophet mocks the invitation to consult whisperers. A people should consult their God. The dead are the wrong address for the living.
AKS says: shouldn’t a people consult their God instead? Why consult the dead on behalf of the living? The question is the argument.
You must not turn to mediums or spirit mediums; do not seek them out, or you will be defiled by them. I am Jehovah your God.
Mediums and spiritists defile.
It is not the dead who praise Jah, nor any who descend into silence.
The dead are in silence.
That is why, just as through one man sin entered into the world and death through sin, and so death spread to all men because they had all sinned.
The ransom is needed because death is not a private accident. It entered through one man and passed on. A corresponding life answers a lost life.
If death were only bad behavior with no inherited loss, one man’s obedience could not be the answer Paul gives two verses later in the argument’s twin, Romans 5:19.
One man is Adam. Sin entered through him, and death through sin, and death spread to all because all sinned. The verse is about inheritance of death, not about each infant committing Adam’s act.

AKS says death was passed on to all men, because all sinned. Passed on keeps the transmission. All sinned is the result of being in that line, which the next verses explain before the law even existed.
For just as through the disobedience of the one man the many were made sinners, so also through the obedience of the one man the many will be made righteous.
One man’s disobedience, one man’s obedience.
For as in Adam all die, so in union with Christ all will be made alive.
In Adam all die. In union with Christ all will be made alive.
For as in Adam all die, so in union with Christ all will be made alive.

Death is in Adam. Life is in union with Christ, and it is future: they will be made alive. The chapter’s subject is resurrection. The ransom is what makes that rising possible. The dead are not already alive in Christ in some other room. They will be made alive.

In Adam all die is the inherited death. In union with Christ all will be made alive is the reversal, and the next verses put that life at his presence, in an order, not at the moment each person dies.

AKS says “as in Adam all die, so in union with Christ all will be made alive.” In union with is the same phrase AKS uses for the shared life of the Son and the Father. It is not a fusion of the many into Christ.
That is why, just as through one man sin entered into the world and death through sin, and so death spread to all men because they had all sinned.
Death passed on through the one man.
Do not be amazed at this, for the hour is coming in which all those in the memorial tombs will hear his voice
The hour is coming when the dead come out of the graves.
‘He will wipe away every tear from their eyes,’ and there will be no more death or mourning or crying or pain, for the former things have passed away.”

Revelation 21:3 says the dwelling place of God is with mankind. Then death is gone. Read with the promise that the righteous dwell in the earth forever, this is the earth freed from death, not a funeral for the planet.
The former things pass away. Death, mourning, crying, and pain are named. The previous verse has God dwelling with mankind. The audience of the vision includes a new earth.

AKS says He will wipe away every tear, and there will be no more death or mourning or crying or pain. Death ends. The verse does not relocate the living to a deathless heaven and leave the earth empty.
And I heard a loud voice from the throne saying: “Look, the dwelling place of God is with man, and He will dwell with them. They will be His people, and God Himself will be with them as their God.
God’s dwelling is with mankind.
They will build houses and dwell in them; they will plant vineyards and eat their fruit.
Houses and vineyards, lived in by the planters.

topics.label: Heaven
topics.ask: A little flock rules there

thoughts.text: No one has ascended into heaven except the One who descended from heaven—the Son of man.

Christendom sends every good soul to heaven at death. This verse says the opposite about everyone before Jesus. David did not ascend. The meek inherit the earth. Heaven is a real hope, and it is limited. The little flock is given the Kingdom.

The new covenant is made with that group, spiritual Israel, and they rule with the Lamb. The great crowd cannot be numbered, comes out of the great tribulation, and lives on the Paradise earth. Death ends on the earth, not by moving everyone to a place where death never was.
Ascended means went up. Jesus says no one has done that, except the Son of man who came down from heaven. The line leaves no room for Abraham, Moses, or David already living there.
AKS says no one has ascended into heaven except the one who descended, the Son of man.
For David did not ascend into heaven, but he himself says: ‘Jehovah said to my Lord, “Sit at My right hand
David did not ascend into heaven.
Happy are the gentle, for they will inherit the earth.
The meek inherit the earth.
The righteous will inherit the earth and dwell in it forever.
The righteous dwell on the earth forever.
And I heard the number of those who were sealed, 144,000 from all the tribes of Israel:
144,000 are sealed for heavenly rule, a numbered group.
In My Father’s house are many rooms. If it were not so, would I have told you that I am going there to prepare a place for you?
A place in the Father’s house is prepared for some, the ones he was speaking to.
‘He will wipe away every tear from their eyes,’ and there will be no more death or mourning or crying or pain, for the former things have passed away.”
No more death. That promise is for the earth, where death has been.
And Jesus said to him: “Truly I tell you today, you will be with me in Paradise.”

Jesus had said he would be killed and raised on the third day. On the day he was raised he said he had not yet ascended to the Father. The criminal could not be with him in Paradise on the day of the execution.

Today belongs with the moment Jesus gave his word, the way solemn promises in the Hebrew Scriptures use today. The Paradise he promised is the restored earth, the home of the great crowd, not heaven that afternoon.
The Greek word for today can stand with the promise or with the day the promise was spoken. The written text had no comma. AKS places the pause after today.
AKS reads, Truly I tell you today, you will be with me in Paradise. The man was not told that he would be in Paradise that same afternoon.
“The Son of man must suffer many things,” He said. “He must be rejected by the elders, chief priests, and scribes, and He must be killed and on the third day be raised to life.”
Jesus said he would be raised on the third day.
“Do not cling to Me,” Jesus said, “for I have not yet ascended to the Father. But go and tell My brothers, ‘I am ascending to My Father and your Father, to My God and your God.’”
After his death he had not yet ascended to the Father.
For the living know that they will die, but the dead know nothing. They have no further reward, because the memory of them is forgotten.
The dead know nothing, so the man was not alive in Paradise that day.
And I heard the number of those who were sealed, 144,000 from all the tribes of Israel:

The little flock is given the kingdom. Their hope is heavenly, and their work is to rule over the earth with the Lamb. They are not the whole company of the saved. John distinguishes them from the great crowd.
Reading 144,000 as a vague “many” erases the contrast the vision draws on purpose.

John hears a number, 144,000. Later he sees them with the Lamb on the heavenly Mount Zion. The number is not a symbol standing in for an uncounted church, because he immediately sees another group that cannot be numbered.
AKS says the number of those sealed was 144,000. Revelation 5:10 says they rule as kings over the earth, not that every worshiper goes to heaven.
Then I looked and saw the Lamb standing on Mount Zion, and with Him 144,000 who had His name and His Father’s name written on their foreheads.
The Lamb, and with him 144,000.
You have made them to be a kingdom and priests to serve our God, and they will rule as kings over the earth.”
They rule as kings over the earth.
Do not be afraid, little flock, for your Father is pleased to give you the kingdom.
The little flock is given the kingdom.

After this I looked and saw a great crowd, which no man was able to number, from every nation and tribe and people and tongue, standing before the throne and before the Lamb. They were wearing white robes and holding palm branches in their hands.
The great crowd is a different group, and it is unnumbered.

After this I looked and saw a great crowd, which no man was able to number, from every nation and tribe and people and tongue, standing before the throne and before the Lamb. They were wearing white robes and holding palm branches in their hands.

The great crowd comes out of the great tribulation. They survive it. They are not taken to heaven to rule. Their hope is life on the Paradise earth, the earth the meek inherit and the earth where God’s will is to be done.
They are Jesus’ other sheep, one flock with the little flock, but not the same hope and not the parties to the new covenant. Standing before the throne is the language of approved worshipers.
Serving in his temple is the courtyard of worship on earth, not a second group of kings on the heavenly Mount Zion.
John hears 144,000, then looks and sees a great crowd that no man can number, from every nation. The two descriptions are not two ways of saying the same group.
AKS says he saw a great crowd which no man was able to number, out of every nation, standing before the throne and before the Lamb.
And I heard the number of those who were sealed, 144,000 from all the tribes of Israel:
The numbered group is stated first, and it is limited.
I have other sheep that are not of this fold. I must bring them in as well, and they will listen to My voice. Then there will be one flock and one shepherd.
Other sheep, not of this fold.
The righteous will inherit the earth and dwell in it forever.
The righteous dwell on the earth forever.
Let your Kingdom come. Let your will take place, as in heaven, also on earth.
God’s will is to take place on earth.
In My Father’s house are many rooms. If it were not so, would I have told you that I am going there to prepare a place for you?

This is a real heavenly hope, spoken to the apostles that night, the men who would share the heavenly calling. The rooms are for those in the new covenant, the little flock the Father is pleased to give the Kingdom.

The same teacher said the meek inherit the earth, and that no one before him had ascended. The other sheep are not told they are going to those rooms. They become one flock under the same shepherd, and their home is Paradise on earth.
The rooms are dwelling places in his Father’s house. The promise is spoken to the apostles with him that night, not to every person who would ever believe.
AKS says he goes to prepare a place so that they may be where he is. It does not say every good person goes there at death.
And if I go and prepare a place for you, I will come back and welcome you into My presence, so that you also may be where I am.
He returns so those disciples may be where he is.
Do not be afraid, little flock, for your Father is pleased to give you the kingdom.
The little flock is given the Kingdom.
I have other sheep that are not of this fold. I must bring them in as well, and they will listen to My voice. Then there will be one flock and one shepherd.
The other sheep are a different group.
No one has ascended into heaven except the One who descended from heaven—the Son of man.
No one else had ascended into heaven.
Do not be afraid, little flock, for your Father is pleased to give you the kingdom.

Heaven’s ruling hope belongs to a little flock. Jesus does not tell a crowd of every good person that the Kingdom is theirs to inherit as kings. He tells a small flock not to be afraid, because the Father wants to give them that Kingdom.

John later hears their number, 144,000, and sees them with the Lamb. The great crowd is the other group, and it cannot be numbered. One flock under one shepherd does not erase the difference in the hope.
Little flock is poimnion, a small flock. The Father is pleased to give them the basileia, the Kingdom. The gift is to that flock, not to every sheep who would ever listen to the shepherd.
AKS says “Do not be afraid, little flock, for your Father is pleased to give you the kingdom.” Little is kept. The kingdom is given to the ones he is addressing.
And I heard the number of those who were sealed, 144,000 from all the tribes of Israel:
The number sealed is 144,000.
Then I looked and saw the Lamb standing on Mount Zion, and with Him 144,000 who had His name and His Father’s name written on their foreheads.
The 144,000 stand with the Lamb on Mount Zion.
I have other sheep that are not of this fold. I must bring them in as well, and they will listen to My voice. Then there will be one flock and one shepherd.
The other sheep are not of this fold.
You have made them to be a kingdom and priests to serve our God, and they will rule as kings over the earth.”
They rule as kings over the earth.
Look, the days are coming, declares Jehovah, when I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah.

The new covenant is real, and it has parties. Jeremiah names the house of Israel and the house of Judah. Hebrews says Jesus mediates that better covenant, founded on better promises, so that those who are called receive the inheritance.

In the Christian Scriptures that house is spiritual Israel: a chosen people, a royal priesthood, a holy nation. That is the little flock. The spirit testifies with their spirit that they are God’s children and heirs with Christ.
The evening meal names the cup as this covenant in his blood. Those in the covenant are the ones who share the bread and the wine. The great crowd is not written into the covenant as a second party.
The blood is still poured out for many, and they receive life on earth under the Kingdom those heirs rule.

The Hebrew is a new berith, a covenant, with the house of Israel and the house of Judah. It replaces the covenant made when he took them by the hand to bring them out of Egypt. Hebrews quotes this promise and calls the later arrangement a new diatheke, with Jesus as its mesites, its mediator.
AKS says Jehovah will make a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah. Covenant is kept. The parties are those two houses, not an unnamed crowd of all who will ever be saved.
Now, however, Jesus has received a much more excellent ministry, just as the covenant He mediates is better and is founded on better promises.
Jesus mediates a better covenant, on better promises.
But God found fault with the people and said: “Look, the days are coming, declares Jehovah, when I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah.
The promise of a new covenant is quoted.

Therefore he is the mediator of a new covenant, so that those who are called may receive the promised eternal inheritance, now that He has died to redeem them from the sins committed under the first covenant.
He is the mediator of a new covenant for those who are called.
In the same way, after supper He took the cup, saying, “This cup is the new covenant in My blood, which is poured out for you.
The cup is the new covenant in his blood.
But you are a chosen people, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, a people for God’s own possession, to proclaim the virtues of Him who called you out of darkness into His marvelous light.
A royal priesthood and a holy nation.
The spirit itself testifies with our spirit that we are God’s children.
The spirit testifies that they are God’s children.
Jesus replied, “Most truly I say to you, no one can see the Kingdom of God unless he is born again.”

Being born again is how the little flock receives the heavenly hope. It is a birth from above, by water and spirit, for those who will see and enter that Kingdom as heirs. It is not a requirement pasted onto the great crowd.

They do not need that birth in order to live in Paradise. They listen to the shepherd, they survive the great tribulation, and the earth is their home. Telling every believer that this verse sends them to heaven at death ignores both the limited flock and the earthly promise.

Born again translates a line that can also be read born from above. The Greek anothen means again or from above. Jesus says no one can see the Kingdom of God without that birth. A few lines later, entering the Kingdom requires being born of water and spirit.
The Kingdom in this night conversation is the heavenly one a person must be born into, not the earth the meek are already promised.
AKS says no one can see the Kingdom of God unless he is born again. Born again is kept. The line is not widened into a slogan for every person who hopes to live on the earth.
Jesus answered, “Most truly I say to you, no one can enter the Kingdom of God unless he is born of water and the spirit.
Born of water and spirit in order to enter the Kingdom.
Therefore, holy brothers, who share in the heavenly calling, set your focus on Jesus, the apostle and high priest whom we confess.
Holy brothers who share in the heavenly calling.
I have other sheep that are not of this fold. I must bring them in as well, and they will listen to My voice. Then there will be one flock and one shepherd.
Other sheep, not of this fold.
Happy are the gentle, for they will inherit the earth.
The meek inherit the earth without this verse moving them to heaven.
Therefore, holy brothers, who share in the heavenly calling, set your focus on Jesus, the apostle and high priest whom we confess.

Hebrews is speaking to people who have a heavenly calling. Their hope is to be where their high priest is. That calling matches the little flock, the new covenant, and the rooms Jesus said he was preparing. It does not cancel Paradise.
A calling that must be shared is not the same statement as “everyone good goes to heaven.”

The brothers addressed are those who share in the heavenly calling. A calling is an invitation given, not a destiny every worshiper already has. The one they are told to look to is the apostle and high priest.
AKS says holy brothers, who share in the heavenly calling. Share in keeps it as something held in common by that group. It does not say all mankind shares it.
In My Father’s house are many rooms. If it were not so, would I have told you that I am going there to prepare a place for you?
He prepares a place for the ones he is speaking to.
But our citizenship is in heaven, and we eagerly await a Savior from there, the Lord Jesus Christ,
Their citizenship is in heaven.
Do not be afraid, little flock, for your Father is pleased to give you the kingdom.
The little flock is given the Kingdom.
The spirit itself testifies with our spirit that we are God’s children.

The ones who receive this witness are the children who will be glorified with Christ. They are co-heirs. That is the little flock under the new covenant, sealed and called to rule with him. The great crowd is not told to announce itself as that heir. They are the other sheep.
The Lamb shepherds them, and they live. Being loved by God is not the same statement as being a co-heir of the heavenly Kingdom.

The spirit itself testifies with our spirit that we are God’s children. The next line says those children are heirs of God and co-heirs with Christ, if they suffer with him so as to be glorified with him. Heirship here is glorification with Christ, the heavenly reward, not a general kindness to every worshiper.
AKS says the spirit itself testifies with our spirit that we are God’s children. The testimony is the spirit’s, together with their spirit. It is not a mood the reader is told to claim.
And if we are children, then we are heirs: heirs of God and co-heirs with Christ—if indeed we suffer with Him, so that we may also be glorified with Him.
Heirs of God and co-heirs with Christ.
Now it is God who establishes both us and you in union with Christ. He anointed us,
God anointed them and sealed them.
Then I looked and saw the Lamb standing on Mount Zion, and with Him 144,000 who had His name and His Father’s name written on their foreheads.
The 144,000 have his name and his Father’s name.
I have other sheep that are not of this fold. I must bring them in as well, and they will listen to My voice. Then there will be one flock and one shepherd.
The other sheep are brought in, and they are not this fold.
I have other sheep that are not of this fold. I must bring them in as well, and they will listen to My voice. Then there will be one flock and one shepherd.

The fold Jesus was addressing is the little flock, the ones given the Kingdom and brought into the new covenant. The other sheep are real, and they are not that fold. He brings them, they listen to his voice, and there is one flock under one shepherd.

The great crowd is that other group: unnumbered, out of every nation, washed in the blood of the Lamb, coming out of the great tribulation. Their place is not the heavenly Mount Zion. It is the earth, in Paradise, under the rule of the Kingdom.

Other sheep are not of this fold. Fold is aule, the enclosure he is already gathering. He must bring the others in. Then there is one poimne, one flock, and one shepherd. One flock is unity under him. It is not a sentence that the other sheep were in the fold all along, or that both groups receive the same inheritance.
AKS says “I have other sheep that are not of this fold.” Not of this fold is kept. One flock and one shepherd come after he brings them in.
Do not be afraid, little flock, for your Father is pleased to give you the kingdom.
This fold is the little flock.

After this I looked and saw a great crowd, which no man was able to number, from every nation and tribe and people and tongue, standing before the throne and before the Lamb. They were wearing white robes and holding palm branches in their hands.
The great crowd no one can number.
“Sir,” I answered, “you know.” So he replied, “These are the ones who have come out of the great tribulation; they have washed their robes and made them white in the blood of the Lamb.
They come out of the great tribulation.
The righteous will inherit the earth and dwell in it forever.
The righteous dwell in the earth forever.
“Sir,” I answered, “you know.” So he replied, “These are the ones who have come out of the great tribulation; they have washed their robes and made them white in the blood of the Lamb.

The great crowd is not a symbol for the 144,000. John has already heard that number. He then sees a crowd he cannot count, from every nation. They come out of the great tribulation. They do not die and wake in heaven as kings.

The Lamb shepherds them, and they hunger and thirst no more. That life is on the earth God formed to be inhabited, the Paradise Jesus promised, the earth the meek inherit. They stand as approved worshipers.
The little flock is the group on Mount Zion with the Lamb, ruling over this earth.

The great crowd is an ochlos no man could number. The elder says these are the ones coming out of the great tribulation. Their robes are washed white in the blood of the Lamb. Coming out means they pass through that tribulation as survivors.
The next lines put them before the throne as worshipers, serving in his naos, his temple, with his tent spread over them. That is protection and approved worship, not a second throne of kings.

AKS says these are the ones who have come out of the great tribulation, and they have washed their robes in the blood of the Lamb. Come out is survival, not a transfer into the sealed group of 144,000.
And I heard the number of those who were sealed, 144,000 from all the tribes of Israel:
The numbered group is stated first.
For this reason, they are before the throne of God and serve Him day and night in His temple; and the One seated on the throne will spread His tabernacle over them.
They serve before the throne, and his tent is over them.
Then I looked and saw the Lamb standing on Mount Zion, and with Him 144,000 who had His name and His Father’s name written on their foreheads.
Mount Zion is where the 144,000 stand, not this crowd.
And Jesus said to him: “Truly I tell you today, you will be with me in Paradise.”
Paradise is the place Jesus promised, and it was not heaven that day.
They will build houses and dwell in them; they will plant vineyards and eat their fruit.
Houses and vineyards on the restored earth.
Then I looked and saw the Lamb standing on Mount Zion, and with Him 144,000 who had His name and His Father’s name written on their foreheads.

This is the little flock in their heavenly place. They carry the name. They are with the Lamb, not standing in the unnumbered crowd of chapter 7. They rule as kings over the earth. Flesh and blood does not inherit that heavenly Kingdom.
They are raised in the first resurrection and reign with him. The earth they rule is not discarded. The great crowd lives on it.

The Lamb stands on Mount Zion, and with him 144,000 who have his name and his Father’s name on their foreheads. Mount Zion in this vision is the heavenly one. Their song is one that only they can learn. A number that is both heard and then seen with the Lamb is not a figure of speech for an uncountable church.
AKS says the Lamb on Mount Zion, and with him 144,000 who had his name and his Father’s name. The number is printed as a number.
You have made them to be a kingdom and priests to serve our God, and they will rule as kings over the earth.”
A kingdom and priests who rule as kings over the earth.
Blessed and holy are those who share in the first resurrection! The second death has no power over them, but they will be priests of God and of Christ and will reign with Him for a thousand years.
The first resurrection. They reign with him.
Now I declare to you, brothers, that flesh and blood cannot inherit the Kingdom of God, nor does the perishable inherit the imperishable.
Flesh and blood cannot inherit the Kingdom of God.
Instead, you have come to Mount Zion, to the city of the living God, the heavenly Jerusalem. You have come to myriads of angels
Mount Zion, the heavenly Jerusalem.
But our citizenship is in heaven, and we eagerly await a Savior from there, the Lord Jesus Christ,

The anointed have their citizenship in heaven because that is where they will rule from. Paul includes himself with them. The savior comes from there, and the Kingdom he brings is the one Jesus taught people to pray would make God’s will happen on earth.
Citizenship for the little flock is not a denial of Paradise for the great crowd.

Citizenship is politeuma, a community and its seat of government. Paul says ours is in heaven. He is writing to holy ones who share the heavenly calling, not issuing a passport to every person who will be saved. They await a savior from there.
AKS says our citizenship is in heaven. Our is the congregation he is addressing. From there keeps the savior’s origin. The verse does not say the earth will be emptied.
Therefore, holy brothers, who share in the heavenly calling, set your focus on Jesus, the apostle and high priest whom we confess.
They share the heavenly calling.
Let your Kingdom come. Let your will take place, as in heaven, also on earth.
God’s will is to take place on earth.
‘He will wipe away every tear from their eyes,’ and there will be no more death or mourning or crying or pain, for the former things have passed away.”
Death ends where mankind lives.
Now I declare to you, brothers, that flesh and blood cannot inherit the Kingdom of God, nor does the perishable inherit the imperishable.

Those who rule with Christ are not carried into heaven as the humans they were. They are changed. That is why the little flock’s hope is a resurrection to spirit life, the first resurrection, and why no one before Jesus had ascended.

The same chapter still has the dead raised because they were dead. It does not turn the earthly promise into a metaphor. Houses, vineyards, and a Paradise on earth belong to humans. The Kingdom in this verse is the heavenly one flesh cannot enter.

Flesh and blood cannot inherit the Kingdom of God, and the perishable cannot inherit the imperishable. The chapter is about the resurrection of those who are raised to a spiritual body. A heavenly inheritance requires that change.
The verse does not say the earth, which is not flesh and blood, cannot be inherited by the meek.
AKS says flesh and blood cannot inherit the Kingdom of God. Inherit is kept. The subject is who enters that Kingdom in a body of flesh.
Blessed and holy are those who share in the first resurrection! The second death has no power over them, but they will be priests of God and of Christ and will reign with Him for a thousand years.
Priests of God who reign with him. The first resurrection.
No one has ascended into heaven except the One who descended from heaven—the Son of man.
No one had ascended into heaven except the Son of man.
Happy are the gentle, for they will inherit the earth.
The meek still inherit the earth.
For David did not ascend into heaven, but he himself says: ‘Jehovah said to my Lord, “Sit at My right hand

If every good man went to heaven at death, Peter could not have said this. David was a man after God’s heart, and Peter says he did not ascend. The Christ is the one exalted. David’s hope was still ahead of him.
Did not ascend is a plain denial. David died, was buried, and his tomb was still there. Peter uses that fact before he quotes the psalm.

AKS says David did not ascend into heaven. The next line is the psalm, “Jehovah said to my Lord,” so the divine name is kept in the quotation and David is not moved to heaven to make the argument easier.
No one has ascended into heaven except the One who descended from heaven—the Son of man.
No one has ascended into heaven except the Son of man.
A Psalm of David. Jehovah said to my Lord: “Sit at My right hand until I make Your enemies a footstool for Your feet.”
The psalm Peter quotes, Jehovah speaking to David’s Lord.
In the same way, after supper He took the cup, saying, “This cup is the new covenant in My blood, which is poured out for you.

The wine means the blood that puts the new covenant into effect. Disciples do not drink blood. They drink wine that Jesus called the covenant in his blood. The pouring out happened at his death. The meal announces that. It does not repeat it.

The covenant itself is the one Jeremiah said Jehovah would make with the house of Israel. In the Christian Scriptures that house is spiritual Israel, the little flock, not every person who later benefits. The great crowd is among the many for whom the blood is poured out.
They are not the fold with whom the cup of the covenant is shared.

The cup is called the new covenant in my blood, poured out. The wine stands for the blood. Drinking a symbol of blood is not the same command as eating blood. The covenant is validated by the blood he pours out, once.
AKS says “This cup is the new covenant in My blood, which is poured out for you.” Cup and blood stay distinct. Poured out is his death, not a weekly offering.
In the same way, after supper He took the cup, saying, “This cup is the new covenant in My blood; do this, as often as you drink it, in remembrance of Me.”
The same cup, in remembrance.
just as the Son of man did not come to be served, but to serve, and to give his life as a ransom in exchange for many.”
The life given as a ransom.

topics.label: Resurrection
topics.ask: Those in the memorial tombs will hear

thoughts.text: Do not be amazed at this, for the hour is coming in which all those in the memorial tombs will hear his voice

Resurrection is the Bible’s hope for the dead, because death is real. Those who did good come out to a resurrection of life. Those who did evil come out to a resurrection of judgment. Paul told a court that he hoped for a resurrection of both the righteous and the unrighteous.
If the soul had never died, there would be no one in the memorial tombs to call. Jesus told Martha, before he called Lazarus out of a tomb, that he is the resurrection and the life.
The dead are in the memorial tombs. They hear his voice there. They are not described as already alive somewhere else, waiting to be improved.
AKS says the hour is coming when all who are in the memorial tombs will hear his voice and come out.
and come out—those who have done good to the resurrection of life, and those who have done evil to the resurrection of judgment.
A resurrection of life and a resurrection of judgment.
and I have the same hope in God that they themselves cherish, that there will be a resurrection of both the righteous and the wicked.
Both the righteous and the wicked.
Jesus said to her, “I am the resurrection and the life. Whoever exercises faith in Me will live, even though he dies.
Jesus is the resurrection and the life.
For the living know that they will die, but the dead know nothing. They have no further reward, because the memory of them is forgotten.
Until that call, the dead know nothing.
Your dead will live; their bodies will rise. Awake and sing, you who dwell in the dust! For your dew is like the dew of the morning, and the earth will bring forth her dead.
The dead will live. Those in the dust will awake.
Now I declare to you, brothers, that flesh and blood cannot inherit the Kingdom of God, nor does the perishable inherit the imperishable.

Those who rule with Christ are not carried into heaven as the humans they were. They are changed. That is why the little flock’s hope is a resurrection to spirit life, the first resurrection, and why no one before Jesus had ascended.

The same chapter still has the dead raised because they were dead. It does not turn the earthly promise into a metaphor. Houses, vineyards, and a Paradise on earth belong to humans. The Kingdom in this verse is the heavenly one flesh cannot enter.

Flesh and blood cannot inherit the Kingdom of God, and the perishable cannot inherit the imperishable. The chapter is about the resurrection of those who are raised to a spiritual body. A heavenly inheritance requires that change.
The verse does not say the earth, which is not flesh and blood, cannot be inherited by the meek.
AKS says flesh and blood cannot inherit the Kingdom of God. Inherit is kept. The subject is who enters that Kingdom in a body of flesh.
Blessed and holy are those who share in the first resurrection! The second death has no power over them, but they will be priests of God and of Christ and will reign with Him for a thousand years.
Priests of God who reign with him. The first resurrection.
No one has ascended into heaven except the One who descended from heaven—the Son of man.
No one had ascended into heaven except the Son of man.
Happy are the gentle, for they will inherit the earth.
The meek still inherit the earth.
and I have the same hope in God that they themselves cherish, that there will be a resurrection of both the righteous and the wicked.

Paul’s hope is a future rising, not a present life of the dead. The wicked are included, which means resurrection is not only a reward for the righteous. Judgment comes after they live again, not while they are still in the Grave.
Resurrection is a rising again of people who died. The hope covers two groups, the righteous and the wicked. Both are dead until that rising.
AKS says there will be a resurrection of both the righteous and the wicked. It does not say both are already alive somewhere else.
Do not be amazed at this, for the hour is coming in which all those in the memorial tombs will hear his voice
All in the memorial tombs will hear his voice and come out.
The sea gave up its dead, and Death and the Grave gave up their dead, and each one was judged according to his deeds.
Death and the Grave give up the dead.
The sea gave up its dead, and Death and the Grave gave up their dead, and each one was judged according to his deeds.
Judgment in this vision happens when the dead are given up. They are not sentenced while already conscious in the Grave. The Grave releases them. That is resurrection, and then the deeds are weighed.
The sea, Death, and the Grave each give up the dead. Giving up the dead means the dead were held there, not living on inside those places.
AKS says Death and the Grave gave up their dead, and each one was judged according to his deeds. Grave is Hades, the common grave, not a chamber of torment.
Do not be amazed at this, for the hour is coming in which all those in the memorial tombs will hear his voice
Those in the graves come out.
and I have the same hope in God that they themselves cherish, that there will be a resurrection of both the righteous and the wicked.
Both the righteous and the wicked rise.
Jesus said to her, “I am the resurrection and the life. Whoever exercises faith in Me will live, even though he dies.

Martha is standing at her brother’s grave. Jesus does not say Lazarus is already alive in another world. He says he himself is the resurrection, and then he calls Lazarus out of the tomb. The hope is a person brought back, not a soul that never left.
The resurrection and the life are titles Jesus takes for himself in front of a tomb. The life he offers is for the one who exercises faith, including the one who dies.
AKS says “I am the resurrection and the life. Whoever exercises faith in Me will live, even though he dies.” Exercises faith is the ongoing verb, not a single past moment that cannot be lost.
After He had said this, He told them, “Our friend Lazarus has fallen asleep, but I am going there to wake him up.”
He first calls that death sleep, then says Lazarus is dead.
Do not be amazed at this, for the hour is coming in which all those in the memorial tombs will hear his voice
The dead in the graves hear his voice.
For David did not ascend into heaven, but he himself says: ‘Jehovah said to my Lord, “Sit at My right hand

If every good man went to heaven at death, Peter could not have said this. David was a man after God’s heart, and Peter says he did not ascend. The Christ is the one exalted. David’s hope was still ahead of him.
Did not ascend is a plain denial. David died, was buried, and his tomb was still there. Peter uses that fact before he quotes the psalm.

AKS says David did not ascend into heaven. The next line is the psalm, “Jehovah said to my Lord,” so the divine name is kept in the quotation and David is not moved to heaven to make the argument easier.
No one has ascended into heaven except the One who descended from heaven—the Son of man.
No one has ascended into heaven except the Son of man.
A Psalm of David. Jehovah said to my Lord: “Sit at My right hand until I make Your enemies a footstool for Your feet.”
The psalm Peter quotes, Jehovah speaking to David’s Lord.
For as in Adam all die, so in union with Christ all will be made alive.

Death is in Adam. Life is in union with Christ, and it is future: they will be made alive. The chapter’s subject is resurrection. The ransom is what makes that rising possible. The dead are not already alive in Christ in some other room. They will be made alive.

In Adam all die is the inherited death. In union with Christ all will be made alive is the reversal, and the next verses put that life at his presence, in an order, not at the moment each person dies.

AKS says “as in Adam all die, so in union with Christ all will be made alive.” In union with is the same phrase AKS uses for the shared life of the Son and the Father. It is not a fusion of the many into Christ.
That is why, just as through one man sin entered into the world and death through sin, and so death spread to all men because they had all sinned.
Death passed on through the one man.
Do not be amazed at this, for the hour is coming in which all those in the memorial tombs will hear his voice
The hour is coming when the dead come out of the graves.
For the Lord Himself will descend from heaven with a loud command, with the voice of an archangel, and with the trumpet of God, and the dead in Christ will be the first to rise.
The one who descends is the Lord Jesus, and the voice of that descent is an archangel’s voice. There is one archangel in Scripture, Michael. Jesus also has angels subject to him.
The verse does not say the words “Jesus is Michael.” It puts the archangel’s voice with the Lord’s own descent, and the other verses have to be read beside it.

Archangel occurs in the singular. The Lord himself descends with a commanding call, with the voice of an archangel, and with God’s trumpet. The voice belongs to the descent of the Lord. The dead in Christ rise. An archangel is the chief angel, and the Bible never uses the word in the plural.

AKS says the Lord Himself will descend from heaven with a loud command, with the voice of an archangel, and with the trumpet of God, and the dead in Christ will be the first to rise. Voice of an archangel is kept.
It is not changed into a voice like an archangel, which would add a comparison the phrase does not require.
But even the archangel Michael, when he disputed with the devil over the body of Moses, did not presume to bring a slanderous charge against him, but said, “Jehovah rebuke you!”
Michael is the archangel. The word is singular.
Then a war broke out in heaven: Michael and his angels fought against the dragon, and the dragon and his angels fought back.
Michael and his angels.
who has gone into heaven and is at the right hand of God, with angels, authorities, and powers subject to Him.
Angels and powers are subject to Jesus.
But Christ has indeed been raised from the dead, the firstfruits of those who have fallen asleep.
Christ has been raised, the firstfruits of those who have fallen asleep. The others are still asleep.

topics.label: Cross
topics.ask: Why Jesus did not die on one

thoughts.text: For the message of the torture stake is foolishness to those who are perishing, but to us who are being saved it is the power of God.

Christendom treats a cross as the shape Jesus died on, and as a symbol to wear or bow toward. The Greek does not say that. The stake made him a curse, so the instrument is not something to honor. Christians flee from idolatry rather than turn the means of his death into an image.
Stauros means an upright stake or pole. It does not name two beams. Xylon, the other word for the same instrument, means timber or a tree, and Deuteronomy uses it of a single stake.
AKS says the torture stake, not a cross. Paul quotes the curse on the one hung on a stake.
Christ redeemed us from the curse of the law by becoming a curse for us. For it is written: “Cursed is everyone who is hung on a stake.”
He became a curse by being hung on a stake, quoting Deuteronomy.

you must not leave the body on the stake overnight, but you must be sure to bury him that day, because anyone who is hung on a stake is under God’s curse. You must not defile the land that Jehovah your God is giving you as an inheritance.
The law is about a stake, one piece of timber, not a crossbeam.
Carrying His own stake, He went out to The Place of the Skull, which in Hebrew is called Golgotha.
He carried his own stake.
The God of our fathers raised up Jesus, whom you had killed by hanging Him on a stake.
Peter says they hung him on a stake. The Greek is xylon, timber.
Therefore, my beloved, flee from idolatry.
Flee from idolatry. A sacred image of the instrument is not worship.
It was now the third hour, and they nailed him to the stake.

The accounts are not two clocks in contradiction. One can include the start of the execution, including the whipping. The other can mark when he was nailed to the stake. Both round the hour. AKS uses stake for the instrument they nailed him to.
The third hour is about nine in the morning, counting from sunrise in three-hour parts of the day. Writers often gave the time in those blocks, so the hour can be approximate.

AKS says it was now the third hour, and they nailed him to the stake. John speaks of about the sixth hour when Pilate handed him over. Scourging was part of the execution and could stand between the sentence and the nailing.
Carrying His own stake, He went out to The Place of the Skull, which in Hebrew is called Golgotha.
He went out carrying his own stake.
More than that, when he came as a man, he humbled himself and became obedient to the point of death, yes, death on a torture stake.
Death on a torture stake.
Christ redeemed us from the curse of the law by becoming a curse for us. For it is written: “Cursed is everyone who is hung on a stake.”

The curse is the point of the quotation. Jesus took the place of those under the Law by dying the death the Law called cursed. That is why the stake is not a charm. The shape people later drew is not in the verse.
Paul quotes Deuteronomy with xylon. The Hebrew there is a tree or a timber, and the law is about hanging a body on a stake. The Greek does not add a crosspiece.
AKS reads hung on a stake, matching the Hebrew law, not hung on a cross.
If a man has committed a sin worthy of death, and he is executed, and you hang his body on a stake,
The law Paul is quoting.
For the message of the torture stake is foolishness to those who are perishing, but to us who are being saved it is the power of God.
The message is about the stake, not a symbol.
More than that, when he came as a man, he humbled himself and became obedient to the point of death, yes, death on a torture stake.
Death on a torture stake.
Along the way they found a man from Cyrene, named Simon, and they forced him to carry the stake of Jesus.

Simon of Cyrene carries the instrument Jesus had been carrying. The accounts call it the same thing they later nail him to. AKS keeps stake so the reader does not import a shaped symbol the Greek noun does not specify.

The Greek word is stauros, a stake or upright pole. The verse says Simon was forced to carry it. The instrument is something one man can carry, and AKS does not turn the word into the later church emblem.
AKS says they forced him to carry the stake of Jesus. Stake translates stauros. Cross would decide a shape the word itself does not draw.
Carrying His own stake, He went out to The Place of the Skull, which in Hebrew is called Golgotha.
He went out carrying his own stake.
If a man has committed a sin worthy of death, and he is executed, and you hang his body on a stake,
The law speaks of a body hung on a stake.
Carrying His own stake, He went out to The Place of the Skull, which in Hebrew is called Golgotha.

John and Matthew are describing one walk to the same place. One moment he carries it. Later Simon is compelled to carry it. Both verses use the word AKS renders stake. The place-name is given in Hebrew so the reader can see this is a report, not a symbol being explained.
He carried it, and the place has a Hebrew name, Golgotha. The instrument is stauros again. AKS does not add a crossbeam the sentence does not mention.
AKS says “Carrying His own stake, He went out.” Stake is the same decision as in the other accounts of the execution.
Along the way they found a man from Cyrene, named Simon, and they forced him to carry the stake of Jesus.
Simon is forced to carry the same stake.
Christ redeemed us from the curse of the law by becoming a curse for us. For it is written: “Cursed is everyone who is hung on a stake.”
The curse is on the one hung on a stake.
The God of our fathers raised up Jesus, whom you had killed by hanging Him on a stake.

Peter’s charge to the court uses the language of the curse text. The Greek can be heard as wood or tree. AKS chooses stake because that is how the law being echoed is rendered, and because the execution accounts use stauros for the same death.
One English word keeps the law and the event together.

The phrase is hanging him on a tree or a timber, the word also used for wood. Peter is echoing the law in Deuteronomy about the one whose body is hung on a stake. AKS follows that Hebrew law’s word rather than a later emblem.
AKS says you killed him by hanging Him on a stake. It does not say tree, and it does not say cross. The matching law in Deuteronomy 21:22 uses stake.
If a man has committed a sin worthy of death, and he is executed, and you hang his body on a stake,
The law: hang his body on a stake.
Christ redeemed us from the curse of the law by becoming a curse for us. For it is written: “Cursed is everyone who is hung on a stake.”
Paul quotes that curse.
If a man has committed a sin worthy of death, and he is executed, and you hang his body on a stake,

This is the law Paul quotes when he says the one hung on a stake is under a curse. If this verse said tree and Galatians said stake, the quotation would look broken. AKS uses stake in both so the reader can see they are one statute.
The Hebrew word is the ordinary word for a tree or a piece of timber set up so a body can be hung on it. It is not the name of a shaped religious symbol.
AKS says you hang his body on a stake. Stake keeps the legal instrument. Tree would be possible English and is not used here, so the later quotations can say stake as well.
Christ redeemed us from the curse of the law by becoming a curse for us. For it is written: “Cursed is everyone who is hung on a stake.”
Paul quotes this curse.
The God of our fathers raised up Jesus, whom you had killed by hanging Him on a stake.
Peter uses the same charge.

So the other disciples told him, “We have seen the Lord!” But he replied, “Unless I see the nail marks in His hands, and put my finger where the nails have been, and put my hand into His side, I will never believe.”
Thomas speaks of the print of the nails. Nails can fasten a body to a timber. They do not require a crossbeam.

topics.label: Idolatry
topics.ask: Why images are not worship

thoughts.text: You must not make for yourself an idol in the form of anything in the heavens above, on the earth below, or in the waters beneath.

Christendom has used statues, icons, and the cross as objects of devotion while saying the worship goes past the object to God. The command does not leave that opening. Jehovah does not give his glory to an idol. An image made by a craftsman cannot speak.
The apostles told people not to think the Divine Being is like gold, silver, or stone, and they said to flee from idolatry.

The Hebrew forbids a carved or shaped image of anything in heaven, on earth, or in the waters, and the next verse forbids bowing to it. The ban is on the act of making and venerating, not only on images of foreign gods by name.
AKS says you shall not make an idol in the form of anything in the heavens or on the earth, and you shall not bow down to them.

You must not bow down to them or worship them; for I, Jehovah your God, am a jealous God, visiting the wrongdoing of the fathers on their children to the third and fourth generations of those who hate Me,
Do not bow down to them or worship them.
I am Jehovah; that is My name! I will not yield My glory to another or My praise to idols.
Jehovah does not share his glory with idols.
Therefore, my beloved, flee from idolatry.
Flee from idolatry.
Little children, keep yourselves from idols.
Keep yourselves from idols.
Therefore, being offspring of God, we should not think that the Divine Being is like gold or silver or stone, an image formed by man’s skill and imagination.
God is not like an image shaped by human skill.
For the message of the torture stake is foolishness to those who are perishing, but to us who are being saved it is the power of God.
The stake is not turned into an image to honor.
For the message of the torture stake is foolishness to those who are perishing, but to us who are being saved it is the power of God.

Christendom treats a cross as the shape Jesus died on, and as a symbol to wear or bow toward. The Greek does not say that. The stake made him a curse, so the instrument is not something to honor. Christians flee from idolatry rather than turn the means of his death into an image.
Stauros means an upright stake or pole. It does not name two beams. Xylon, the other word for the same instrument, means timber or a tree, and Deuteronomy uses it of a single stake.
AKS says the torture stake, not a cross. Paul quotes the curse on the one hung on a stake.
Christ redeemed us from the curse of the law by becoming a curse for us. For it is written: “Cursed is everyone who is hung on a stake.”
He became a curse by being hung on a stake, quoting Deuteronomy.

you must not leave the body on the stake overnight, but you must be sure to bury him that day, because anyone who is hung on a stake is under God’s curse. You must not defile the land that Jehovah your God is giving you as an inheritance.
The law is about a stake, one piece of timber, not a crossbeam.
Carrying His own stake, He went out to The Place of the Skull, which in Hebrew is called Golgotha.
He carried his own stake.
The God of our fathers raised up Jesus, whom you had killed by hanging Him on a stake.
Peter says they hung him on a stake. The Greek is xylon, timber.
Therefore, my beloved, flee from idolatry.
Flee from idolatry. A sacred image of the instrument is not worship.
I am Jehovah; that is My name! I will not yield My glory to another or My praise to idols.

The verse is why the name is printed. Jehovah identifies himself, and in the same breath he will not yield his glory to another or his praise to carved images. Hiding the name and then bowing to an image both miss what he said.
The speaker gives his personal name and then refuses to hand his glory to another or his praise to idols. A title such as Lord does not do that work. The name is the point of the sentence.
AKS reads “I am Jehovah; that is My name.” It does not replace the name with Lord, and it does not soften the refusal of idol praise.
May people know that you, whose name is Jehovah, You alone are the Most High over all the earth.
People are to know that his name is Jehovah.
You must not make for yourself an idol in the form of anything in the heavens above, on the earth below, or in the waters beneath.
No idol, and no bowing to one.
Little children, keep yourselves from idols.

John does not limit idols to statues of other nations’ gods. He tells his readers to keep themselves from idols after telling them to know the true God. An image bowed to, kissed, or treated as a channel of worship is the thing the command refuses.
The last line of the letter is a command, not a suggestion about taste. Idols are to be kept away from. The letter has just said the Son of God has come so that readers may know the one who is true.
AKS says “Little children, keep yourselves from idols.” It does not add an exception for images used as aids.
You must not make for yourself an idol in the form of anything in the heavens above, on the earth below, or in the waters beneath.
No idol of anything in heaven or on earth, and no bowing.
I am Jehovah; that is My name! I will not yield My glory to another or My praise to idols.
Jehovah does not yield his praise to idols.
Therefore, my beloved, flee from idolatry.
Paul has just said you cannot share the Lord’s table and the table of demons. The conclusion is flight. An image that is only “a reminder” is still the thing this command tells the reader to leave.
Flee is the urgent verb. Idolatry is not a custom to be handled carefully. It is something to run from. The chapter has been talking about the cup and the table of demons.
AKS says “flee from idolatry.” It does not say avoid the excess of idolatry, or keep the image and drop the excess.
Little children, keep yourselves from idols.
Keep yourselves from idols.
You must not make for yourself an idol in the form of anything in the heavens above, on the earth below, or in the waters beneath.
The command not to make the image or bow to it.

topics.label: Spiritism
topics.ask: Why the dead cannot be consulted

thoughts.text: casts spells, consults a medium or spirit medium, or inquires of the dead.

Christendom has often prayed to the dead, or tried to hear from them. The dead know nothing, so they cannot answer. At Endor a figure spoke as Samuel after God had refused to speak to Saul. That was not Samuel raised. A wicked spirit can imitate a dead person.
Spiritism sits with idolatry among the works of the flesh. Isaiah tells people to consult their God, not the dead, on behalf of the living.
The verse names a medium, a spiritist, and the one who inquires of the dead. Those are practices, not a metaphor for ordinary grief.
AKS says not to consult a medium or a spiritist, or to inquire of the dead. Whoever does these things is detestable to Jehovah.
For whoever does these things is detestable to Jehovah. And because of these detestable things, Jehovah your God is driving out the nations before you.
These practices are detestable to Jehovah.
You must not turn to mediums or spirit mediums; do not seek them out, or you will be defiled by them. I am Jehovah your God.
Do not turn to mediums or spiritists.
When men tell you to consult mediums and spirit mediums who whisper and mutter, shouldn’t a people consult their God instead? Why consult the dead on behalf of the living?
Why consult the dead on behalf of the living?
For the living know that they will die, but the dead know nothing. They have no further reward, because the memory of them is forgotten.
The dead know nothing, so they cannot send a message.

Then Samuel said to Saul, “Why have you disturbed me by bringing me up?” “I am deeply distressed,” replied Saul. “The Philistines are fighting against me, and God has turned away from me. He no longer answers me, either by prophets or by dreams. So I have called on you to tell me what to do.”
The figure at Endor was not Samuel. God had already refused Saul.
idolatry and spiritism; hatred, discord, jealousy, and rage; rivalries, divisions, factions,
Spiritism is listed with idolatry among the works of the flesh.
You must not turn to mediums or spirit mediums; do not seek them out, or you will be defiled by them. I am Jehovah your God.

The dead are silent. Asking them for guidance is asking people who know nothing. This law says the contact itself defiles, whether or not the medium seems kind. The one to consult is Jehovah, who names himself in the same verse.
Mediums and spiritists are people who claim contact with the dead or with spirits. Turning to them defiles. The verse ends by naming Jehovah as the one who speaks the ban.
AKS says you must not turn to mediums or spiritists, or you will be defiled by them. I am Jehovah your God. The name is kept. Spiritists is the practice, not a metaphor for bad advice.
casts spells, consults a medium or spirit medium, or inquires of the dead.
No medium, no spiritist, no inquiry of the dead.
For the living know that they will die, but the dead know nothing. They have no further reward, because the memory of them is forgotten.
The dead know nothing to tell.
When men tell you to consult mediums and spirit mediums who whisper and mutter, shouldn’t a people consult their God instead? Why consult the dead on behalf of the living?
Isaiah does not treat the dead as helpers who can still speak if the rite is done properly. He treats the consultation as absurd. The living ask God. The dead have nothing to give the living.
The prophet mocks the invitation to consult whisperers. A people should consult their God. The dead are the wrong address for the living.
AKS says: shouldn’t a people consult their God instead? Why consult the dead on behalf of the living? The question is the argument.
You must not turn to mediums or spirit mediums; do not seek them out, or you will be defiled by them. I am Jehovah your God.
Mediums and spiritists defile.
It is not the dead who praise Jah, nor any who descend into silence.
The dead are in silence.
Then Saul said to his servants, “Find me a woman who is a medium, so I can go and consult her.” “There is a medium at Endor,” his servants replied.
Saul’s search for a woman who consulted the dead is the act of a man Jehovah had already left. It is not a pattern to follow.

topics.label: Mary
topics.ask: One mediator, not the mother of God

thoughts.text: For there is one God, and there is one mediator between God and men, a man, Christ Jesus,
Mary was the mother of Jesus, highly favored, and a woman of faith. She is not the mother of God, and she is not a mediator beside her son. God has always existed. He cannot have a mother.
When a woman blessed the womb that bore Jesus, he answered that the happy ones are those who hear God’s word and obey it. He had brothers. Worship and prayer go to God, not to a queen of heaven.
Mediator is singular. The verse names a man, Christ Jesus. It does not name his mother, and it does not call her the mother of God.
AKS says there is one God, and one mediator between God and men, a man, Christ Jesus. Mary is called highly favored, not full of grace and not a mediatrix.
The angel appeared to her and said, “Greetings, you who are highly favored! Jehovah is with you.”
She is highly favored. Jehovah is with her.
As Jesus was saying these things, a woman in the crowd raised her voice and said, “Happy is the womb that bore You, and happy are the breasts that nursed You!”
A woman blessed the womb that bore him.
But He replied, “Happy rather are those who hear the word of God and obey it.”
Happy rather are those who hear the word of God and obey it.
“Isn’t this the carpenter’s son? Isn’t His mother’s name Mary, and aren’t His brothers James, Joseph, Simon, and Judas?
His brothers are named. She did not remain childless.
“Away from Me, Satan!” Jesus told him. “For it is written: ‘Worship Jehovah your God and serve Him only.’”
Worship belongs to God alone.
The angel appeared to her and said, “Greetings, you who are highly favored! Jehovah is with you.”

The angel tells Mary she has been shown favor. He does not say she is the source of grace or a mediator. The greeting “Jehovah is with you” is the greeting Gideon heard. AKS uses the name there so the reader can see which Lord is meant, and it does not call her full of grace.

The Greek verb means to show favor, to treat graciously. It does not say Mary is a store of grace for other people to draw on. An older Latin line, full of grace, turned the favor she received into a title.

AKS says “Greetings, you who are highly favored! Jehovah is with you.” Highly favored keeps the verb as favor shown to her. Jehovah in the greeting follows the Hebrew form of this angelic hello, as in Judges 6:12. The note does not claim a surviving Greek copy of this verse still prints the four letters.
And the angel of Jehovah appeared to Gideon and said, “Jehovah is with you, O mighty man of valor.”
The same greeting: Jehovah is with you.
For there is one God, and there is one mediator between God and men, a man, Christ Jesus,
One mediator, the man Christ Jesus.
But He replied, “Happy rather are those who hear the word of God and obey it.”

Jesus does not deny that Mary bore him. He refuses to let that fact become the reason for the blessing. The people who hear and obey are the happy ones. That answer blocks every later attempt to build devotion on her motherhood instead of on obedience to God.
A woman in the crowd blesses the womb that bore him. Jesus answers with rather. The happiness he names is hearing the word of God and obeying it, not the biological tie.
AKS says “Happy rather are those who hear the word of God and obey it.” Rather is the correction. The woman’s blessing is not accepted as the last word.
As Jesus was saying these things, a woman in the crowd raised her voice and said, “Happy is the womb that bore You, and happy are the breasts that nursed You!”
The blessing he answers.
The angel appeared to her and said, “Greetings, you who are highly favored! Jehovah is with you.”
