She is highly favored. She is not the mediator.
“I am Jehovah’s servant,” Mary answered. “May it happen to me according to your word.” Then the angel left her.
Mary calls herself the slave of Jehovah. A slave is not a person to be prayed to.
“Woman, what is that to you and to Me?” Jesus replied. “My hour has not yet come.”
Jesus does not take direction from his mother in the matter of his hour. She is not the one who commands him.
With one accord they all continued in prayer, along with the women and Mary the mother of Jesus, and with His brothers.
Mary is with the disciples, praying. She is one of them, not the one they address.

topics.label: Titles
topics.ask: Why no one is called father

thoughts.text: And do not call anyone on earth your father, for you have one Father, who is in heaven.

Religious titles do the opposite of what Jesus told his followers. They are not to be called Rabbi. They have one Teacher, and they are all brothers. They are not to call a man father in the faith. They have one Father. They are not to be called leaders.
Their Leader is the Christ. Holy Father, in Jesus’ own prayer, is a title for God, not for a man.

Father here is a title of honor, the same kind of title as Rabbi. Jesus is not taking the family word away from a parent. He used that word for parents himself. The ban is on a religious title that lifts one man above his brothers.
AKS says do not call anyone on earth your father, for you have one Father, who is in heaven. The next line says one Leader, the Christ.
But you are not to be called ‘Rabbi,’ for you have one Teacher, and you are all brothers.
Do not be called Rabbi. One is your Teacher, and you are brothers.
Nor are you to be called leaders, for your Leader is one, the Christ.
Do not be called leaders. Your Leader is the Christ.
I will no longer be in the world, but they are in the world, and I am coming to You. Holy Father, protect them by Your name, the name You gave Me, so that they may be one as We are one.
Holy Father is how Jesus addresses God.
But you are not to be called ‘Rabbi,’ for you have one Teacher, and you are all brothers.

The next lines forbid father as a religious title and leader as a title. This line starts the series. One Teacher, and the rest are brothers. AKS does not turn Rabbi into a harmless courtesy the verse forgot to cancel.

Rabbi is the honorary title. Jesus forbids it for his disciples. The reason is that they have one Teacher and they are all brothers. A title that lifts one brother over the others breaks the sentence.
AKS says you are not to be called Rabbi, for you have one Teacher, and you are all brothers. Teacher is the one they have. Brothers is what they are.
And do not call anyone on earth your father, for you have one Father, who is in heaven.
Do not call anyone on earth your father.
Nor are you to be called leaders, for your Leader is one, the Christ.
Nor are you to be called leaders.
Nor are you to be called leaders, for your Leader is one, the Christ.
Taken with the ban on Rabbi and on father, the chapter leaves the disciples as brothers under one Teacher, one Father, and one Leader. Holy Father, in Jesus’ own prayer, belongs to God.
These verses are why a religious title that sets a man above his brothers does not fit the command.
Leaders is the title he withholds. The one Leader is the Christ. The disciples are not a staircase of religious ranks with a man at the top.
AKS says you are not to be called leaders, for your Leader is one, the Christ. Leader is reserved. It is not distributed.
But you are not to be called ‘Rabbi,’ for you have one Teacher, and you are all brothers.
One Teacher, and you are brothers.
And do not call anyone on earth your father, for you have one Father, who is in heaven.
One Father, who is in heaven.
This is a trustworthy saying: If anyone aspires to be an overseer, he desires a noble task.

The desire is for a task: watching over a flock. Paul tells the elders in Ephesus that the holy spirit made them overseers to shepherd the congregation. The qualifications that follow are about character, family, and teaching, not about a chain of ordination invented later.
No one in the congregation is to be called Father as a religious title. One is their Father in heaven.
The Greek ἐπίσκοπος (episkopos) is one who watches over. διάκονος (diakonos) is one who serves. Both words describe work. They do not describe a later rank with a special robe or title of Father.

AKS reads “if anyone aspires to be an overseer, he desires a noble task.” Task keeps the work in view. Bishop would import a later office the sentence does not name. The paired workers in Philippi are ministerial servants, not deacons of a denomination.
Paul and Timothy, slaves of Christ Jesus, To all the holy ones in union with Christ Jesus at Philippi, together with the overseers and ministerial servants:
Overseers and ministerial servants are named beside the holy ones, as workers among them.
Keep watch over yourselves and the entire flock of which the holy spirit has made you overseers. Be shepherds of the congregation of God, which He purchased with the blood of His own Son.
Overseers are to shepherd the congregation of God.
And do not call anyone on earth your father, for you have one Father, who is in heaven.
Do not call anyone on earth your father. The title belongs to the Father in heaven.

topics.label: Sabbath
topics.ask: Why the weekly rest is not required

thoughts.text: Therefore let no one judge you by what you eat or drink, or with regard to a feast, a New Moon, or a Sabbath.

Christians are not required to keep a weekly sabbath. That rest was a sign for Israel under the Law. Jesus kept it because he was born under that Law. His death ended the Law’s claim. Sunday did not become a new sabbath.
Esteeming one day above another is left to a person’s own mind. No one is to be judged for it.
Sabbath is the rest day named in the Law. Here it is listed with a feast and a new moon, the calendar of that Law. The next verse calls those things a shadow.
AKS says let no one judge you by what you eat or drink, or with regard to a feast, a New Moon, or a Sabbath.
These are a shadow of the things to come, but the body that casts it belongs to Christ.
These are a shadow. The body that casts it belongs to Christ.
The Israelites must keep the Sabbath, celebrating it as a permanent covenant for the generations to come.
The Sabbath was a covenant sign for Israel.
One person regards a certain day above the others, while someone else considers every day alike. Each one should be fully convinced in his own mind.
One person esteems a day. Another esteems every day alike.
But when the time had fully come, God sent His Son, born of a woman, born under the law,
Jesus was born under the Law, which is why he kept its sabbath.
One person regards a certain day above the others, while someone else considers every day alike. Each one should be fully convinced in his own mind.

If the weekly Sabbath were still the Christian rule, this verse could not leave the matter to personal conviction. Paul allows a brother to regard every day alike. That is the end of a commanded Sabbath rest as a law for the congregation.

One person ranks a day above the others. Another treats every day alike. Paul does not settle the dispute by imposing the Sabbath. He says each should be convinced in his own mind, inside a chapter about not judging a brother.
AKS says someone else considers every day alike. Alike is the real alternative. The verse does not say the Sabbath remains the day that must be kept.
Therefore let no one judge you by what you eat or drink, or with regard to a feast, a New Moon, or a Sabbath.
Let no one judge you regarding a Sabbath.
These are a shadow of the things to come, but the body that casts it belongs to Christ.
Those days were a shadow.
These are a shadow of the things to come, but the body that casts it belongs to Christ.

A shadow is useful until the person arrives. Paul says the days, including a sabbath, were that shadow, and the reality is Christ. Keeping the shadow as if it were still the law is judging people by something that has given way.
Shadow is the word for the outline that points to a body. The feast, the new moon, and the Sabbath are the shadow. The body that casts the shadow belongs to Christ.
AKS says these are a shadow of the things to come, but the body that casts it belongs to Christ. These looks back at the feast, the new moon, and the Sabbath in the previous verse.
Therefore let no one judge you by what you eat or drink, or with regard to a feast, a New Moon, or a Sabbath.
The verse that lists the Sabbath among the things not to judge by.
One person regards a certain day above the others, while someone else considers every day alike. Each one should be fully convinced in his own mind.
A Christian may consider every day alike.
You are observing special days and months and seasons and years!

Paul does not praise them for recovering a holy day. He is afraid his work was wasted because they are watching the calendar again. The Sabbath and the festival year sit inside that rebuke. Christ, not the day, is what they were called to.
Observing days, months, seasons, and years is what Paul is troubled by. The Galatians were turning back to elementary things as if those calendars could finish what Christ began.
AKS says “You are observing special days and months and seasons and years.” The exclamation is a rebuke, not a calendar to adopt.
Therefore let no one judge you by what you eat or drink, or with regard to a feast, a New Moon, or a Sabbath.
Do not let a sabbath day decide your standing.
One person regards a certain day above the others, while someone else considers every day alike. Each one should be fully convinced in his own mind.
Every day may be regarded alike.
There remains, then, a Sabbath rest for the people of God.
A sabbath rest remains for the people of God. The rest in view is the one still ahead, not a weekly obligation kept in order to be saved.

topics.label: Salvation
topics.ask: Why it can be lost

thoughts.text: Therefore, my beloved, just as you have always obeyed, not only in my presence, but now even more in my absence, continue to work out your salvation with fear and trembling.

A person who has believed is not told that the matter is finished. Salvation is kept by continuing. People who were enlightened, who tasted the heavenly gift, and who shared in the holy spirit can fall away.

If someone deliberately keeps on sinning after knowing the truth, no sacrifice for sins remains. Paul disciplined his body so that after preaching to others he would not be disqualified. The sheep in the Son’s hand are safe from being snatched.
That is not a promise that they may walk away and still be saved.
Work out is ongoing. Fear and trembling is the tone of someone who can fail, not of someone whose past confession cannot be undone.
AKS says continue to work out your salvation with fear and trembling.
It is impossible for those who have once been enlightened, who have tasted the heavenly gift, who have shared in the holy spirit,
Those once enlightened can fall away.
If we deliberately go on sinning after we have received the accurate knowledge of the truth, no further sacrifice for sins remains,
Willful sin after knowing the truth leaves no sacrifice.
No, I discipline my body and make it my slave, so that after I have preached to others, I myself will not be disqualified.
Paul could still be disqualified.
I give them everlasting life, and they will never perish. No one can snatch them out of My hand.
No one snatches the sheep. The verse does not say the sheep cannot leave.
But the one who perseveres to the end will be saved.

Jesus is talking about a hard season, and he ties salvation to staying through it. That is the opposite of a teaching that says the outcome is locked the moment a person first believes. The end is still ahead, and the persevering is still required.
Saved here belongs to the one who perseveres to the end. The verb is ongoing. A past moment of belief, with no continuance, is not what the sentence rewards.
AKS says the one who perseveres to the end will be saved. Perseveres is endurance, not a finished transaction that cannot be walked away from.
Therefore, my beloved, just as you have always obeyed, not only in my presence, but now even more in my absence, continue to work out your salvation with fear and trembling.
Work out your salvation with fear and trembling.
As the body without the spirit is dead, so faith without deeds is dead.
Faith without deeds is dead.
As the body without the spirit is dead, so faith without deeds is dead.

James refuses a faith that says the right sentence and does nothing. He compares it to a corpse. Salvation that cannot be lost, and that does not need to be lived, has no room for this line. The faith that lives is the faith that acts.
The comparison is a body without spirit. That body is dead. Faith without deeds is the same kind of dead. Deeds are not a decoration added to a faith that was already complete.

AKS says as the body without the spirit is dead, so faith without deeds is dead. Spirit here is the life-breath that makes the body a living person, matching the way Genesis speaks of breath. It is not a third person of God.
Therefore, my beloved, just as you have always obeyed, not only in my presence, but now even more in my absence, continue to work out your salvation with fear and trembling.
Salvation is worked out.
But the one who perseveres to the end will be saved.
Persevering to the end is what is saved.
For it is by undeserved kindness you have been saved through faith, and this not from yourselves; it is the gift of God,

The rescue is a gift of God. It is not from yourselves, so no one may boast. Faith receives it. Faith does not turn the gift into something the person produced. The next line still says we are created for good works. The kindness is undeserved. The life that follows is not idle.
The Greek χάρις (charis) is a gift, favor shown to someone who has not earned it. It is kindness with the debt left unpaid by the receiver.

AKS reads “by undeserved kindness you have been saved through faith.” Undeserved keeps the point that the gift is not a wage. Kindness keeps the warmth of the word. Grace, left alone, has become a church term that no longer says this.
To all in Rome who are loved by God and called to be holy ones: Undeserved kindness and peace to you from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
Undeserved kindness and peace come from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
For the wages sin pays is death, but the gift God gives is everlasting life by Christ Jesus our Lord.
The wages of sin is death. The gift is everlasting life.
not by works, so that no one can boast.
The salvation is not from works, so that no one may boast.

topics.label: Easter
topics.ask: Why it is not a Bible festival

thoughts.text: Get rid of the old leaven, that you may be a new unleavened batch, as you really are. For Christ, our Passover lamb, has been sacrificed.

Easter is not a Bible festival. The name and the customs come from old fertility rites. What the text commands is the remembrance of Christ’s death. He is the Passover lamb, and the bread and the cup are kept in memory of him.
Teaching human tradition as if it were doctrine is the thing Jesus condemned. Separate from what is unclean rather than dress a pagan spring feast in his name.
Pascha is Passover. The verse names that meal and that lamb. It does not name a spring goddess, eggs, or a sunrise service.
AKS says Christ, our Passover lamb, has been sacrificed. Acts 12:4 also says Passover. It does not put a later festival name there.
And this day will be a memorial for you, and you are to celebrate it as a feast to Jehovah, as a permanent regulation for the generations to come.
The memorial Israel was told to keep was Passover.
And He took the bread, gave thanks and broke it, and gave it to them, saying, “This is My body, given for you; do this in remembrance of Me.”
Do this in remembrance of me. The command is his death, not his birth.
He arrested him and put him in prison, handing him over to be guarded by four squads of four soldiers each. Herod intended to bring him out to the people after the Passover.
The season is the Passover.
They worship Me in vain; they teach as doctrine the orders of men.’
Worship is empty when human rules are taught as doctrine.
“Therefore come out from among them and be separate, says Jehovah. Touch no unclean thing, and I will receive you.”
Come out from among them and be separate.
He arrested him and put him in prison, handing him over to be guarded by four squads of four soldiers each. Herod intended to bring him out to the people after the Passover.

Luke is dating Herod’s plan by the Passover. Putting a spring festival’s later name into the sentence makes the Bible sound as if that festival belonged to the apostles. AKS keeps Passover so the verse stays inside the feast it is actually naming.

The Greek word is pascha, the Passover. It is the same word Paul uses when he says Christ our Passover lamb has been sacrificed. An older English Bible put Easter in this verse. That is a later festival name, not the word Luke wrote.
AKS says Herod intended to bring him out after the Passover. It does not say Easter. The word is the Jewish feast already under way in the chapter.
Get rid of the old leaven, that you may be a new unleavened batch, as you really are. For Christ, our Passover lamb, has been sacrificed.
Christ, our Passover lamb.
And He took the bread, gave thanks and broke it, and gave it to them, saying, “This is My body, given for you; do this in remembrance of Me.”
The meal Jesus gave is tied to that Passover night, not to a later holiday.
See to it that no one takes you captive through philosophy and empty deception, which are based on human tradition and the spiritual forces of the world rather than on Christ.
Watch that no one takes you captive through the tradition of men. A festival the Scriptures never command is that kind of tradition.

topics.label: Nationalism
topics.ask: No part of the world, and no sword

thoughts.text: They are no part of the world, just as I am no part of the world.

National pride asks people to take up the sword for a country. Jesus says his followers are no part of the world, as he was no part of it. His kingdom is no part of this world, so his servants do not fight to keep him from arrest. Those who draw the sword die by it.

The nations are to beat swords into plowshares and stop training for war. Governing authorities are still obeyed, and Caesar is given what is his. When a command conflicts with God, God is obeyed rather than men. Brothers do not train to kill brothers.
The phrase is out of the world. AKS reads no part of the world. It is a separation from the world’s fights and loyalties, not a command to leave the earth.
AKS says they are no part of the world, just as I am no part of the world.
Jesus answered, “My Kingdom is no part of this world; if it were, My servants would fight to prevent My arrest by the Jews. But now My Kingdom is no part of this realm.”
The Kingdom is no part of this world, so his servants do not fight.
“Put your sword back in its place,” Jesus said to him. “For all who draw the sword will die by the sword.
All who draw the sword will die by the sword.

Then He will judge between the nations and arbitrate for many peoples. They will beat their swords into plowshares and their spears into pruning hooks. Nation will no longer take up the sword against nation, nor train anymore for war.
They will beat swords into plowshares and learn war no more.
Everyone must submit himself to the governing authorities, for there is no authority except that which is from God. The authorities that exist have been appointed by God.
Be in subjection to the governing authorities.
“Caesar’s,” they answered. So Jesus told them, “Give to Caesar what is Caesar’s, and to God what is God’s.”
Give Caesar what is Caesar’s, and God what is God’s.
But Peter and the other apostles replied, “We must obey God rather than men.
Obey God rather than men when the two conflict.

Then He will judge between the nations and arbitrate for many peoples. They will beat their swords into plowshares and their spears into pruning hooks. Nation will no longer take up the sword against nation, nor train anymore for war.

God’s stated future is the end of war between nations. His people do not spend the present learning to kill one another for a flag while they pray for that future. The verse is a promise, and it is also a direction.
The verbs are future and final. Nations beat swords into plowshares and stop learning war. The judge between the nations is Jehovah, not a country.
AKS says nation will no longer take up the sword against nation, nor train anymore for war. Train anymore is the end of military schooling, not a pause between campaigns.
Jesus answered, “My Kingdom is no part of this world; if it were, My servants would fight to prevent My arrest by the Jews. But now My Kingdom is no part of this realm.”
His servants do not fight. The Kingdom is no part of this world.
“Put your sword back in its place,” Jesus said to him. “For all who draw the sword will die by the sword.
Those who draw the sword die by it.
“Put your sword back in its place,” Jesus said to him. “For all who draw the sword will die by the sword.

Peter is defending the Christ, and even that cause is refused. If the sword is wrong when it is drawn for Jesus, it is not made right by drawing it for a country. The Kingdom he is about to describe to Pilate does not keep him by fighting.
Jesus stops the sword in the moment it is drawn for him. The proverb is general: all who take the sword die by it. He does not add an exception for a righteous nation.
AKS says “Put your sword back in its place. For all who draw the sword will die by the sword.” All is unrestricted.
Jesus answered, “My Kingdom is no part of this world; if it were, My servants would fight to prevent My arrest by the Jews. But now My Kingdom is no part of this realm.”
My servants would fight if my Kingdom were part of this world.

Then He will judge between the nations and arbitrate for many peoples. They will beat their swords into plowshares and their spears into pruning hooks. Nation will no longer take up the sword against nation, nor train anymore for war.
They will not train for war anymore.
Jesus answered, “My Kingdom is no part of this world; if it were, My servants would fight to prevent My arrest by the Jews. But now My Kingdom is no part of this realm.”

Jesus explains his arrest with a political fact. His Kingdom does not belong to this order of nations, so his people are not its soldiers. Caesar still receives what is Caesar’s, and the governing authorities are still obeyed.
When the order is to kill, this verse has already said his servants do not fight.
No part of this world is the same separation Jesus prays for his disciples. If the Kingdom were part of this world, his servants would fight. They do not. That is the proof he offers Pilate.
AKS says “My Kingdom is no part of this world” and “My servants would fight.” No part of is the phrase used of the disciples in John 17. Fight is the thing his servants do not do.
They are no part of the world, just as I am no part of the world.
They are no part of the world, just as he is.
Everyone must submit himself to the governing authorities, for there is no authority except that which is from God. The authorities that exist have been appointed by God.
They still submit to the governing authorities.
Everyone must submit himself to the governing authorities, for there is no authority except that which is from God. The authorities that exist have been appointed by God.

Relative subjection is real. Taxes are paid. Laws are kept. Honor is given. The same apostle’s Lord said that those who draw the sword die by it, and that his servants do not fight to keep a kingdom of this world. When a command conflicts with God, God is obeyed rather than men.
Submission does not include killing a brother for a nation.
Submit is the command toward the authorities that exist. It is not a command to become the authority’s weapon. The chapter goes on to taxes, honor, and fear. It does not go on to military service.
AKS says everyone must submit himself to the governing authorities, for the authorities that exist have been appointed by God. Submit is obedience in the civil sphere. It is not rendered as enlist.
Jesus answered, “My Kingdom is no part of this world; if it were, My servants would fight to prevent My arrest by the Jews. But now My Kingdom is no part of this realm.”
His servants do not fight.
But Peter and the other apostles replied, “We must obey God rather than men.
We must obey God rather than men.
Then Peter began to speak: “I now truly understand that God does not show favoritism,
God is not partial. The nation a person is born into does not put him closer to God.

topics.ask: Why the name is to be used

thoughts.text: May people know that you, whose name is Jehovah, You alone are the Most High over all the earth.

Some say God’s name should not be used. Scripture says the opposite. The name appears thousands of times in the Hebrew text. Psalm 83 asks that people know it. Jesus taught his disciples to pray that the Father’s name be sanctified, and he said he had made that name known.

Exodus 20:7 forbids taking the name up in a worthless way. It does not forbid saying it. The psalms that contain the name were sung aloud. Not knowing the ancient vowels is no reason to hide the name.
People still say Jesus without claiming to have recovered a first-century pronunciation. Jehovah is the form long used in English for the name, and AKS keeps it where the Hebrew text has it.
The divine name is a personal name, not a title such as Lord or God. The teaching that the name is too holy to speak is not this verse. The verse exists so that people will know the name.
AKS reads that people may know that You alone, whose name is Jehovah, are Most High over all the earth. The name is printed, not replaced with Lord.

God also told Moses, “Say to the Israelites, ‘Jehovah, the God of your fathers—the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob—has sent me to you.’ This is My name forever, and this is how I am to be remembered in every generation.
The name Jehovah is the memorial for every generation.
So then, this is how you should pray: ‘Our Father in the heavens, let your name be sanctified.
Let your name be sanctified.
You must not take the name of Jehovah your God in vain, for Jehovah will not leave anyone unpunished who takes His name in vain.
Worthless use is forbidden. Use itself is not.
I have revealed Your name to those You have given Me out of the world. They were Yours; You gave them to Me, and they have kept Your word.
Jesus made the Father’s name known.
And I have made Your name known to them and will continue to make it known, so that the love You have for Me may be in them, and I in union with them.”
He would continue to make the name known.
And everyone who calls on the name of Jehovah will be saved; for on Mount Zion and in Jerusalem there will be deliverance, as Jehovah has promised, among the remnant called by Jehovah.
People must call on the name of Jehovah.
Jesus replied, “It is also written: ‘Do not put Jehovah your God to the test.’”
This verse quotes or closely cites Deuteronomy 6:16, where the divine name appears. AKS keeps Jehovah in the quotation so the reader can see who is being spoken of in the Hebrew passage.

Do not test Jehovah your God as you tested Him at Massah.

Isaiah asks who has directed the spirit of Jehovah, or been His counselor.
for, “The earth is Jehovah’s, and everything in it.”
This verse quotes or closely cites Psalm 24:1, where the divine name appears. AKS keeps Jehovah in the quotation so the reader can see who is being spoken of in the Hebrew passage.
The name is a translation decision about the quotation, not a claim that every later Greek copy still prints the Hebrew letters.

The Hebrew passage uses the divine name. Later copies of the Christian Greek Scriptures generally use a word meaning Lord (kyrios) where a translator must decide whether the quotation still refers to that name.

AKS uses Jehovah in this quotation because the Hebrew passage being quoted contains the divine name, and the speaker or writer is citing that passage. This note does not claim that a surviving Greek copy of this verse still shows the four letters of the name. It records why the name is restored in the quotation.
A Psalm of David. The earth is Jehovah’s, and everything in it, the world and all who dwell in it.
The earth belongs to Jehovah.
But God found fault with the people and said: “Look, the days are coming, declares Jehovah, when I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah.
This verse quotes or closely cites Jeremiah 31:31, where the divine name appears. AKS keeps Jehovah in the quotation so the reader can see who is being spoken of in the Hebrew passage.
The name is a translation decision about the quotation, not a claim that every later Greek copy still prints the Hebrew letters.

The Hebrew passage uses the divine name. Later copies of the Christian Greek Scriptures generally use a word meaning Lord (kyrios) where a translator must decide whether the quotation still refers to that name.

AKS uses Jehovah in this quotation because the Hebrew passage being quoted contains the divine name, and the speaker or writer is citing that passage. This note does not claim that a surviving Greek copy of this verse still shows the four letters of the name. It records why the name is restored in the quotation.
Look, the days are coming, declares Jehovah, when I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah.
Jehovah promises the new covenant.
“This is the covenant I will make with them after those days, declares Jehovah. I will put My laws in their hearts and inscribe them on their minds.”
This verse quotes or closely cites Jeremiah 31:33, where the divine name appears. AKS keeps Jehovah in the quotation so the reader can see who is being spoken of in the Hebrew passage.
The name is a translation decision about the quotation, not a claim that every later Greek copy still prints the Hebrew letters.

The Hebrew passage uses the divine name. Later copies of the Christian Greek Scriptures generally use a word meaning Lord (kyrios) where a translator must decide whether the quotation still refers to that name.

AKS uses Jehovah in this quotation because the Hebrew passage being quoted contains the divine name, and the speaker or writer is citing that passage. This note does not claim that a surviving Greek copy of this verse still shows the four letters of the name. It records why the name is restored in the quotation.
Look, the days are coming, declares Jehovah, when I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah.
The same promise is the setting for the law written on the heart.
For the eyes of Jehovah are on the righteous, and His ears are inclined to their prayer. But Jehovah’s presence is against those who do evil.”
This verse quotes or closely cites Psalm 34:15, where the divine name appears. AKS keeps Jehovah in the quotation so the reader can see who is being spoken of in the Hebrew passage.
The name is a translation decision about the quotation, not a claim that every later Greek copy still prints the Hebrew letters.

The Hebrew passage uses the divine name. Later copies of the Christian Greek Scriptures generally use a word meaning Lord (kyrios) where a translator must decide whether the quotation still refers to that name.

AKS uses Jehovah in this quotation because the Hebrew passage being quoted contains the divine name, and the speaker or writer is citing that passage. This note does not claim that a surviving Greek copy of this verse still shows the four letters of the name. It records why the name is restored in the quotation.
The eyes of Jehovah are on the righteous, and His ears are inclined to their cry.
Jehovah’s eyes are on the righteous.
And: “In the beginning, O Lord, You laid the foundations of the earth, and the heavens are the work of Your hands.

Hebrews 1:10 quotes the lines in Psalm 102 about the one who laid the earth’s foundations. AKS keeps “O Lord” there. The psalm as a whole is spoken to Jehovah, but that is not treated as a warrant to change this verse’s wording.

Psalm 102 is a prayer addressed to Jehovah, and the name appears in that psalm. AKS’s wording of Psalm 102:25 does not print the name in that particular verse. Later copies of Hebrews use a word meaning Lord (kyrios) in the quotation.
AKS reads Hebrews 1:10 as “O Lord,” not Jehovah. The name is not inserted. This note does not claim that a surviving Greek copy of the verse still shows the four letters of the name.
A prayer of one who is afflicted, when he grows faint and pours out his lament before Jehovah. Hear my prayer, O Jehovah; let my cry for help come before You.
The psalm opens as a prayer before Jehovah.
In the beginning You laid the foundations of the earth, and the heavens are the work of Your hands.
The lines about the earth’s foundations that Hebrews quotes. AKS does not print Jehovah in this verse.
now that you have tasted that the Lord is kind.
This verse draws on Psalm 34:8, and that Hebrew passage uses the divine name. AKS does not automatically copy the name into the Christian Greek Scripture verse.
Here the published AKS wording uses Lord, because the quotation’s wording and context are not treated as a blank warrant to insert the name.

The Hebrew passage uses the divine name. Later copies of the Christian Greek Scriptures generally use a word meaning Lord (kyrios) where a translator must decide whether the quotation still refers to that name.

The Hebrew passage contains the divine name, but AKS does not place Jehovah in this Christian Greek Scripture verse. The Greek copies use a word meaning Lord, and the verse’s own context has to be read before the name is inserted. AKS leaves the wording as Lord here.
Taste and see that Jehovah is good; blessed is the man who takes refuge in Him!
The psalm says Jehovah is good.

God also told Moses, “Say to the Israelites, ‘Jehovah, the God of your fathers—the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob—has sent me to you.’ This is My name forever, and this is how I am to be remembered in every generation.

Exodus 3:15 gives the name as the memorial by which God is to be remembered. A title can describe a role. This name identifies the one who spoke to Moses and to the fathers. AKS keeps it visible so readers are not left thinking the text only said Lord.
The four Hebrew letters of the divine name are not a title such as God or Lord. AKS represents them by the name Jehovah, the form long used in English for that name.
Where the Hebrew text has the divine name, AKS prints Jehovah rather than substituting Lord or God. That choice is about the name itself, not about every later Greek word for Lord.
Listen, O Israel: Jehovah our God is one Jehovah.
Israel’s confession uses the divine name.
A Psalm of David. Jehovah said to my Lord: “Sit at My right hand until I make Your enemies a footstool for Your feet.”

Jesus later asks how David can call this descendant Lord. The verse itself already separates the speaker from the one invited to the place of honor. Collapsing both into a single title hides that conversation.
Psalm 110:1 uses the divine name for the one who speaks, and a different Hebrew word for “my lord,” the one addressed. The two are not the same word and not the same person.
AKS reads “Jehovah said to my Lord.” The name is kept for the speaker. Lord, for the one told to sit at his right hand, is the other figure in the verse.
‘Jehovah said to my Lord, “Sit at My right hand until I put Your enemies under Your feet.”’
Jesus quotes the psalm and keeps the two persons distinct.
now that you have tasted that the Lord is kind.

A mechanical swap would erase real differences between passages. Psalm 34:8 uses the divine name. This later line, in AKS, says Lord. The notes on each quotation record that decision instead of hiding it.
Kyrios means lord or master. In quotations of the Hebrew Scriptures it sometimes stands where the divine name stood, and sometimes it means a human or messianic lord. The verse decides which.
AKS does not replace every Lord with Jehovah. Where the Hebrew quotation and the context support the divine name, AKS uses Jehovah. Where they do not, AKS keeps Lord, as in this line.
Taste and see that Jehovah is good; blessed is the man who takes refuge in Him!
The Hebrew line uses the divine name.
God said to Moses: “I Will Become What I Choose to Become.” And he added: “This is what you are to say to the Israelites, ‘I Will Become has sent me to you.’”

Moses asked what he should say when Israel asked for the name of the God of their fathers. The answer is first a statement about what God will become toward them, and then the personal name by which he is to be remembered. The verb and the name belong together.
One describes his activity. The other identifies him.
The Hebrew expression is a verb of becoming, spoken as something God will be or will prove to be. It is not a static I am. AKS also allows the sense I Will Prove to Be What I Will Prove to Be.
AKS reads I Will Become What I Choose to Become, and then I Will Become has sent me to you. The memorial name in the next verse is Jehovah.

God also told Moses, “Say to the Israelites, ‘Jehovah, the God of your fathers—the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob—has sent me to you.’ This is My name forever, and this is how I am to be remembered in every generation.
Jehovah is the name to be remembered for all generations.
Listen, O Israel: Jehovah our God is one Jehovah.
The word Trinity never appears in Scripture. This is the confession Jesus himself calls the greatest commandment’s opening. Jehovah is one. He is not described here as three coequal persons.
Later lines that are asked to carry that idea, including “I and the Father are one,” have to be read so they do not cancel this sentence.
The confession uses the divine name and the word one. It identifies one person, Jehovah, not a group of persons sharing a title.
AKS reads “Hear, O Israel: Jehovah our God is one Jehovah.” The name is kept, and one is not expanded into three.
Jesus replied, “This is the most important: ‘Hear, O Israel, Jehovah our God is one Jehovah.
Jesus quotes this confession as the first command.
I and the Father are one.”
A different kind of oneness, tested by John 17:21.
May people know that you, whose name is Jehovah, You alone are the Most High over all the earth.
Jehovah alone is the Most High.
So then, this is how you should pray: ‘Our Father in the heavens, let your name be sanctified.

Jesus did not teach his disciples to avoid the divine name. He taught them to pray about it first. Replacing the name everywhere with Lord makes this line hollow, because the reader no longer knows which name is being hallowed.
AKS keeps Jehovah in the Hebrew Scriptures so the name in this prayer has someone to point to.
The model prayer opens with the Father’s name, not with a title standing in for a hidden name. A name that must not be spoken cannot be the first petition.
AKS reads “let your name be sanctified.” Sanctified means set apart as holy, which includes knowing whose name it is.
May people know that you, whose name is Jehovah, You alone are the Most High over all the earth.
The name is Jehovah, and he alone is Most High.
I have revealed Your name to those You have given Me out of the world. They were Yours; You gave them to Me, and they have kept Your word.
Jesus revealed the name to his disciples.
You must not take the name of Jehovah your God in vain, for Jehovah will not leave anyone unpunished who takes His name in vain.

The idea that God forbade the pronouncing of his name does not come from this verse. The verse names Jehovah and then forbids a cheap or empty use of that name. Faithful people called on the name. Hiding it was a later custom, not this command.
The command is about worthless or vain use. The Hebrew writers who received this law used the name constantly, including in public song.
AKS says you shall not take the name of Jehovah your God in vain. It does not say you shall not speak the name.
May people know that you, whose name is Jehovah, You alone are the Most High over all the earth.
The name is to be known.
And everyone who calls on the name of Jehovah will be saved; for on Mount Zion and in Jerusalem there will be deliverance, as Jehovah has promised, among the remnant called by Jehovah.
Call on the name of Jehovah and be saved.
I have revealed Your name to those You have given Me out of the world. They were Yours; You gave them to Me, and they have kept Your word.

If the divine name were too sacred for human lips, the Son would not list the revealing of it as part of his work. He says he made it known and would continue to make it known. Removing the name from the Hebrew quotations he and the apostles used hides the very thing he revealed.
Jesus says he revealed the Father’s name to the disciples. A ministry that made the name known cannot be the source of a rule that the name must not be used.
AKS says “I have revealed Your name.” The name is something disclosed, not something retired.
And I have made Your name known to them and will continue to make it known, so that the love You have for Me may be in them, and I in union with them.”
He continues to make the name known.

God also told Moses, “Say to the Israelites, ‘Jehovah, the God of your fathers—the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob—has sent me to you.’ This is My name forever, and this is how I am to be remembered in every generation.
The memorial name is Jehovah.
So then, this is how you should pray: ‘Our Father in the heavens, let your name be sanctified.
The prayer asks that the name be sanctified.
I am Jehovah; that is My name! I will not yield My glory to another or My praise to idols.

The verse is why the name is printed. Jehovah identifies himself, and in the same breath he will not yield his glory to another or his praise to carved images. Hiding the name and then bowing to an image both miss what he said.
The speaker gives his personal name and then refuses to hand his glory to another or his praise to idols. A title such as Lord does not do that work. The name is the point of the sentence.
AKS reads “I am Jehovah; that is My name.” It does not replace the name with Lord, and it does not soften the refusal of idol praise.
May people know that you, whose name is Jehovah, You alone are the Most High over all the earth.
People are to know that his name is Jehovah.
You must not make for yourself an idol in the form of anything in the heavens above, on the earth below, or in the waters beneath.
No idol, and no bowing to one.
And I have made Your name known to them and will continue to make it known, so that the love You have for Me may be in them, and I in union with them.”

Jesus closes the prayer the way he opened his work with the disciples: the Father’s name is something he made known, and he would keep making it known. A Bible that never prints the name leaves this sentence without the word he said he revealed.
Made known is something disclosed and then continued. The name is not a secret Jesus retired after one mention.
AKS says “I have made Your name known to them and will continue to make it known.” Known is the verb. The name is the object.
I have revealed Your name to those You have given Me out of the world. They were Yours; You gave them to Me, and they have kept Your word.
The same prayer, earlier: I have revealed your name.

God also told Moses, “Say to the Israelites, ‘Jehovah, the God of your fathers—the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob—has sent me to you.’ This is My name forever, and this is how I am to be remembered in every generation.
The name to be remembered in every generation.
And everyone who calls on the name of Jehovah will be saved; for on Mount Zion and in Jerusalem there will be deliverance, as Jehovah has promised, among the remnant called by Jehovah.

Rescue in this verse is for people who call on a name, not on a substitute title. Peter and Paul both quote the line. AKS keeps Jehovah here so those later quotations have a Hebrew sentence to point back to.
The Hebrew line names the one to be called on. Later quotations of this promise are why AKS restores Jehovah in Acts 2:21 and Romans 10:13, and why the Hebrew verse itself is not printed as Lord.
AKS reads “everyone who calls on the name of Jehovah will be saved.” The name stays in the promise. Lord would hide who is being called on.
And everyone who calls on the name of Jehovah will be saved.’
Peter quotes this promise.
for, “Everyone who calls on the name of Jehovah will be saved.”
Paul quotes the same promise.

At that time those who feared Jehovah spoke with one another, and Jehovah listened and heard them. So a scroll of remembrance was written before Him regarding those who feared Jehovah and honored His name.
The people in this verse are not marked for refusing to say the name. They are marked for fearing Jehovah and honoring his name. That is the opposite of treating the name as too holy to use.
Honored his name is esteem, not avoidance. The scroll of remembrance is for people who feared Jehovah and treated the name as something to be held in honor.
AKS says a scroll of remembrance was written for those who feared Jehovah and honored His name. The name is the object of the honor.
May people know that you, whose name is Jehovah, You alone are the Most High over all the earth.
The name they honored is Jehovah.
You must not take the name of Jehovah your God in vain, for Jehovah will not leave anyone unpunished who takes His name in vain.
Worthless use is forbidden. Honor is commanded by the contrast.
The angel appeared to her and said, “Greetings, you who are highly favored! Jehovah is with you.”

The angel tells Mary she has been shown favor. He does not say she is the source of grace or a mediator. The greeting “Jehovah is with you” is the greeting Gideon heard. AKS uses the name there so the reader can see which Lord is meant, and it does not call her full of grace.

The Greek verb means to show favor, to treat graciously. It does not say Mary is a store of grace for other people to draw on. An older Latin line, full of grace, turned the favor she received into a title.

AKS says “Greetings, you who are highly favored! Jehovah is with you.” Highly favored keeps the verb as favor shown to her. Jehovah in the greeting follows the Hebrew form of this angelic hello, as in Judges 6:12. The note does not claim a surviving Greek copy of this verse still prints the four letters.
And the angel of Jehovah appeared to Gideon and said, “Jehovah is with you, O mighty man of valor.”
The same greeting: Jehovah is with you.
For there is one God, and there is one mediator between God and men, a man, Christ Jesus,
One mediator, the man Christ Jesus.
But even the archangel Michael, when he disputed with the devil over the body of Moses, did not presume to bring a slanderous charge against him, but said, “Jehovah rebuke you!”

One person is called the archangel, and his name is Michael. He does not act as the Almighty. He asks Jehovah to rebuke the devil. That fits a chief angel who has a God over him. The Lord Jesus descends with an archangel’s voice and also has a God. The titles meet.
They are not two rival commanders of the holy angels.

Michael is called the archangel, with the article in the sense of the chief. He disputes with the devil and does not bring a judgment of his own. He says Jehovah rebuke you. The name in that rebuke is a translation decision: the Hebrew pattern of the angel’s rebuke uses the divine name, as in Zechariah 3:2.

AKS says the archangel Michael said, “Jehovah rebuke you.” Archangel is singular and is Michael’s title. Jehovah is used in the rebuke because that is the divine-name formula of the rebuke, not because every Lord in Jude becomes Jehovah.
For the Lord Himself will descend from heaven with a loud command, with the voice of an archangel, and with the trumpet of God, and the dead in Christ will be the first to rise.
The Lord descends with an archangel’s voice.
And Jehovah said to Satan: “Jehovah rebukes you, Satan! Indeed, Jehovah, who has chosen Jerusalem, rebukes you! Is not this man a firebrand snatched from the fire?”
The rebuke formula: Jehovah rebukes you, Satan.
After this I heard a sound like the roar of a great crowd in heaven, shouting: “Praise Jah! Salvation and glory and power belong to our God!

The great crowd shouts that salvation, glory, and power belong to our God. The first word of the shout already contains a form of his name. A translation that wants the name known does not hide that form inside a borrowed cheer.
The same short name is why the English form Jehovah is used wherever the four letters of the name stand in the Hebrew Scriptures.
The Hebrew הַלְלוּ־יָהּ (hallelu-Yah) is a command to praise, joined to Yah, a short form of the divine name. The shout is not a word with the name buried inside it.
AKS reads “Praise Jah!” The two parts stay visible: praise, and the name. Hallelujah would leave a reader hearing a cheer and missing whose name is in it.
May people know that you, whose name is Jehovah, You alone are the Most High over all the earth.
People are to know that Jehovah alone is the Most High.

God also told Moses, “Say to the Israelites, ‘Jehovah, the God of your fathers—the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob—has sent me to you.’ This is My name forever, and this is how I am to be remembered in every generation.
The name Jehovah is how he is to be remembered for all generations.
And I heard a sound like the roar of a great crowd, like the rushing of many waters, and like a mighty rumbling of thunder, crying out: “Praise Jah! For Jehovah our God the Almighty reigns.
The crowd shouts Praise Jah again as Jehovah begins to rule.
“Away from Me, Satan!” Jesus told him. “For it is written: ‘Worship Jehovah your God and serve Him only.’”

This verse quotes Deuteronomy 6:13, where the divine name appears. AKS keeps Jehovah in the quotation so the reader can see who is being spoken of. One Greek verb covers more than one act. A deep bow of honor is obeisance.

The devotion that may be given only to Jehovah is worship. Jesus uses the second when Satan asks to be bowed to as God. Revelation uses worship again when an angel tells John to stop and to worship God.
The distinction is in the English so a reader can see which act the verse is talking about.

Jesus answers Satan with a line from Deuteronomy. The Hebrew passage uses the divine name. The Greek verb in his answer is προσκυνέω (proskyneō), the same verb used when people bow. In this sentence the act is the exclusive honor of God, so the English is worship, not a general bow.

AKS reads “Worship Jehovah your God and serve Him only.” Jehovah is kept because the Hebrew passage being quoted contains the divine name. Worship is kept for this act. The sentence does not say the bow given to Jesus as Son is this same exclusive worship.
Fear Jehovah your God, serve Him only, and take your oaths in His name.
The command Jesus quotes: fear Jehovah and serve him.

On coming to the house, they saw the Child with His mother Mary, and they fell down and did obeisance to Him. Then they opened their treasures and presented Him with gifts of gold and frankincense and myrrh.
The astrologers’ bow to the child is called obeisance, not this exclusive worship.
“Lord, I believe,” he said. And he did obeisance to Jesus.
The man who was healed does obeisance to Jesus after calling him Lord.

topics.label: Birthdays
topics.ask: Why they are not a Bible pattern

thoughts.text: On the third day, which was Pharaoh’s birthday, he held a feast for all his officials, and in their presence he lifted up the heads of the chief cupbearer and the chief baker.

Scripture never shows a servant of God celebrating a birthday. That is not an accident of silence. It records two birthday feasts, both of men who did not serve Jehovah, and both are told in a bad light. Pharaoh’s feast includes an execution.

Herod’s feast ends with the head of John the Baptizer. The day of one’s death is said to be better than the day of one’s birth, because a finished life can have a good name and a mere birthday cannot.

The one observance Jesus told his disciples to keep is a memorial of his death, not of a birth. The later birthday custom also grew up with astrology and with rites meant to protect the person from spirits. Those are practices Scripture condemns.
The text does not contain a sentence that says “do not keep a birthday.” It does give the pattern, and the pattern is not a celebration.
The Hebrew narrative marks Pharaoh’s birthday as the day of a feast. The Bible does not pause to forbid the word birthday. It does show what the two birthday feasts it records were like.
AKS says the third day was Pharaoh’s birthday, and he held a feast. At that feast the baker was hanged. The only other birthday feast is Herod’s.
On Herod’s birthday, her opportunity arose. Herod held a banquet for his nobles and military commanders and the leading men of Galilee.
Herod’s birthday banquet, the other birthday in Scripture.
A good name is better than fine perfume, and one’s day of death is better than his day of birth.
The day of death is better than the day of birth.
And He took the bread, gave thanks and broke it, and gave it to them, saying, “This is My body, given for you; do this in remembrance of Me.”
The observance Jesus commanded is a memorial of his death.
Though these nations, which you will take possession of, listen to conjurers and fortune-tellers, Jehovah your God has not permitted you to do so.
Divination and customs like it are rejected.
On Herod’s birthday, her opportunity arose. Herod held a banquet for his nobles and military commanders and the leading men of Galilee.

This is the second and last birthday celebration in the Bible. Like Pharaoh’s, it belongs to a man outside the worship of Jehovah, and someone dies because of it. No apostle, prophet, or faithful king is shown doing this.
The silence around their births, and the darkness around these two feasts, is the Bible’s comment.
The account is a banquet on Herod’s birthday. The daughter’s dance pleases him, and the outcome is the death of John.
AKS says the opportunity came on Herod’s birthday, at a banquet for his nobles. The scene is not told as a model.
On the third day, which was Pharaoh’s birthday, he held a feast for all his officials, and in their presence he lifted up the heads of the chief cupbearer and the chief baker.
Pharaoh’s birthday feast.
A good name is better than fine perfume, and one’s day of death is better than his day of birth.
The day of death is better than the day of birth.
On Herod’s birthday, however, the daughter of Herodias danced before them and pleased Herod
Herod’s birthday is the setting of a dance and a murder. The Scriptures do not add a birthday of a faithful servant as a model.
After this, Job opened his mouth and cursed the day of his birth.
Job curses the day of his birth. The day is grief, not a festival.

topics.label: Christmas
topics.ask: Why it is not a Bible festival

thoughts.text: And there were shepherds residing in the fields nearby, keeping watch over their flocks by night.
The Bible does not give the day Jesus was born, and it never says to celebrate that day. Shepherds out with the flocks at night fit the warmer months, not the winter date later chosen.

That date was set to fall on a pagan sun festival, and the customs that gathered around it, feasting, gift-giving, lights, and trees, come from those older rites, not from Luke. Calling the result a feast to God does not make it one.

Israel once proclaimed a feast to Jehovah in front of a calf, and God rejected it. Jesus said worship is in vain when human precepts are taught as doctrine. Christmas is not of divine appointment. The birth matters. The festival does not.
The account says the shepherds were living out of doors and keeping watch at night over their flocks. It does not give a date. It does not tell anyone to celebrate the birth.
AKS says shepherds were residing in the fields nearby, keeping watch by night. A midwinter date is not in the verse.
Now in those days a decree went out from Caesar Augustus that a census should be taken of the whole empire.
A registration brought them to Bethlehem. No date is stated.
Jesus Himself was about thirty years old when He began His ministry. He was regarded as the son of Joseph, the son of Heli,
Jesus was about thirty when he began his work.
When Aaron saw this, he built an altar before the calf and proclaimed: “Tomorrow will be a feast to Jehovah.”
A feast named for Jehovah can still be worship he rejects.
They worship Me in vain; they teach as doctrine the orders of men.’”
Worship taught from human precepts is in vain.
A good name is better than fine perfume, and one’s day of death is better than his day of birth.
The day of death is better than the day of birth.
When Aaron saw this, he built an altar before the calf and proclaimed: “Tomorrow will be a feast to Jehovah.”
Putting God’s name on a celebration does not sanctify the celebration. The calf festival was called a feast to Jehovah and was still rebellion.

The same principle reaches any festival built from rites he did not command, including a birthday of the Son placed on a pagan date and filled with customs from that date. Good motives do not rewrite the command.
Aaron builds an altar to the calf and announces a feast to Jehovah. The name of the true God is attached to a worship God had not asked for.
AKS says Aaron proclaimed, “Tomorrow shall be a feast to Jehovah.” The next verses show the feast as something God rejects.
And there were shepherds residing in the fields nearby, keeping watch over their flocks by night.
The birth account gives no festival and no winter date.
Jesus replied, “And why do you break the command of God for the sake of your tradition?
Tradition is not allowed to override God’s command.
This is what Jehovah says: “Do not learn the ways of the nations or be terrified by the signs in the heavens, though the nations themselves are terrified by them.
Do not learn the way of the nations, and do not be terrified by the signs of the heavens the way they are.
Today in the city of David a Savior has been born to you. He is Christ the Lord!
The announcement is that a savior was born. The day is not dated, and no annual feast is commanded.

You must not worship Jehovah your God in this way, because they practice for their gods every detestable thing which Jehovah hates. They even burn their sons and daughters in the fire as sacrifices to their gods.
You must not worship Jehovah in their way. A custom taken from the nations does not become clean because the name of God is attached to it.

topics.label: Blood
topics.ask: Why blood is not taken as food

thoughts.text: You must abstain from food sacrificed to idols, from blood, from the meat of strangled animals, and from sexual immorality. You will do well to avoid these things. Farewell.

Blood stands for life, and life belongs to God. After the Flood, humans could eat flesh, but not the blood. Israel was told the same, because the life is the blood. The Christian congregation received the command again: abstain from blood.

Eating blood, or meat that was never bled, sets that command aside. Taking whole blood into the body as a transfusion is the same kind of taking in. It is not a use the Bible allows merely because the method is medical and later.

The command is to keep abstaining from blood. It stands in the same list as idol food, meat from a strangled animal, and sexual immorality. It is not a ceremony of the Mosaic Law that the letter cancels. The letter is imposing it on Christians.
AKS says you must abstain from food sacrificed to idols, from blood, from the meat of strangled animals, and from sexual immorality.
But you must not eat meat with its lifeblood still in it.
Do not eat flesh with its blood.

For the life of all flesh is its blood. Therefore I have told the Israelites, ‘You must not eat the blood of any living thing, because the life of all flesh is its blood; whoever eats it must be cut off.’
The life of the flesh is its blood.
Instead, we should write and tell them to abstain from food polluted by idols, from sexual immorality, from the meat of strangled animals, and from blood.
The same command, given to be written to the congregations.
But you must not eat meat with its lifeblood still in it.

The line is older than the Law of Moses and is repeated for Christians. Blood is not eaten, and it is not taken into the body to keep a person alive. The life is in the blood, so the main parts of blood are included, not only blood left whole. A small fraction is different.

Scripture does not name every fraction a later treatment might use, so that choice is personal and is made in prayer. Blood that has been stored in order to be put back is still the blood the command says to abstain from. The verse is not a medical list.
It is a command, and the command is kept.
The command to Noah is about eating flesh that still has its blood, its life. It is given to the family from which all nations come, not only to Israel.
AKS says you must not eat meat with its lifeblood still in it. The life and the blood are one prohibition.
You must abstain from food sacrificed to idols, from blood, from the meat of strangled animals, and from sexual immorality. You will do well to avoid these things. Farewell.
Christians are told to keep abstaining from blood.

For the life of all flesh is its blood. Therefore I have told the Israelites, ‘You must not eat the blood of any living thing, because the life of all flesh is its blood; whoever eats it must be cut off.’
The life of all flesh is its blood.
Brothers, I have applied these things to myself and Apollos for your benefit, so that you may learn from us not to go beyond what is written. Then you will not take pride in one man over another.
Do not go beyond the things that are written.

For the life of all flesh is its blood. Therefore I have told the Israelites, ‘You must not eat the blood of any living thing, because the life of all flesh is its blood; whoever eats it must be cut off.’

The law gives the reason inside the ban. Blood is the life, so it is not food. Acts 15 repeats abstain from blood for Christians. The verse is about blood as life, not about a menu. It does not, by itself, list every medical fraction of blood. Those limits are not written here.
Life and blood are identified. The prohibition is not a dietary preference. Whoever eats the blood is cut off, because he has eaten the life.
AKS says the life of all flesh is its blood, and you must not eat the blood of any living thing. Life is nephesh, the same word elsewhere rendered soul. Eating blood is eating the life.
You must abstain from food sacrificed to idols, from blood, from the meat of strangled animals, and from sexual immorality. You will do well to avoid these things. Farewell.
Abstain from blood.
Only be sure not to eat the blood, because the blood is the life, and you must not eat the life with the meat.
Do not eat the life with the meat.
Only be sure not to eat the blood, because the blood is the life, and you must not eat the life with the meat.

Moses does not say blood may be eaten if it is a small amount or if the eater is grateful. The life is in the blood, and the life is not food. That is the line behind the later Christian command to abstain from blood.
The sentence equates the blood and the life and then forbids eating the life with the meat. The ban is restated so Israel will not treat blood as a sauce.
AKS says be sure not to eat the blood, because the blood is the life, and you must not eat the life with the meat. Life and blood stay paired.

For the life of all flesh is its blood. Therefore I have told the Israelites, ‘You must not eat the blood of any living thing, because the life of all flesh is its blood; whoever eats it must be cut off.’
The life of the flesh is its blood.
But you must not eat meat with its lifeblood still in it.
The command already given to Noah.

topics.label: Kingdom
topics.ask: A government, and life on earth

thoughts.text: Let your Kingdom come. Let your will take place, as in heaven, also on earth.

God’s Kingdom is a government he sets up, with Jesus as the King he appointed. It is not a vague reign already complete in human hearts, because Jesus tells us to pray for it to come and for the earth to feel its will.

Daniel says this kingdom will crush human kingdoms and stand forever. The meek and the righteous inherit the earth and live on it. A limited number, 144,000, rule as kings with the Lamb over the earth.

A great crowd no one can number survives out of the great tribulation with the earthly hope. Jesus called those people his other sheep. The prayer is answered on the earth, not by abandoning the earth.
Kingdom in this prayer is a rule, not a feeling inside the worshiper. Jesus asks that it come, and that God’s will be done on earth as in heaven.
AKS reads “Let your Kingdom come. Let your will take place, as in heaven, also on earth.”

In the days of those kings, the God of heaven will set up a kingdom that will never be destroyed, nor will it be left to another people. It will shatter all these kingdoms and bring them to an end, but will itself stand forever.
God’s kingdom shatters human kingdoms and stands forever.
The righteous will inherit the earth and dwell in it forever.
The righteous will dwell on the earth forever.
Happy are the gentle, for they will inherit the earth.
The meek inherit the earth.
And I heard the number of those who were sealed, 144,000 from all the tribes of Israel:
The number sealed is 144,000.

After this I looked and saw a great crowd, which no man was able to number, from every nation and tribe and people and tongue, standing before the throne and before the Lamb. They were wearing white robes and holding palm branches in their hands.
A great crowd no man can number.
You have made them to be a kingdom and priests to serve our God, and they will rule as kings over the earth.”
They rule as kings over the earth.
I have other sheep that are not of this fold. I must bring them in as well, and they will listen to My voice. Then there will be one flock and one shepherd.
The other sheep become one flock.
‘He will wipe away every tear from their eyes,’ and there will be no more death or mourning or crying or pain, for the former things have passed away.”
Death, mourning, and pain pass away.
And I heard the number of those who were sealed, 144,000 from all the tribes of Israel:

The little flock is given the kingdom. Their hope is heavenly, and their work is to rule over the earth with the Lamb. They are not the whole company of the saved. John distinguishes them from the great crowd.
Reading 144,000 as a vague “many” erases the contrast the vision draws on purpose.

John hears a number, 144,000. Later he sees them with the Lamb on the heavenly Mount Zion. The number is not a symbol standing in for an uncounted church, because he immediately sees another group that cannot be numbered.
AKS says the number of those sealed was 144,000. Revelation 5:10 says they rule as kings over the earth, not that every worshiper goes to heaven.
Then I looked and saw the Lamb standing on Mount Zion, and with Him 144,000 who had His name and His Father’s name written on their foreheads.
The Lamb, and with him 144,000.
You have made them to be a kingdom and priests to serve our God, and they will rule as kings over the earth.”
They rule as kings over the earth.
Do not be afraid, little flock, for your Father is pleased to give you the kingdom.
The little flock is given the kingdom.

After this I looked and saw a great crowd, which no man was able to number, from every nation and tribe and people and tongue, standing before the throne and before the Lamb. They were wearing white robes and holding palm branches in their hands.
The great crowd is a different group, and it is unnumbered.

After this I looked and saw a great crowd, which no man was able to number, from every nation and tribe and people and tongue, standing before the throne and before the Lamb. They were wearing white robes and holding palm branches in their hands.

The great crowd comes out of the great tribulation. They survive it. They are not taken to heaven to rule. Their hope is life on the Paradise earth, the earth the meek inherit and the earth where God’s will is to be done.
They are Jesus’ other sheep, one flock with the little flock, but not the same hope and not the parties to the new covenant. Standing before the throne is the language of approved worshipers.
Serving in his temple is the courtyard of worship on earth, not a second group of kings on the heavenly Mount Zion.
John hears 144,000, then looks and sees a great crowd that no man can number, from every nation. The two descriptions are not two ways of saying the same group.
AKS says he saw a great crowd which no man was able to number, out of every nation, standing before the throne and before the Lamb.
And I heard the number of those who were sealed, 144,000 from all the tribes of Israel:
The numbered group is stated first, and it is limited.
I have other sheep that are not of this fold. I must bring them in as well, and they will listen to My voice. Then there will be one flock and one shepherd.
Other sheep, not of this fold.
The righteous will inherit the earth and dwell in it forever.
The righteous dwell on the earth forever.
Let your Kingdom come. Let your will take place, as in heaven, also on earth.
God’s will is to take place on earth.
Do not be afraid, little flock, for your Father is pleased to give you the kingdom.

Heaven’s ruling hope belongs to a little flock. Jesus does not tell a crowd of every good person that the Kingdom is theirs to inherit as kings. He tells a small flock not to be afraid, because the Father wants to give them that Kingdom.

John later hears their number, 144,000, and sees them with the Lamb. The great crowd is the other group, and it cannot be numbered. One flock under one shepherd does not erase the difference in the hope.
Little flock is poimnion, a small flock. The Father is pleased to give them the basileia, the Kingdom. The gift is to that flock, not to every sheep who would ever listen to the shepherd.
AKS says “Do not be afraid, little flock, for your Father is pleased to give you the kingdom.” Little is kept. The kingdom is given to the ones he is addressing.
And I heard the number of those who were sealed, 144,000 from all the tribes of Israel:
The number sealed is 144,000.
Then I looked and saw the Lamb standing on Mount Zion, and with Him 144,000 who had His name and His Father’s name written on their foreheads.
The 144,000 stand with the Lamb on Mount Zion.
I have other sheep that are not of this fold. I must bring them in as well, and they will listen to My voice. Then there will be one flock and one shepherd.
The other sheep are not of this fold.
You have made them to be a kingdom and priests to serve our God, and they will rule as kings over the earth.”
They rule as kings over the earth.
I have other sheep that are not of this fold. I must bring them in as well, and they will listen to My voice. Then there will be one flock and one shepherd.

The fold Jesus was addressing is the little flock, the ones given the Kingdom and brought into the new covenant. The other sheep are real, and they are not that fold. He brings them, they listen to his voice, and there is one flock under one shepherd.

The great crowd is that other group: unnumbered, out of every nation, washed in the blood of the Lamb, coming out of the great tribulation. Their place is not the heavenly Mount Zion. It is the earth, in Paradise, under the rule of the Kingdom.

Other sheep are not of this fold. Fold is aule, the enclosure he is already gathering. He must bring the others in. Then there is one poimne, one flock, and one shepherd. One flock is unity under him. It is not a sentence that the other sheep were in the fold all along, or that both groups receive the same inheritance.
AKS says “I have other sheep that are not of this fold.” Not of this fold is kept. One flock and one shepherd come after he brings them in.
Do not be afraid, little flock, for your Father is pleased to give you the kingdom.
This fold is the little flock.

After this I looked and saw a great crowd, which no man was able to number, from every nation and tribe and people and tongue, standing before the throne and before the Lamb. They were wearing white robes and holding palm branches in their hands.
The great crowd no one can number.
“Sir,” I answered, “you know.” So he replied, “These are the ones who have come out of the great tribulation; they have washed their robes and made them white in the blood of the Lamb.
They come out of the great tribulation.
The righteous will inherit the earth and dwell in it forever.
The righteous dwell in the earth forever.
“Sir,” I answered, “you know.” So he replied, “These are the ones who have come out of the great tribulation; they have washed their robes and made them white in the blood of the Lamb.

The great crowd is not a symbol for the 144,000. John has already heard that number. He then sees a crowd he cannot count, from every nation. They come out of the great tribulation. They do not die and wake in heaven as kings.

The Lamb shepherds them, and they hunger and thirst no more. That life is on the earth God formed to be inhabited, the Paradise Jesus promised, the earth the meek inherit. They stand as approved worshipers.
The little flock is the group on Mount Zion with the Lamb, ruling over this earth.

The great crowd is an ochlos no man could number. The elder says these are the ones coming out of the great tribulation. Their robes are washed white in the blood of the Lamb. Coming out means they pass through that tribulation as survivors.
The next lines put them before the throne as worshipers, serving in his naos, his temple, with his tent spread over them. That is protection and approved worship, not a second throne of kings.

AKS says these are the ones who have come out of the great tribulation, and they have washed their robes in the blood of the Lamb. Come out is survival, not a transfer into the sealed group of 144,000.
And I heard the number of those who were sealed, 144,000 from all the tribes of Israel:
The numbered group is stated first.
For this reason, they are before the throne of God and serve Him day and night in His temple; and the One seated on the throne will spread His tabernacle over them.
They serve before the throne, and his tent is over them.
Then I looked and saw the Lamb standing on Mount Zion, and with Him 144,000 who had His name and His Father’s name written on their foreheads.
Mount Zion is where the 144,000 stand, not this crowd.
And Jesus said to him: “Truly I tell you today, you will be with me in Paradise.”
Paradise is the place Jesus promised, and it was not heaven that day.
They will build houses and dwell in them; they will plant vineyards and eat their fruit.
Houses and vineyards on the restored earth.
Then I looked and saw the Lamb standing on Mount Zion, and with Him 144,000 who had His name and His Father’s name written on their foreheads.

This is the little flock in their heavenly place. They carry the name. They are with the Lamb, not standing in the unnumbered crowd of chapter 7. They rule as kings over the earth. Flesh and blood does not inherit that heavenly Kingdom.
They are raised in the first resurrection and reign with him. The earth they rule is not discarded. The great crowd lives on it.

The Lamb stands on Mount Zion, and with him 144,000 who have his name and his Father’s name on their foreheads. Mount Zion in this vision is the heavenly one. Their song is one that only they can learn. A number that is both heard and then seen with the Lamb is not a figure of speech for an uncountable church.
AKS says the Lamb on Mount Zion, and with him 144,000 who had his name and his Father’s name. The number is printed as a number.
You have made them to be a kingdom and priests to serve our God, and they will rule as kings over the earth.”
A kingdom and priests who rule as kings over the earth.
Blessed and holy are those who share in the first resurrection! The second death has no power over them, but they will be priests of God and of Christ and will reign with Him for a thousand years.
The first resurrection. They reign with him.
Now I declare to you, brothers, that flesh and blood cannot inherit the Kingdom of God, nor does the perishable inherit the imperishable.
Flesh and blood cannot inherit the Kingdom of God.
Instead, you have come to Mount Zion, to the city of the living God, the heavenly Jerusalem. You have come to myriads of angels
Mount Zion, the heavenly Jerusalem.

Then He will judge between the nations and arbitrate for many peoples. They will beat their swords into plowshares and their spears into pruning hooks. Nation will no longer take up the sword against nation, nor train anymore for war.

God’s stated future is the end of war between nations. His people do not spend the present learning to kill one another for a flag while they pray for that future. The verse is a promise, and it is also a direction.
The verbs are future and final. Nations beat swords into plowshares and stop learning war. The judge between the nations is Jehovah, not a country.
AKS says nation will no longer take up the sword against nation, nor train anymore for war. Train anymore is the end of military schooling, not a pause between campaigns.
Jesus answered, “My Kingdom is no part of this world; if it were, My servants would fight to prevent My arrest by the Jews. But now My Kingdom is no part of this realm.”
His servants do not fight. The Kingdom is no part of this world.
“Put your sword back in its place,” Jesus said to him. “For all who draw the sword will die by the sword.
Those who draw the sword die by it.
Jesus answered, “My Kingdom is no part of this world; if it were, My servants would fight to prevent My arrest by the Jews. But now My Kingdom is no part of this realm.”

Jesus explains his arrest with a political fact. His Kingdom does not belong to this order of nations, so his people are not its soldiers. Caesar still receives what is Caesar’s, and the governing authorities are still obeyed.
When the order is to kill, this verse has already said his servants do not fight.
No part of this world is the same separation Jesus prays for his disciples. If the Kingdom were part of this world, his servants would fight. They do not. That is the proof he offers Pilate.
AKS says “My Kingdom is no part of this world” and “My servants would fight.” No part of is the phrase used of the disciples in John 17. Fight is the thing his servants do not do.
They are no part of the world, just as I am no part of the world.
They are no part of the world, just as he is.
Everyone must submit himself to the governing authorities, for there is no authority except that which is from God. The authorities that exist have been appointed by God.
They still submit to the governing authorities.
