In the days of those kings, the God of heaven will set up a kingdom that will never be destroyed, nor will it be left to another people. It will shatter all these kingdoms and bring them to an end, but will itself stand forever.

Daniel’s statue is a line of human kingdoms. The stone that strikes it is God’s kingdom, and it replaces them. The earth is what remains for the kingdom to fill. The verse is about rulership changing hands, from men to God, and not returning.
The God of heaven sets up a kingdom in the days of those kings. It shatters the other kingdoms and is not passed to another people. Human empires end. This kingdom does not.
AKS says it will shatter all these kingdoms and bring them to an end, but will itself stand forever. Shatter is the end of those governments, not the end of the earth they stood on.
Let your Kingdom come. Let your will take place, as in heaven, also on earth.
Let your Kingdom come. Let your will take place on earth.
Then the seventh angel sounded his trumpet, and loud voices called out in heaven: “The kingdom of the world has become the kingdom of our Lord and of His Christ, and He will reign forever and ever.”
The kingdom of the world has become the kingdom of our Lord and of his Christ.
But seek first the Kingdom of God and His righteousness, and all these things will be added to you.

Jesus has just taught them to pray for the Kingdom to come and for God’s will to be done on earth. This verse tells them to seek that Kingdom first. It is a government they can put ahead of their own anxiety, not a mood.
First is a priority, not a hobby. The Kingdom and God’s righteousness come before the food and clothing the paragraph has been worrying about.
AKS says seek first the Kingdom of God and His righteousness, and all these things will be added to you. Kingdom is kept as a reign, not changed into a feeling inside the reader.
Let your Kingdom come. Let your will take place, as in heaven, also on earth.
The prayer for the Kingdom and for God’s will on earth.

In the days of those kings, the God of heaven will set up a kingdom that will never be destroyed, nor will it be left to another people. It will shatter all these kingdoms and bring them to an end, but will itself stand forever.
The kingdom God sets up stands forever.
Then the seventh angel sounded his trumpet, and loud voices called out in heaven: “The kingdom of the world has become the kingdom of our Lord and of His Christ, and He will reign forever and ever.”

Heaven announces a transfer. The world’s kingdom becomes the Lord’s and the Christ’s. That fits a Kingdom that comes so God’s will is done on earth. It does not fit a plan in which the earth is thrown away and only a heavenly realm remains.
The kingdom of the world, singular, becomes the kingdom of our Lord and of his Christ. World-rule changes hands. He will reign. The verse does not say the planet is discarded.
AKS says the kingdom of the world has become the kingdom of our Lord and of His Christ, and He will reign forever and ever. Kingdom is rulership. World is the human order that had been ruling.

In the days of those kings, the God of heaven will set up a kingdom that will never be destroyed, nor will it be left to another people. It will shatter all these kingdoms and bring them to an end, but will itself stand forever.
God’s kingdom shatters the human ones and stands.
Let your Kingdom come. Let your will take place, as in heaven, also on earth.
On earth, as in heaven.
Who then is the faithful and discreet slave, whom the master has put in charge of his household servants, to give them their food at the proper time?

Jesus asks who the slave is. The master puts him over the household. The slave does not take the title for himself, and the disciples were just told not to be called leaders. His assigned work is food at the right time, meaning what the household needs in order to keep living.
The verse is about being found doing that when the master comes, not about wearing a rank.

The Greek for slave is doulos, a slave, not a dignified office. Discreet renders the word for sensible, thoughtful judgment. The master does the appointing. The work is to give the household its food at the proper time.

AKS says the faithful and discreet slave, whom the master has put in charge of his household servants, to give them their food at the proper time. Slave is kept. Servant would soften doulos into a volunteer. Discreet keeps the good sense the master is looking for, rather than a vague wise.
Nor are you to be called leaders, for your Leader is one, the Christ.
They are not to be called leaders. Their Leader is the Christ.
And this good news of the Kingdom will be preached in all the inhabited earth for a witness to all the nations, and then the end will come.
The good news of the Kingdom is preached in all the earth before the end.
The righteous will inherit the earth and dwell in it forever.
The hope in this psalm is the earth kept and lived on. Jesus later gives the meek that same inheritance. The great crowd, which no one can number, is who lives that hope after the great tribulation.
A teaching that moves every good person off the earth at death has to erase this line. AKS leaves the address as the earth.
Inherit the earth and dwell in it forever is a permanent home, not a waiting room before heaven. Forever is the duration of the dwelling, and the place is the earth.
AKS says the righteous will inherit the earth and dwell in it forever. Earth is the land, the ground underfoot. Forever is not quietly changed into a long time in heaven.
Happy are the gentle, for they will inherit the earth.
The meek inherit the earth.

For thus says Jehovah, who created the heavens—He is God; He formed the earth and fashioned it; He established it; He did not create it for nothing, but formed it to be inhabited: “I am Jehovah, and there is no one else.
He formed the earth to be inhabited.
And this good news of the Kingdom will be preached in all the inhabited earth for a witness to all the nations, and then the end will come.

Before the end, the Kingdom is announced everywhere as a witness. That work is part of the sign, not an optional extra. The end that follows is the conclusion of the system he was asked about, not the destruction of the earth the meek inherit.
This good news of the Kingdom is preached in all the inhabited earth, for a witness, and then the end comes. The end is tied to the witness being given, not to a secret removal of believers.

AKS says this good news of the Kingdom will be preached in all the inhabited earth for a witness to all the nations, and then the end will come. Kingdom stays a reign. Inhabited earth is the audience. The end is the close he was asked about.

While Jesus was sitting on the Mount of Olives, the disciples came to Him privately. “Tell us,” they said, “when will these things happen, and what will be the sign of Your presence and of the conclusion of the system of things?”
They asked for the sign of his presence and of that conclusion.
Therefore go and make disciples of all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the holy spirit,
Make disciples of all nations.
But when they believed Philip as he preached the good news of the Kingdom of God and the name of Jesus Christ, they were baptized, both men and women.

Baptism here follows belief in the Kingdom and in the name of Jesus. Infants cannot believe that message. The verse names men and women because those are the ones who believed. The commission is to make disciples and then baptize them, in that sense.

They believed Philip as he preached the good news of the Kingdom and the name of Jesus, and then they were baptized, both men and women. Belief and baptism are joined. The subjects are men and women, people able to believe the message.
AKS says when they believed, they were baptized, both men and women. Men and women excludes the idea that the verse is about households of infants. The message believed includes the Kingdom.
Therefore go and make disciples of all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the holy spirit,
Make disciples, baptizing them.
He gave orders to stop the chariot. Then both Philip and the eunuch went down into the water, and Philip baptized him.
A believer goes down into the water.

And He was given dominion, glory, and kingship, that the people of every nation and language should serve Him. His dominion is an everlasting dominion that will not pass away, and His kingdom is one that will never be destroyed.
Rulership, dignity, and a kingdom are given to the son of man. Peoples serve him. His rulership will not pass away.
For to us a child is born, to us a son is given, and the government will be upon His shoulders. And He will be called Wonderful Counselor, Mighty God, Eternal Father, Prince of Peace.
The Prince of Peace receives the rulership on his shoulder. The government is a person who rules, not a feeling in the heart only.

topics.label: Ransom
topics.ask: A corresponding life, given for many

thoughts.text: just as the Son of man did not come to be served, but to serve, and to give his life as a ransom in exchange for many.”

A ransom corresponds to the loss. Adam’s perfect life was lost, and death passed to his children. Jesus gives his life, a corresponding one, for many. The giver is the Son of Man, a man. The one God and the ransom are not the same person spending himself on himself.
Ransom is the price that releases. For many means the price covers more than one, not that the Son was paying himself. He gives his life. The life is the payment.
AKS says the Son of man came to give his life as a ransom in exchange for many. Ransom is the release-price. Life is what he gives. The verse does not say God died.
who gave himself as a corresponding ransom for all—this is to be witnessed to at the proper time.
The corresponding ransom, the fuller Greek word.
For just as through the disobedience of the one man the many were made sinners, so also through the obedience of the one man the many will be made righteous.
Through one man’s obedience the many are made righteous.
who gave himself as a corresponding ransom for all—this is to be witnessed to at the proper time.

There is one God, and one mediator, the man Christ Jesus. The ransom is not God paying himself. It is the man Jesus giving a life that corresponds to what was lost. That is why the mediator is called a man, and why the one God and the mediator are not the same person.
The word appears only here. It joins ransom with a prefix meaning in exchange for, or corresponding to. Jesus’ perfect life answers the perfect life Adam lost.
AKS says he gave himself as a corresponding ransom for all. Where Jesus speaks of a ransom in exchange for many, the simpler word for ransom is used. Here Paul uses the fuller word.
For there is one God, and there is one mediator between God and men, a man, Christ Jesus,
One God, and one mediator, the man Christ Jesus.
just as the Son of man did not come to be served, but to serve, and to give his life as a ransom in exchange for many.”
The simpler word, a ransom for many.
So it is written: “The first man Adam became a living soul”; the last Adam a life-giving spirit.
Adam became a living soul. The last Adam is a life-giving spirit.
For the wages sin pays is death, but the gift God gives is everlasting life by Christ Jesus our Lord.

Sin does not pay a person by keeping him alive to suffer. It pays death. Life that does not end is a gift, and the verse says where that gift is found: by Christ Jesus. An immortal soul would already be drawing wages the verse does not offer.
Wages are what the work pays. The pay for sin is death, not life in another form. The opposite gift is everlasting life, and it comes by Christ Jesus, not from a soul that already had it.
AKS says the wages sin pays is death, but the gift God gives is everlasting life by Christ Jesus our Lord. Death and life are the two outcomes. The life is given through him, not absorbed into him.
Look, every soul belongs to Me; both father and son are Mine. The soul who sins is the one who will die.
The soul who sins will die.
By the sweat of your face you will eat bread until you return to the ground, for out of it you were taken. For dust you are and to dust you will return.”
The sentence on Adam was a return to dust.
That is why, just as through one man sin entered into the world and death through sin, and so death spread to all men because they had all sinned.
The ransom is needed because death is not a private accident. It entered through one man and passed on. A corresponding life answers a lost life.
If death were only bad behavior with no inherited loss, one man’s obedience could not be the answer Paul gives two verses later in the argument’s twin, Romans 5:19.
One man is Adam. Sin entered through him, and death through sin, and death spread to all because all sinned. The verse is about inheritance of death, not about each infant committing Adam’s act.

AKS says death was passed on to all men, because all sinned. Passed on keeps the transmission. All sinned is the result of being in that line, which the next verses explain before the law even existed.
For just as through the disobedience of the one man the many were made sinners, so also through the obedience of the one man the many will be made righteous.
One man’s disobedience, one man’s obedience.
For as in Adam all die, so in union with Christ all will be made alive.
In Adam all die. In union with Christ all will be made alive.
For just as through the disobedience of the one man the many were made sinners, so also through the obedience of the one man the many will be made righteous.

The ransom works as a correspondence. Adam’s act made the many sinners. Christ’s obedience makes the many righteous. Paul calls both of them a man. That is why the mediator can be “a man, Christ Jesus,” and why the payment is a human life given, not the Almighty dying.

The many were made sinners through one man’s disobedience. The many will be made righteous through one man’s obedience. The two men stay distinct. The second is not the God against whom the first rebelled.
AKS says through the disobedience of the one man the many were made sinners, and through the obedience of the one man the many will be made righteous. One man, both times.
For there is one God, and there is one mediator between God and men, a man, Christ Jesus,
One God, and one mediator, a man.
just as the Son of man did not come to be served, but to serve, and to give his life as a ransom in exchange for many.”
His life a ransom for many.
For as in Adam all die, so in union with Christ all will be made alive.

Death is in Adam. Life is in union with Christ, and it is future: they will be made alive. The chapter’s subject is resurrection. The ransom is what makes that rising possible. The dead are not already alive in Christ in some other room. They will be made alive.

In Adam all die is the inherited death. In union with Christ all will be made alive is the reversal, and the next verses put that life at his presence, in an order, not at the moment each person dies.

AKS says “as in Adam all die, so in union with Christ all will be made alive.” In union with is the same phrase AKS uses for the shared life of the Son and the Father. It is not a fusion of the many into Christ.
That is why, just as through one man sin entered into the world and death through sin, and so death spread to all men because they had all sinned.
Death passed on through the one man.
Do not be amazed at this, for the hour is coming in which all those in the memorial tombs will hear his voice
The hour is coming when the dead come out of the graves.
you were bought at a price. Therefore glorify God with your body.

Paul’s moral command sits on a purchase. Someone paid. The reader’s body is not free for sexual misuse because it was bought. The price, read with the ransom verses, is the life Christ gave. Glorifying God with the body is what people do with something that cost that much.

Bought at a price is purchase language. The price is not named in this verse. The surrounding letters name the blood and the life. The body is to be used for God’s glory because it is not the reader’s to spend as if it had no owner.
AKS says you were bought at a price. Therefore glorify God with your body. Price keeps the ransom idea without adding a theory the verse does not spell.
just as the Son of man did not come to be served, but to serve, and to give his life as a ransom in exchange for many.”
The life given as a ransom.
In Him we have redemption through His blood, the forgiveness of our trespasses, according to the riches of His undeserved kindness
Redemption through his blood.
In the same way, after supper He took the cup, saying, “This cup is the new covenant in My blood, which is poured out for you.

The wine means the blood that puts the new covenant into effect. Disciples do not drink blood. They drink wine that Jesus called the covenant in his blood. The pouring out happened at his death. The meal announces that. It does not repeat it.

The covenant itself is the one Jeremiah said Jehovah would make with the house of Israel. In the Christian Scriptures that house is spiritual Israel, the little flock, not every person who later benefits. The great crowd is among the many for whom the blood is poured out.
They are not the fold with whom the cup of the covenant is shared.

The cup is called the new covenant in my blood, poured out. The wine stands for the blood. Drinking a symbol of blood is not the same command as eating blood. The covenant is validated by the blood he pours out, once.
AKS says “This cup is the new covenant in My blood, which is poured out for you.” Cup and blood stay distinct. Poured out is his death, not a weekly offering.
In the same way, after supper He took the cup, saying, “This cup is the new covenant in My blood; do this, as often as you drink it, in remembrance of Me.”
The same cup, in remembrance.
just as the Son of man did not come to be served, but to serve, and to give his life as a ransom in exchange for many.”
The life given as a ransom.
Now since the children have flesh and blood, He too shared in their humanity, so that by His death He might destroy him who holds the power of death, that is, the devil,
He shared blood and flesh in order to bring to nothing the one who has the means to cause death. A spirit could not die that death.

topics.label: Paradise
topics.ask: The great crowd lives on the earth

thoughts.text: The righteous will inherit the earth and dwell in it forever.
The hope in this psalm is the earth kept and lived on. Jesus later gives the meek that same inheritance. The great crowd, which no one can number, is who lives that hope after the great tribulation.
A teaching that moves every good person off the earth at death has to erase this line. AKS leaves the address as the earth.
Inherit the earth and dwell in it forever is a permanent home, not a waiting room before heaven. Forever is the duration of the dwelling, and the place is the earth.
AKS says the righteous will inherit the earth and dwell in it forever. Earth is the land, the ground underfoot. Forever is not quietly changed into a long time in heaven.
Happy are the gentle, for they will inherit the earth.
The meek inherit the earth.

For thus says Jehovah, who created the heavens—He is God; He formed the earth and fashioned it; He established it; He did not create it for nothing, but formed it to be inhabited: “I am Jehovah, and there is no one else.
He formed the earth to be inhabited.
And Jesus said to him: “Truly I tell you today, you will be with me in Paradise.”

Jesus had said he would be killed and raised on the third day. On the day he was raised he said he had not yet ascended to the Father. The criminal could not be with him in Paradise on the day of the execution.

Today belongs with the moment Jesus gave his word, the way solemn promises in the Hebrew Scriptures use today. The Paradise he promised is the restored earth, the home of the great crowd, not heaven that afternoon.
The Greek word for today can stand with the promise or with the day the promise was spoken. The written text had no comma. AKS places the pause after today.
AKS reads, Truly I tell you today, you will be with me in Paradise. The man was not told that he would be in Paradise that same afternoon.
“The Son of man must suffer many things,” He said. “He must be rejected by the elders, chief priests, and scribes, and He must be killed and on the third day be raised to life.”
Jesus said he would be raised on the third day.
“Do not cling to Me,” Jesus said, “for I have not yet ascended to the Father. But go and tell My brothers, ‘I am ascending to My Father and your Father, to My God and your God.’”
After his death he had not yet ascended to the Father.
For the living know that they will die, but the dead know nothing. They have no further reward, because the memory of them is forgotten.
The dead know nothing, so the man was not alive in Paradise that day.

After this I looked and saw a great crowd, which no man was able to number, from every nation and tribe and people and tongue, standing before the throne and before the Lamb. They were wearing white robes and holding palm branches in their hands.

The great crowd comes out of the great tribulation. They survive it. They are not taken to heaven to rule. Their hope is life on the Paradise earth, the earth the meek inherit and the earth where God’s will is to be done.
They are Jesus’ other sheep, one flock with the little flock, but not the same hope and not the parties to the new covenant. Standing before the throne is the language of approved worshipers.
Serving in his temple is the courtyard of worship on earth, not a second group of kings on the heavenly Mount Zion.
John hears 144,000, then looks and sees a great crowd that no man can number, from every nation. The two descriptions are not two ways of saying the same group.
AKS says he saw a great crowd which no man was able to number, out of every nation, standing before the throne and before the Lamb.
And I heard the number of those who were sealed, 144,000 from all the tribes of Israel:
The numbered group is stated first, and it is limited.
I have other sheep that are not of this fold. I must bring them in as well, and they will listen to My voice. Then there will be one flock and one shepherd.
Other sheep, not of this fold.
The righteous will inherit the earth and dwell in it forever.
The righteous dwell on the earth forever.
Let your Kingdom come. Let your will take place, as in heaven, also on earth.
God’s will is to take place on earth.
I have other sheep that are not of this fold. I must bring them in as well, and they will listen to My voice. Then there will be one flock and one shepherd.

The fold Jesus was addressing is the little flock, the ones given the Kingdom and brought into the new covenant. The other sheep are real, and they are not that fold. He brings them, they listen to his voice, and there is one flock under one shepherd.

The great crowd is that other group: unnumbered, out of every nation, washed in the blood of the Lamb, coming out of the great tribulation. Their place is not the heavenly Mount Zion. It is the earth, in Paradise, under the rule of the Kingdom.

Other sheep are not of this fold. Fold is aule, the enclosure he is already gathering. He must bring the others in. Then there is one poimne, one flock, and one shepherd. One flock is unity under him. It is not a sentence that the other sheep were in the fold all along, or that both groups receive the same inheritance.
AKS says “I have other sheep that are not of this fold.” Not of this fold is kept. One flock and one shepherd come after he brings them in.
Do not be afraid, little flock, for your Father is pleased to give you the kingdom.
This fold is the little flock.

After this I looked and saw a great crowd, which no man was able to number, from every nation and tribe and people and tongue, standing before the throne and before the Lamb. They were wearing white robes and holding palm branches in their hands.
The great crowd no one can number.
“Sir,” I answered, “you know.” So he replied, “These are the ones who have come out of the great tribulation; they have washed their robes and made them white in the blood of the Lamb.
They come out of the great tribulation.
The righteous will inherit the earth and dwell in it forever.
The righteous dwell in the earth forever.
“Sir,” I answered, “you know.” So he replied, “These are the ones who have come out of the great tribulation; they have washed their robes and made them white in the blood of the Lamb.

The great crowd is not a symbol for the 144,000. John has already heard that number. He then sees a crowd he cannot count, from every nation. They come out of the great tribulation. They do not die and wake in heaven as kings.

The Lamb shepherds them, and they hunger and thirst no more. That life is on the earth God formed to be inhabited, the Paradise Jesus promised, the earth the meek inherit. They stand as approved worshipers.
The little flock is the group on Mount Zion with the Lamb, ruling over this earth.

The great crowd is an ochlos no man could number. The elder says these are the ones coming out of the great tribulation. Their robes are washed white in the blood of the Lamb. Coming out means they pass through that tribulation as survivors.
The next lines put them before the throne as worshipers, serving in his naos, his temple, with his tent spread over them. That is protection and approved worship, not a second throne of kings.

AKS says these are the ones who have come out of the great tribulation, and they have washed their robes in the blood of the Lamb. Come out is survival, not a transfer into the sealed group of 144,000.
And I heard the number of those who were sealed, 144,000 from all the tribes of Israel:
The numbered group is stated first.
For this reason, they are before the throne of God and serve Him day and night in His temple; and the One seated on the throne will spread His tabernacle over them.
They serve before the throne, and his tent is over them.
Then I looked and saw the Lamb standing on Mount Zion, and with Him 144,000 who had His name and His Father’s name written on their foreheads.
Mount Zion is where the 144,000 stand, not this crowd.
And Jesus said to him: “Truly I tell you today, you will be with me in Paradise.”
Paradise is the place Jesus promised, and it was not heaven that day.
They will build houses and dwell in them; they will plant vineyards and eat their fruit.
Houses and vineyards on the restored earth.
Happy are the gentle, for they will inherit the earth.

Jesus is quoting the hope of Psalm 37. The meek do not inherit a cloud. They inherit the earth. That saying belongs with the prayer that God’s will be done on earth, and with a Paradise promise made to a dying man.

Inherit is a real possession. The earth is the inheritance. Happy, not blessed in a vague sense only, is how AKS opens these lines, matching the earlier note on those conscious of their spiritual need.
AKS says “Happy are the meek, for they will inherit the earth.” Earth is not rendered as the land of heaven.
But the gentle will inherit the earth and delight in abundant prosperity.
The meek inherit the earth and delight in prosperity.
The righteous will inherit the earth and dwell in it forever.
They dwell in it forever.

For thus says Jehovah, who created the heavens—He is God; He formed the earth and fashioned it; He established it; He did not create it for nothing, but formed it to be inhabited: “I am Jehovah, and there is no one else.

The earth is not a disposable stage. Jehovah formed it to be lived on, and he says so while declaring that he alone is God. A future that burns the planet and moves the righteous elsewhere contradicts the purpose stated in this verse.

Empty is the word Genesis uses for the earth before it was ordered. Jehovah says he did not create the earth for that. He formed it to be inhabited. The verse also identifies the maker: I am Jehovah, and there is no other.
AKS says He did not create it to be empty, but formed it to be inhabited. Empty keeps the Genesis word. Inhabited is the purpose. The name Jehovah is printed, not replaced.
God blessed them and said to them, “Be fruitful and multiply, and fill the earth and subdue it; rule over the fish of the sea and the birds of the air and every creature that crawls upon the earth.”
Fill the earth and subdue it.
The righteous will inherit the earth and dwell in it forever.
Dwell in the earth forever.
They will build houses and dwell in them; they will plant vineyards and eat their fruit.

The promise is not a symbol for mansions in a realm without soil. People build, live, plant, and eat. That is the earth as Isaiah pictures God’s restored purpose, and it matches the meek inheriting the earth rather than leaving it.

Houses and vineyards are ordinary earth-life, with the promise that the builders will be the ones who live there and eat the fruit. The context is a new state of God’s people, not a metaphor that erases the houses.
AKS says they will build houses and dwell in them; they will plant vineyards and eat their fruit. Dwell and eat stay physical.

For thus says Jehovah, who created the heavens—He is God; He formed the earth and fashioned it; He established it; He did not create it for nothing, but formed it to be inhabited: “I am Jehovah, and there is no one else.
Formed to be inhabited.
‘He will wipe away every tear from their eyes,’ and there will be no more death or mourning or crying or pain, for the former things have passed away.”
No more death, mourning, crying, or pain.
‘He will wipe away every tear from their eyes,’ and there will be no more death or mourning or crying or pain, for the former things have passed away.”

Revelation 21:3 says the dwelling place of God is with mankind. Then death is gone. Read with the promise that the righteous dwell in the earth forever, this is the earth freed from death, not a funeral for the planet.
The former things pass away. Death, mourning, crying, and pain are named. The previous verse has God dwelling with mankind. The audience of the vision includes a new earth.

AKS says He will wipe away every tear, and there will be no more death or mourning or crying or pain. Death ends. The verse does not relocate the living to a deathless heaven and leave the earth empty.
And I heard a loud voice from the throne saying: “Look, the dwelling place of God is with man, and He will dwell with them. They will be His people, and God Himself will be with them as their God.
God’s dwelling is with mankind.
They will build houses and dwell in them; they will plant vineyards and eat their fruit.
Houses and vineyards, lived in by the planters.
God blessed them and said to them, “Be fruitful and multiply, and fill the earth and subdue it; rule over the fish of the sea and the birds of the air and every creature that crawls upon the earth.”

Eden was the start of a home that was meant to spread. The blessing is still about the earth. Sin interrupted it. The later promises of inheritance, houses, and no more death are that assignment resumed, not a different address.
The first assignment is fruitfulness, filling the earth, and subduing it. The earth is the home they are told to spread through. Nothing in the blessing moves them to heaven.
AKS says be fruitful and multiply, and fill the earth and subdue it. Fill the earth is the purpose. Subdue is care and dominion, not ruin.

For thus says Jehovah, who created the heavens—He is God; He formed the earth and fashioned it; He established it; He did not create it for nothing, but formed it to be inhabited: “I am Jehovah, and there is no one else.
He did not create the earth to be empty.
The righteous will inherit the earth and dwell in it forever.
The righteous dwell in it forever.
The wolf will live with the lamb, and the leopard will lie down with the goat; the calf and young lion and fatling will be together, and a little child will lead them.
The wolf will reside with the lamb. The peace described is on the earth, among the animals of the earth.

topics.label: Last days
topics.ask: The sign of the presence, then the end

thoughts.text: And this good news of the Kingdom will be preached in all the inhabited earth for a witness to all the nations, and then the end will come.

Before the end, the Kingdom is announced everywhere as a witness. That work is part of the sign, not an optional extra. The end that follows is the conclusion of the system he was asked about, not the destruction of the earth the meek inherit.
This good news of the Kingdom is preached in all the inhabited earth, for a witness, and then the end comes. The end is tied to the witness being given, not to a secret removal of believers.

AKS says this good news of the Kingdom will be preached in all the inhabited earth for a witness to all the nations, and then the end will come. Kingdom stays a reign. Inhabited earth is the audience. The end is the close he was asked about.

While Jesus was sitting on the Mount of Olives, the disciples came to Him privately. “Tell us,” they said, “when will these things happen, and what will be the sign of Your presence and of the conclusion of the system of things?”
They asked for the sign of his presence and of that conclusion.
Therefore go and make disciples of all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the holy spirit,
Make disciples of all nations.
But the one who perseveres to the end will be saved.

Jesus is talking about a hard season, and he ties salvation to staying through it. That is the opposite of a teaching that says the outcome is locked the moment a person first believes. The end is still ahead, and the persevering is still required.
Saved here belongs to the one who perseveres to the end. The verb is ongoing. A past moment of belief, with no continuance, is not what the sentence rewards.
AKS says the one who perseveres to the end will be saved. Perseveres is endurance, not a finished transaction that cannot be walked away from.
Therefore, my beloved, just as you have always obeyed, not only in my presence, but now even more in my absence, continue to work out your salvation with fear and trembling.
Work out your salvation with fear and trembling.
As the body without the spirit is dead, so faith without deeds is dead.
Faith without deeds is dead.

While Jesus was sitting on the Mount of Olives, the disciples came to Him privately. “Tell us,” they said, “when will these things happen, and what will be the sign of Your presence and of the conclusion of the system of things?”

The question is double: when, and what is the sign of your presence and of the close of this system. Presence covers a period. Jesus compares the days of Noah to the presence of the Son of man, days in which people ate and drank and did not notice.
A single lightning arrival cannot be those days. AKS keeps presence here so the sign can be a season, and it keeps come where the Greek word is come.

The disciples ask for the sign of his parousia and of the conclusion of the system of things. Parousia is being alongside. Paul uses the same word for his own presence as the opposite of his absence, and for his physical presence in contrast with his letters. It names a stay, not only an arrival.
A different verb, come, appears later in the chapter and in Acts 1:11. Those lines are not this word.

AKS reads “the sign of Your presence and of the conclusion of the system of things.” Presence translates parousia because the word means being alongside, as it does when AKS says Paul’s presence and his physical presence. Coming would hide that. Where the Greek verb is come, AKS says come.
Verse 30 says coming on the clouds. Acts 1:11 says he will come back. Those are not rewritten as presence.
Therefore, my beloved, just as you have always obeyed, not only in my presence, but now even more in my absence, continue to work out your salvation with fear and trembling.
Paul’s presence, set over against his absence. The same Greek word.
For some say, “His letters are weighty and forceful, but his physical presence is unimpressive, and his speaking is of no account.”
His physical presence. The same Greek word.
At that time the sign of the Son of man will appear in heaven, and all the tribes of the earth will mourn. They will see the Son of man coming on the clouds of heaven with power and great glory.
A different word: coming on the clouds. AKS does not force presence onto it.
“Men of Galilee,” they said, “why do you stand here looking into the sky? This same Jesus, who has been taken from you into heaven, will come back in the same way you have seen Him go into heaven.”
He will come back in the same way. That verb is come, and AKS says come.
Nation will rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom. There will be famines and earthquakes in various places.

War, famine, and earthquake are named together. One of them in one century is not the sign. The disciples asked for the sign of a presence and of the close of the system, and Jesus gives a composite. The verse is part of that composite, and he says the end is still later.

Nation against nation and kingdom against kingdom, with famines and earthquakes in various places, is one cluster inside the sign. Jesus has just said these things are not yet the end. They are the beginning of pangs.

AKS says nation will rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom. There will be famines and earthquakes in various places. The list is kept literal. It is not turned into a private spiritual struggle.

While Jesus was sitting on the Mount of Olives, the disciples came to Him privately. “Tell us,” they said, “when will these things happen, and what will be the sign of Your presence and of the conclusion of the system of things?”
The question this answer belongs to.
And this good news of the Kingdom will be preached in all the inhabited earth for a witness to all the nations, and then the end will come.
The preaching comes, and then the end.
But understand this: In the last days terrible times will come.

Paul’s last days are recognized by the kind of people in them: lovers of themselves and of money, without natural affection, and the rest of the list. That list sits beside Jesus’ list of wars, food shortage, and earthquakes.
Together they are a season, which is what a presence allows and a single instant does not.
The last days are a period Paul tells Timothy to understand. Terrible times will come, and the next verses list attitudes, not only armies. The phrase is a season of people, marked by what they love.
AKS says in the last days terrible times will come. Last days is the period. It is not softened into a personal old age.
For men will be lovers of themselves, lovers of money, boastful, arrogant, abusive, disobedient to their parents, ungrateful, unholy,
The attitudes that mark those days.

While Jesus was sitting on the Mount of Olives, the disciples came to Him privately. “Tell us,” they said, “when will these things happen, and what will be the sign of Your presence and of the conclusion of the system of things?”
The presence those days belong to.
Most importantly, you must understand that in the last days scoffers will come, scoffing and following their own evil desires.

Peter expected the last days to include people who laugh at the idea that God will act. Their laughing is not evidence that the promise failed. It is one of the things the last days were said to contain.
Scoffers come in the last days, following their own desires, and the next verse has them asking where the promised presence is. The mockery is part of the period, not a reason to drop the promise.

AKS says in the last days scoffers will come, scoffing and following their own evil desires. Last days matches Paul’s phrase. The scoffing is aimed at the promise, which the chapter goes on to defend.
But understand this: In the last days terrible times will come.
Terrible times in the last days.
But the one who perseveres to the end will be saved.
The one who perseveres to the end is saved.

“At that time Michael, the great prince who stands watch over your people, will rise up. There will be a time of distress, the likes of which will not have occurred from the beginning of nations until that time. But at that time your people—everyone whose name is found written in the book—will be delivered.

Daniel’s protector is not a minor angel. He is the great prince, and he acts at the worst distress. That rank fits the one archangel, the one who commands the angels, the one whose voice is heard when the Lord descends. The people who are delivered are those written in the book.
The verse is about a prince acting for God’s people, not about a second savior beside the Christ.

Michael is the great prince who stands watch over Daniel’s people. He rises up in a time of distress unlike any before it. Prince is a ruler’s title. Standing watch is guardianship. The same Michael is the archangel and the leader of the angels against the dragon.

AKS says Michael, the great prince who stands watch over your people, will rise up. There will be a time of distress. Great prince keeps the rank. Rise up is the action at that distress, the distress Jesus later calls unequaled.
Then a war broke out in heaven: Michael and his angels fought against the dragon, and the dragon and his angels fought back.
Michael commands the angels in the war with the dragon.
But even the archangel Michael, when he disputed with the devil over the body of Moses, did not presume to bring a slanderous charge against him, but said, “Jehovah rebuke you!”
He is the archangel.
All these are the beginning of birth pains.
All these things are a beginning of pangs of distress. The beginning is not the finish.
They will fall by the edge of the sword and be led captive into all the nations. And Jerusalem will be trodden down by the Gentiles, until the times of the Gentiles are fulfilled.
Jerusalem will be trampled until the appointed times of the nations are fulfilled. The times have a limit.

topics.label: Presence
topics.ask: Why parousia is not only a coming

thoughts.text: While Jesus was sitting on the Mount of Olives, the disciples came to Him privately. “Tell us,” they said, “when will these things happen, and what will be the sign of Your presence and of the conclusion of the system of things?”

A different verb, come, appears later in the chapter and in Acts 1:11. Those lines are not this word.

Verse 30 says coming on the clouds. Acts 1:11 says he will come back. Those are not rewritten as presence.

Paul’s presence, set over against his absence. The same Greek word.
For some say, “His letters are weighty and forceful, but his physical presence is unimpressive, and his speaking is of no account.”
His physical presence. The same Greek word.

“Men of Galilee,” they said, “why do you stand here looking into the sky? This same Jesus, who has been taken from you into heaven, will come back in the same way you have seen Him go into heaven.”
He will come back in the same way. That verb is come, and AKS says come.
As it was in the days of Noah, so will it be at the presence of the Son of man.
Just as the days of Noah were, so the presence of the Son of man will be. People were eating and drinking and did not notice.
And they were oblivious until the flood came and swept them all away. So will it be at the presence of the Son of man.
They took no note until the flood came. The presence is a time in which most people do not discern what is happening.
“Where is the promise of His presence?” they will ask. “Ever since our fathers fell asleep, everything continues as it has from the beginning of creation.”
Ridiculers say, Where is this promised presence of his? The word they mock is presence, and they expect a spectacle.
For just as the lightning comes from the east and flashes as far as the west, so will be the presence of the Son of man.
The lightning comes out of the east and shines to the west. The presence is not a hidden private event for one city.

topics.label: Armageddon
topics.ask: God’s war, not the end of the earth

thoughts.text: And they assembled the kings in the place that in Hebrew is called Armageddon.

The only use of the name is this gathering. It is not a local battle near an old town that happens to exhaust the prophecy, because the kings of the entire earth were the ones summoned. It is God’s war.
The promises that the meek inherit the earth still stand after human rulership ends.

Armageddon is a Hebrew place-name in a vision. It occurs once. The gathering of the kings is to that symbolic place for the war just described. A single valley cannot hold every king of the earth, and the verse does not say the planet is what gets destroyed.
AKS says they assembled the kings in the place that in Hebrew is called Armageddon. Hebrew is noted so the name stays a name. Kings are the ones assembled, which matches the war of God’s great day.
These are demonic spirits that perform signs and go out to all the kings of the earth, to assemble them for battle on the great day of God the Almighty.
The battle on the great day of God.
Then I saw heaven standing open, and there before me was a white horse. And its rider is called Faithful and True. With righteousness He judges and wages war.
The rider judges and wages war.
The righteous will inherit the earth and dwell in it forever.
The earth remains the home of the righteous.

In the days of those kings, the God of heaven will set up a kingdom that will never be destroyed, nor will it be left to another people. It will shatter all these kingdoms and bring them to an end, but will itself stand forever.

Daniel’s statue is a line of human kingdoms. The stone that strikes it is God’s kingdom, and it replaces them. The earth is what remains for the kingdom to fill. The verse is about rulership changing hands, from men to God, and not returning.
The God of heaven sets up a kingdom in the days of those kings. It shatters the other kingdoms and is not passed to another people. Human empires end. This kingdom does not.
AKS says it will shatter all these kingdoms and bring them to an end, but will itself stand forever. Shatter is the end of those governments, not the end of the earth they stood on.
Let your Kingdom come. Let your will take place, as in heaven, also on earth.
Let your Kingdom come. Let your will take place on earth.
Then the seventh angel sounded his trumpet, and loud voices called out in heaven: “The kingdom of the world has become the kingdom of our Lord and of His Christ, and He will reign forever and ever.”
The kingdom of the world has become the kingdom of our Lord and of his Christ.
Then the seventh angel sounded his trumpet, and loud voices called out in heaven: “The kingdom of the world has become the kingdom of our Lord and of His Christ, and He will reign forever and ever.”

Heaven announces a transfer. The world’s kingdom becomes the Lord’s and the Christ’s. That fits a Kingdom that comes so God’s will is done on earth. It does not fit a plan in which the earth is thrown away and only a heavenly realm remains.
The kingdom of the world, singular, becomes the kingdom of our Lord and of his Christ. World-rule changes hands. He will reign. The verse does not say the planet is discarded.
AKS says the kingdom of the world has become the kingdom of our Lord and of His Christ, and He will reign forever and ever. Kingdom is rulership. World is the human order that had been ruling.

In the days of those kings, the God of heaven will set up a kingdom that will never be destroyed, nor will it be left to another people. It will shatter all these kingdoms and bring them to an end, but will itself stand forever.
God’s kingdom shatters the human ones and stands.
Let your Kingdom come. Let your will take place, as in heaven, also on earth.
On earth, as in heaven.
These are demonic spirits that perform signs and go out to all the kings of the earth, to assemble them for battle on the great day of God the Almighty.

Armageddon is this gathering, named in the next verse. It is the great day of God, so it is his war against the kings who are assembled, not a human world war that happens to use a Hebrew nickname. The earth is where the kings are. The fighter is God.

Demonic spirits gather the kings of the earth for battle on the great day of God the Almighty. The battle is God’s day, not a war the nations chose as their own project only. Kings are gathered. The next verse will name the place.

AKS says demonic spirits go out to all the kings of the earth, to assemble them for battle on the great day of God the Almighty. Demonic spirits keeps the agents as spirits, not as human diplomats only. Almighty belongs to God, the one fighting.
And they assembled the kings in the place that in Hebrew is called Armageddon.
The place is called Armageddon.

In the days of those kings, the God of heaven will set up a kingdom that will never be destroyed, nor will it be left to another people. It will shatter all these kingdoms and bring them to an end, but will itself stand forever.
God’s kingdom brings human kingdoms to an end.
Then I saw heaven standing open, and there before me was a white horse. And its rider is called Faithful and True. With righteousness He judges and wages war.

Jesus is the one who rides to this war. The kings were gathered by demonic spirits to God’s great day. Here the faithful rider is the one who judges and fights. The earth is not the enemy. The rulership that refused God is.

The rider is called Faithful and True. He judges and wages war in righteousness. The war is his. The chapter goes on to a sword from his mouth and to kings assembled against him. This is the heavenly side of the day Revelation 16 announced.
AKS says its rider is called Faithful and True. With righteousness He judges and wages war. Wages war keeps a real conflict. Righteousness keeps it from being revenge for its own sake.
And they assembled the kings in the place that in Hebrew is called Armageddon.
Armageddon, the gathering.
and to grant relief to you who are oppressed and to us as well. This will take place when the Lord Jesus is revealed from heaven with His mighty angels
The Lord Jesus is revealed from heaven with his mighty angels.
Then I saw the beast and the kings of the earth with their armies assembled to wage war against the One seated on the horse, and against His army.
The kings and their armies are gathered to wage war against the one seated on the horse. It is a war against him, and he wins it.
For the upright will inhabit the land, and the blameless will remain in it;
The upright will reside in the earth. A war of God that wiped the earth away would cancel the promise.

topics.label: Suffering
topics.ask: Why God is not the cause

thoughts.text: When tempted, no one should say, “God is tempting me.” For God cannot be tempted by evil, nor does He tempt anyone.

When suffering is blamed on God, this verse is the first correction. He does not tempt. He is not pushed into evil. The hard things in the world have another source: human sin, inherited death, and the one who rules the world that lies away from God. Jehovah hates what is wicked.
He does not commit it.
Cannot be tempted by evil, and does not tempt anyone, are both denials. James is closing the door on the excuse that God is the source of the trial that becomes sin.
AKS says God cannot be tempted by evil, nor does He tempt anyone. Tempt stays the word. The verse is not rewritten so that God sends moral tests he has just refused.
We know that we are of God, and that the whole world is under the power of the evil one.
The whole world lies in the power of the evil one.
That is why, just as through one man sin entered into the world and death through sin, and so death spread to all men because they had all sinned.
Death passed on from the one man, not as a mood of God.
We know that we are of God, and that the whole world is under the power of the evil one.
Suffering on this scale is what a world looks like when it is under a liar and a murderer. John does not call that arrangement God’s government. God’s purpose for the earth still stands.
This verse says who is dominating the present order, which is why the Kingdom has to replace it.

We are of God, and the whole world is under the evil one. The split explains why a good God and a cruel world can be spoken of in one verse. The world in this sense is the human order under that ruler, not the ground itself.
AKS says the whole world is under the power of the evil one. Under the power keeps a ruler. It does not say the world is identical with him, and it does not say God is the one wielding that power.

You belong to your father, the devil, and you want to carry out his desires. He was a murderer from the beginning, refusing to uphold the truth, because there is no truth in him. When he lies, he speaks his native language, because he is a liar and the father of lies.
He was a murderer and the father of the lie.
The god of this system of things has blinded the minds of unbelievers, so they cannot see the light of the good news of the glory of Christ, who is the image of God.
The god of this system blinds minds.

You belong to your father, the devil, and you want to carry out his desires. He was a murderer from the beginning, refusing to uphold the truth, because there is no truth in him. When he lies, he speaks his native language, because he is a liar and the father of lies.
Jesus does not describe evil as an impersonal force. He describes a liar who murdered from the beginning, the one behind the first lie, you will not die. Death entered by that lie.
The verse is why Satan is treated as a real rebel, not as a cartoon and not as a dark mood inside men only.
The devil is someone’s father in this rebuke, a person with desires, a history from the beginning, and a native language of lying. A mere principle does not have desires or a beginning as a murderer.

AKS says he was a murderer from the beginning, refusing to uphold the truth, because there is no truth in him. When he lies, he speaks his native language. He is a liar and the father of lies. Personhood is left intact.
“You will not surely die,” the serpent told the woman.
The first lie: you will not surely die.
And the great dragon was hurled down—that ancient serpent called the devil and Satan, the deceiver of the whole world. He was hurled to the earth, and his angels with him.
The ancient serpent, the devil, Satan.

And to Adam He said: “Because you have listened to the voice of your wife and have eaten from the tree of which I commanded you not to eat, cursed is the ground because of you; through toil you will eat of it all the days of your life.
The ground is cursed because of the man’s act. Suffering entered through rebellion, not because God designed pain as a gift.
So Satan went out from the presence of Jehovah and infected Job with terrible boils from the soles of his feet to the crown of his head.
The one who strikes Job is Satan. The sores are not Jehovah’s handiwork.

topics.label: Satan
topics.ask: A real rebel, not a mere idea

thoughts.text: You belong to your father, the devil, and you want to carry out his desires. He was a murderer from the beginning, refusing to uphold the truth, because there is no truth in him. When he lies, he speaks his native language, because he is a liar and the father of lies.
Jesus does not describe evil as an impersonal force. He describes a liar who murdered from the beginning, the one behind the first lie, you will not die. Death entered by that lie.
The verse is why Satan is treated as a real rebel, not as a cartoon and not as a dark mood inside men only.
The devil is someone’s father in this rebuke, a person with desires, a history from the beginning, and a native language of lying. A mere principle does not have desires or a beginning as a murderer.

AKS says he was a murderer from the beginning, refusing to uphold the truth, because there is no truth in him. When he lies, he speaks his native language. He is a liar and the father of lies. Personhood is left intact.
“You will not surely die,” the serpent told the woman.
The first lie: you will not surely die.
And the great dragon was hurled down—that ancient serpent called the devil and Satan, the deceiver of the whole world. He was hurled to the earth, and his angels with him.
The ancient serpent, the devil, Satan.
We know that we are of God, and that the whole world is under the power of the evil one.
Suffering on this scale is what a world looks like when it is under a liar and a murderer. John does not call that arrangement God’s government. God’s purpose for the earth still stands.
This verse says who is dominating the present order, which is why the Kingdom has to replace it.

We are of God, and the whole world is under the evil one. The split explains why a good God and a cruel world can be spoken of in one verse. The world in this sense is the human order under that ruler, not the ground itself.
AKS says the whole world is under the power of the evil one. Under the power keeps a ruler. It does not say the world is identical with him, and it does not say God is the one wielding that power.

You belong to your father, the devil, and you want to carry out his desires. He was a murderer from the beginning, refusing to uphold the truth, because there is no truth in him. When he lies, he speaks his native language, because he is a liar and the father of lies.
He was a murderer and the father of the lie.
The god of this system of things has blinded the minds of unbelievers, so they cannot see the light of the good news of the glory of Christ, who is the image of God.
The god of this system blinds minds.
And the great dragon was hurled down—that ancient serpent called the devil and Satan, the deceiver of the whole world. He was hurled to the earth, and his angels with him.

The serpent in Eden, the devil, and Satan are the same one. He has angels. He deceives the whole world. When he is thrown down, the earth is the place of his fury, which is why the world can be under his power while God remains the maker of the earth.

Four names are stacked on one being: the great dragon, the ancient serpent, the devil, and Satan, the deceiver of the whole world. He is hurled down, and his angels with him. Angels mark him as a spirit creature with followers, not a symbol of disease.

AKS says that ancient serpent called the devil and Satan, the deceiver of the whole world. He was hurled to the earth, and his angels with him. The names are kept distinct so the reader can see they are one rebel.

You belong to your father, the devil, and you want to carry out his desires. He was a murderer from the beginning, refusing to uphold the truth, because there is no truth in him. When he lies, he speaks his native language, because he is a liar and the father of lies.
A murderer from the beginning, the father of the lie.
We know that we are of God, and that the whole world is under the power of the evil one.
The world is under the power of the evil one.
The god of this system of things has blinded the minds of unbelievers, so they cannot see the light of the good news of the glory of Christ, who is the image of God.

The verse would be nonsense if the Almighty blinded people to his own good news. The god of this system is the rebel who already rules the world that lies in his power. AKS says system of things so the reader does not think God gave the earth itself to Satan.
The earth remains God’s. The present order is what this god blinds people inside.

A god of this system is a ruler of an age, not the only true God. He blinds minds so they do not see the good news. Paul has already said there is one God, the Father. This god is the other one, small g in the sense of a false god, written here as the god of a system.

AKS says the god of this system of things has blinded the minds of unbelievers. System of things is the age or order, not the planet. God is not capitalized as the Almighty. The true God is the one whose image Christ is.
We know that we are of God, and that the whole world is under the power of the evil one.
The whole world under the evil one.
yet for us there is but one God, the Father, from whom all things came and for whom we exist. And there is but one Lord, Jesus Christ, through whom all things came and through whom we exist.
One God, the Father. This other god is not that one.
Then a war broke out in heaven: Michael and his angels fought against the dragon, and the dragon and his angels fought back.

Michael leads the holy angels against Satan. Jesus is the one to whom angels are subject, and he is revealed with his mighty angels. If those were two commanders, the Bible would be describing two loyal hosts. It describes one.
Michael is the heavenly name of the one who also came as Jesus. The verse still does not contain a sentence that says “Michael, that is, Jesus.” The reader puts the commands side by side.

Michael and his angels fight the dragon and the dragon’s angels. His angels means he commands them. Jesus is also said to come with his angels, and angels are subject to him. Scripture does not describe two loyal angelic armies.
AKS says Michael and his angels fought against the dragon. His angels keeps the command. The dragon is the one the next verses call the devil and Satan.
For the Lord Himself will descend from heaven with a loud command, with the voice of an archangel, and with the trumpet of God, and the dead in Christ will be the first to rise.
An archangel’s voice at the Lord’s descent.
and to grant relief to you who are oppressed and to us as well. This will take place when the Lord Jesus is revealed from heaven with His mighty angels
The Lord Jesus with his mighty angels.
And the great dragon was hurled down—that ancient serpent called the devil and Satan, the deceiver of the whole world. He was hurled to the earth, and his angels with him.
The dragon he fights is Satan.
One day the sons of God came to present themselves before Jehovah, and Satan also came with them.
Satan comes in among the sons of God and answers Jehovah. A conversation requires a person.
The tempter came to Him and said, “If You are the Son of God, tell these stones to become bread.”
The Tempter approaches Jesus and speaks. Jesus answers him. Neither treats the other as an idea.
Be sober-minded and alert. Your adversary the devil prowls around like a roaring lion, seeking someone to devour.
The Devil walks about like a roaring lion, seeking to devour. A warning about a lion is a warning about an enemy.

topics.label: Prayer
topics.ask: To the Father, through the Son

thoughts.text: In that day you will no longer ask Me anything. Most truly I say to you, whatever you ask the Father in My name, He will give you.

Jesus points prayer past himself to the Father, and he attaches his name to the asking. That is the pattern: to the Father, through the Son. Repeating many words, or asking a creature, is not this verse. The giver is the Father.
In that day they will no longer ask Jesus himself. They will ask the Father in his name. The name is the authority by which the request is made. The Father is the giver.
AKS says whatever you ask the Father in My name, He will give you. The Father is asked. The name is Jesus’ name, the means, not a second recipient.
Jesus answered, “I am the way and the truth and the life. No one comes to the Father except through Me.
The way to the Father.
Be anxious for nothing, but in everything, by prayer and petition, with thanksgiving, present your requests to God.
Requests are presented to God.
So then, this is how you should pray: ‘Our Father in the heavens, let your name be sanctified.

Jesus did not teach his disciples to avoid the divine name. He taught them to pray about it first. Replacing the name everywhere with Lord makes this line hollow, because the reader no longer knows which name is being hallowed.
AKS keeps Jehovah in the Hebrew Scriptures so the name in this prayer has someone to point to.
The model prayer opens with the Father’s name, not with a title standing in for a hidden name. A name that must not be spoken cannot be the first petition.
AKS reads “let your name be sanctified.” Sanctified means set apart as holy, which includes knowing whose name it is.
May people know that you, whose name is Jehovah, You alone are the Most High over all the earth.
The name is Jehovah, and he alone is Most High.
I have revealed Your name to those You have given Me out of the world. They were Yours; You gave them to Me, and they have kept Your word.
Jesus revealed the name to his disciples.
Jesus answered, “I am the way and the truth and the life. No one comes to the Father except through Me.

Jesus does not say he is the final address of prayer. He says he is the way to the Father. The model prayer opens with our Father. Asking in Jesus’ name, in the next lines, is asking the Father by means of the Son. Mary is not added as another way. There is one.

The way, the truth, and the life are titles of the Son, and the destination is the Father. No one comes to the Father except through him. Prayer that stops at the Son, or that goes to someone else, misses the address.
AKS says “I am the way and the truth and the life. No one comes to the Father except through Me.” Through me is the route. The Father is the one approached.
So then, this is how you should pray: ‘Our Father in the heavens, let your name be sanctified.
Pray: our Father.
In that day you will no longer ask Me anything. Most truly I say to you, whatever you ask the Father in My name, He will give you.
Ask the Father in Jesus’ name.
Be anxious for nothing, but in everything, by prayer and petition, with thanksgiving, present your requests to God.

The requests go to God. Jesus is the way those requests travel, as he said the same night he taught the disciples to use his name. AKS does not insert other names into the address. One God receives the prayer.

Prayer, petition, and thanksgiving are all aimed at God. Anxiety is answered by asking, not by a ritual address to the dead or to a saint. God here is the Father, the one God Paul has already distinguished from the Lord Jesus.
AKS says by prayer and petition, with thanksgiving, present your requests to God. To God is the direction. Thanksgiving is included, not a show of many words.
When you pray, do not babble on like pagans, for they think that by their many words they will be heard.
Do not babble. Many words are not what gets a hearing.
And this is the confidence that we have before Him: If we ask anything according to His will, He hears us.
Ask according to his will, and he hears.
But a time is coming and has now come when the true worshipers will worship the Father in spirit and in truth, for the Father is seeking such as these to worship Him.

The woman asks which mountain. Jesus says the Father is looking for worshipers in spirit and truth. Worship is not tied to a shrine, an image, or a city. It is aimed at the Father, which is why prayer goes to him through the Son, and why an idol cannot stand in.
True worshipers worship the Father. The place is no longer the mountain or Jerusalem, which is the argument of the conversation. Spirit and truth are the manner. The Father is seeking such people.

AKS says the true worshipers will worship the Father in spirit and in truth, for the Father is seeking such as these to worship Him. The Father is the one worshiped. Spirit is not a call to chase a feeling. Truth is the opposite of a worship built on a tradition he did not ask for.
God is a Spirit, and His worshipers must worship Him in spirit and in truth.”
God is a Spirit. Worship matches what he is.
Jesus answered, “I am the way and the truth and the life. No one comes to the Father except through Me.
The way to the Father.
For there is one God, and there is one mediator between God and men, a man, Christ Jesus,
The one mediator is Christ Jesus. Prayer reaches God through that one man.

topics.label: Memorial
topics.ask: A remembrance, not a repeated sacrifice

thoughts.text: And He took the bread, gave thanks and broke it, and gave it to them, saying, “This is My body, given for you; do this in remembrance of Me.”

Jesus hands them bread on the night of the Passover and tells them to do it as a remembrance. A remembrance points back to a body given once. It is not a priest making the body present again. The emblem is bread. The command is to remember him.

The bread is given with a meaning: this is my body, given for you. Do this is a command to repeat the meal in remembrance. Remembrance is a memorial of a death, not a new sacrifice. The verb is remember, not re-offer.
AKS says “This is My body, given for you; do this in remembrance of Me.” Remembrance keeps the memorial sense. The loaf is not said to turn into flesh.
In the same way, after supper He took the cup, saying, “This cup is the new covenant in My blood, which is poured out for you.
The cup is the new covenant in his blood.
For as often as you eat this bread and drink this cup, you proclaim the Lord’s death until He comes.
You proclaim his death until he comes.
Look, the days are coming, declares Jehovah, when I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah.

The new covenant is real, and it has parties. Jeremiah names the house of Israel and the house of Judah. Hebrews says Jesus mediates that better covenant, founded on better promises, so that those who are called receive the inheritance.

In the Christian Scriptures that house is spiritual Israel: a chosen people, a royal priesthood, a holy nation. That is the little flock. The spirit testifies with their spirit that they are God’s children and heirs with Christ.
The evening meal names the cup as this covenant in his blood. Those in the covenant are the ones who share the bread and the wine. The great crowd is not written into the covenant as a second party.
The blood is still poured out for many, and they receive life on earth under the Kingdom those heirs rule.

The Hebrew is a new berith, a covenant, with the house of Israel and the house of Judah. It replaces the covenant made when he took them by the hand to bring them out of Egypt. Hebrews quotes this promise and calls the later arrangement a new diatheke, with Jesus as its mesites, its mediator.
AKS says Jehovah will make a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah. Covenant is kept. The parties are those two houses, not an unnamed crowd of all who will ever be saved.
Now, however, Jesus has received a much more excellent ministry, just as the covenant He mediates is better and is founded on better promises.
Jesus mediates a better covenant, on better promises.
But God found fault with the people and said: “Look, the days are coming, declares Jehovah, when I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah.
The promise of a new covenant is quoted.

Therefore he is the mediator of a new covenant, so that those who are called may receive the promised eternal inheritance, now that He has died to redeem them from the sins committed under the first covenant.
He is the mediator of a new covenant for those who are called.
In the same way, after supper He took the cup, saying, “This cup is the new covenant in My blood, which is poured out for you.
The cup is the new covenant in his blood.
But you are a chosen people, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, a people for God’s own possession, to proclaim the virtues of Him who called you out of darkness into His marvelous light.
A royal priesthood and a holy nation.
The spirit itself testifies with our spirit that we are God’s children.
The spirit testifies that they are God’s children.
In the same way, after supper He took the cup, saying, “This cup is the new covenant in My blood, which is poured out for you.

The wine means the blood that puts the new covenant into effect. Disciples do not drink blood. They drink wine that Jesus called the covenant in his blood. The pouring out happened at his death. The meal announces that. It does not repeat it.

The covenant itself is the one Jeremiah said Jehovah would make with the house of Israel. In the Christian Scriptures that house is spiritual Israel, the little flock, not every person who later benefits. The great crowd is among the many for whom the blood is poured out.
They are not the fold with whom the cup of the covenant is shared.

The cup is called the new covenant in my blood, poured out. The wine stands for the blood. Drinking a symbol of blood is not the same command as eating blood. The covenant is validated by the blood he pours out, once.
AKS says “This cup is the new covenant in My blood, which is poured out for you.” Cup and blood stay distinct. Poured out is his death, not a weekly offering.
In the same way, after supper He took the cup, saying, “This cup is the new covenant in My blood; do this, as often as you drink it, in remembrance of Me.”
The same cup, in remembrance.
just as the Son of man did not come to be served, but to serve, and to give his life as a ransom in exchange for many.”
The life given as a ransom.
For as often as you eat this bread and drink this cup, you proclaim the Lord’s death until He comes.

Paul’s “as often” is inside the memorial Jesus started, which was a yearly Passover setting, not a command to invent a new schedule. What the verse itself stresses is the meaning: the death is proclaimed, and the proclaiming lasts until he comes.
Bread and cup remain bread and cup. The death is what is announced.

As often as you eat and drink, you proclaim his death until he comes. The meal looks back to a death and forward to a coming. It is an announcement. It ends when he comes. It is not an endless sacrifice.
AKS says as often as you eat this bread and drink this cup, you proclaim the Lord’s death until He comes. Proclaim is announcement. Until he comes gives the meal a finish.
And He took the bread, gave thanks and broke it, and gave it to them, saying, “This is My body, given for you; do this in remembrance of Me.”
Do this in remembrance of me.
He arrested him and put him in prison, handing him over to be guarded by four squads of four soldiers each. Herod intended to bring him out to the people after the Passover.
The season is still called the Passover.
so also Christ was offered once to bear the sins of many; and He will appear a second time, not to bear sin, but to bring salvation to those who eagerly await Him.
Christ was offered once for all time to bear the sins of many. Once is the number.
But when this Priest had offered for all time one sacrifice for sins, He sat down at the right hand of God.
He offered one sacrifice for sins for all time and sat down. A finished sacrifice is not offered again.

topics.label: Baptism
topics.ask: Immersion of a believer

thoughts.text: He gave orders to stop the chariot. Then both Philip and the eunuch went down into the water, and Philip baptized him.

The eunuch sees water and asks what prevents him from being baptized. They go down into it. That is immersion of a believer who has heard the good news, not a rite performed on an infant who cannot ask. Jesus himself came up out of the water when he was baptized.

Both Philip and the eunuch go down into the water, and Philip baptizes him. Baptize is immerse. Going down into the water is what the verb looks like in a narrative. A sprinkle does not require both men to go down into the water.
AKS says both went down into the water, and Philip baptized him. Down into the water is kept. Baptized is not changed into christened or sprinkled.
As soon as Jesus came up out of the water, He saw the heavens breaking open and the spirit descending on Him like a dove.
Jesus came up out of the water.
But when they believed Philip as he preached the good news of the Kingdom of God and the name of Jesus Christ, they were baptized, both men and women.
Men and women who believed were baptized.
Therefore go and make disciples of all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the holy spirit,

The Trinity is sometimes rested on this commission. The line does not say the three are one God. Elsewhere people are baptized in the name of Jesus, and the spirit is what the Father gives. The Father and the Son are persons. The spirit is God’s active force.
One authority over baptism is not a statement that three persons are the same God.
The verse names the Father, the Son, and the holy spirit under one name, that is, one authority. Naming three together does not make them one being, and the holy spirit is not given a personal name.
AKS says disciples are baptized in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the holy spirit. Spirit is not capitalized as a personal title.
Peter replied, “Repent and be baptized, every one of you, in the name of Jesus Christ for the forgiveness of your sins, and you will receive the gift of the holy spirit.
Baptism is also described as in the name of Jesus Christ.
Now the earth was formless and empty, and darkness was over the surface of the deep. And God’s active force was moving over the surface of the waters.
God’s active force, not a third person.
So if you who are evil know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more will your Father in heaven give the holy spirit to those who ask Him!”
The Father gives holy spirit to those who ask.
As soon as Jesus was baptized, He went up out of the water. Suddenly the heavens were opened, and He saw the spirit of God descending like a dove and resting on Him.
At the baptism the reader can count the persons who speak and are seen as persons: Jesus in the water, and the Father whose voice comes from heaven. The spirit is what descends on the Son.
It is compared to a bird, the way Scripture compares God’s power to breath, wind, or something poured out. That picture is not a third Almighty.

The spirit is compared to a dove that descends and rests. A person is not described as arriving and taking a seat beside the Father. The one in the water is Jesus. The voice that follows is the Father’s.
AKS says the spirit of God descending like a dove and resting on Him. Spirit is not capitalized as a personal name. He went up out of the water, which is what immersion looks like.
Now the earth was formless and empty, and darkness was over the surface of the deep. And God’s active force was moving over the surface of the waters.
God’s active force, not a third person.
the spirit of truth. The world cannot receive it, because it neither sees it nor knows it. But you do know it, for it abides with you and will be in you.
The helper is called it.
But when they believed Philip as he preached the good news of the Kingdom of God and the name of Jesus Christ, they were baptized, both men and women.

Baptism here follows belief in the Kingdom and in the name of Jesus. Infants cannot believe that message. The verse names men and women because those are the ones who believed. The commission is to make disciples and then baptize them, in that sense.

They believed Philip as he preached the good news of the Kingdom and the name of Jesus, and then they were baptized, both men and women. Belief and baptism are joined. The subjects are men and women, people able to believe the message.
AKS says when they believed, they were baptized, both men and women. Men and women excludes the idea that the verse is about households of infants. The message believed includes the Kingdom.
