Therefore go and make disciples of all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the holy spirit,
Make disciples, baptizing them.
He gave orders to stop the chariot. Then both Philip and the eunuch went down into the water, and Philip baptized him.
A believer goes down into the water.
Or aren’t you aware that all of us who were baptized into Christ Jesus were baptized into His death?

Paul’s argument needs a baptism that can picture a burial. Going under the water is that picture. The death is Christ’s, the ransom death, and the baptized person is joined to it. A mark on an unknowing infant does not bury anyone into that death.

Baptized into Christ Jesus is baptized into his death. The picture that follows is burial and rising. Immersion fits a burial. The person goes into the water as into a death and comes up to walk in a new life.
AKS says all of us who were baptized into Christ Jesus were baptized into His death. Into his death keeps the burial figure. It is not a washing only of the forehead.
He gave orders to stop the chariot. Then both Philip and the eunuch went down into the water, and Philip baptized him.
Down into the water.
And He took the bread, gave thanks and broke it, and gave it to them, saying, “This is My body, given for you; do this in remembrance of Me.”
The body given, the death baptism points to.
As soon as Jesus came up out of the water, He saw the heavens breaking open and the spirit descending on Him like a dove.

Jesus’ own baptism was in the Jordan, and he came up out of the water. That is the act later commanded for disciples. The spirit descends on him. The Father is the one who speaks in the matching account. Two persons, and the spirit as what comes upon the Son.

Came up out of the water means he had been in it. Immediately the spirit descends like a dove. The baptism of Jesus is the pattern of immersion, and the spirit is again compared to a bird resting, not introduced as a third speaker.
AKS says as soon as Jesus came up out of the water, he saw the heavens breaking open and the spirit descending on Him like a dove. Out of the water is the immersion. Spirit is lowercase.
As soon as Jesus was baptized, He went up out of the water. Suddenly the heavens were opened, and He saw the spirit of God descending like a dove and resting on Him.
He went up out of the water, and the spirit descended like a dove.
He gave orders to stop the chariot. Then both Philip and the eunuch went down into the water, and Philip baptized him.
Philip and the eunuch go down into the water.
As they traveled along the road and came to some water, the eunuch said, “Look, here is water! What is there to prevent me from being baptized?”
The man sees water and asks what prevents him from being baptized. The water is enough to go into.
We were therefore buried with Him through baptism into death, in order that, just as Christ was raised from the dead through the glory of the Father, we too may walk in newness of life.
We were buried with him through our baptism into his death. Burial is a covering, not a sprinkling.

topics.label: Creation
topics.ask: God made the kinds, and the earth to be lived on

thoughts.text: Then God said, “Let the earth bring forth vegetation: seed-bearing plants and fruit trees, each bearing fruit with seed according to its kind.” And it was so.

God tells the earth to bring forth vegetation by kinds, and later the living creatures by kinds. The wording is reproduction within a kind, seed according to its kind. AKS does not translate that as an open process in which every kind is a stage of another.
The maker is still God, speaking.

Kind is the Hebrew grouping, min. Each plant bears fruit with seed according to its kind. The phrase is repeated for animals. The text sorts living things into kinds that reproduce as those kinds. It does not describe one kind turning into another.

AKS says seed-bearing plants and fruit trees, each bearing fruit with seed according to its kind. Kind is kept. Species would pretend the Hebrew word is a modern taxonomic rank. According to its kind is the boundary the verse actually draws.
So God created the great sea creatures and every living thing that moves, with which the waters teemed according to their kinds, and every winged bird after its kind. And God saw that it was good.
Sea creatures and birds, according to their kinds.
In the beginning God created the heavens and the earth.
God created. The kinds are his work.

For thus says Jehovah, who created the heavens—He is God; He formed the earth and fashioned it; He established it; He did not create it for nothing, but formed it to be inhabited: “I am Jehovah, and there is no one else.

The earth is not a disposable stage. Jehovah formed it to be lived on, and he says so while declaring that he alone is God. A future that burns the planet and moves the righteous elsewhere contradicts the purpose stated in this verse.

Empty is the word Genesis uses for the earth before it was ordered. Jehovah says he did not create the earth for that. He formed it to be inhabited. The verse also identifies the maker: I am Jehovah, and there is no other.
AKS says He did not create it to be empty, but formed it to be inhabited. Empty keeps the Genesis word. Inhabited is the purpose. The name Jehovah is printed, not replaced.
God blessed them and said to them, “Be fruitful and multiply, and fill the earth and subdue it; rule over the fish of the sea and the birds of the air and every creature that crawls upon the earth.”
Fill the earth and subdue it.
The righteous will inherit the earth and dwell in it forever.
Dwell in the earth forever.
God blessed them and said to them, “Be fruitful and multiply, and fill the earth and subdue it; rule over the fish of the sea and the birds of the air and every creature that crawls upon the earth.”

Eden was the start of a home that was meant to spread. The blessing is still about the earth. Sin interrupted it. The later promises of inheritance, houses, and no more death are that assignment resumed, not a different address.
The first assignment is fruitfulness, filling the earth, and subduing it. The earth is the home they are told to spread through. Nothing in the blessing moves them to heaven.
AKS says be fruitful and multiply, and fill the earth and subdue it. Fill the earth is the purpose. Subdue is care and dominion, not ruin.

For thus says Jehovah, who created the heavens—He is God; He formed the earth and fashioned it; He established it; He did not create it for nothing, but formed it to be inhabited: “I am Jehovah, and there is no one else.
He did not create the earth to be empty.
The righteous will inherit the earth and dwell in it forever.
The righteous dwell in it forever.
In the beginning God created the heavens and the earth.

The first sentence of Scripture gives the heavens and the earth an origin in God’s act. It does not say the universe assembled itself, and it does not say a committee of gods did the work. One God created. What follows orders that creation by his word.

Created is the verb for bringing into existence. In the beginning marks a start. God is the actor, singular in sense even though the Hebrew word for God can wear a plural shape. The next verse does not introduce a second creator.

AKS says in the beginning God created the heavens and the earth. Created is kept as an act, not as a slow becoming God only watched. God is singular in English because the verb and the sense are one maker.
By faith we understand that the universe was formed at God’s command, so that what is seen was not made out of what was visible.
What is seen was not made out of what was visible.

For thus says Jehovah, who created the heavens—He is God; He formed the earth and fashioned it; He established it; He did not create it for nothing, but formed it to be inhabited: “I am Jehovah, and there is no one else.
He formed the earth to be inhabited.
By faith we understand that the universe was formed at God’s command, so that what is seen was not made out of what was visible.

Faith here is not a guess against the sentence. The sentence says God’s command formed the universe, and the seen did not come from the seen. That is creation by the one who speaks, the same God who said let there be, and who formed the earth to be inhabited.
By faith we understand that the universe was formed at God’s command, so that what is seen was not made out of what was visible. The visible world is not its own parent. The command is God’s.

AKS says the universe was formed at God’s command, so that what is seen was not made out of what was visible. Command keeps a speaker. Not made out of what was visible denies that the present world is only a rearrangement of earlier visible stuff the verse is willing to call the source.
In the beginning God created the heavens and the earth.
In the beginning God created.
“Worthy are You, our Jehovah and God, to receive glory and honor and power, for You created all things; by Your will they exist and were created.”
He created all things, and by his will they exist.
He stretches out the northern sky over empty space, suspending the earth upon nothing;

Job credits God with hanging the earth on nothing. The point for the reader is the maker, not a later science lesson hidden in the poetry. The earth is his, hung by him, and formed to be lived on. It is not an accident and not a god.
Nothing is the empty place the earth is hung upon. The north is stretched over empty space. The line is a maker suspending his work, not a flat disk that needs a pillar.
AKS says he stretches out the northern sky over empty space, suspending the earth upon nothing. Upon nothing is kept. The verse is not padded with a cosmology the Hebrew does not state.

For thus says Jehovah, who created the heavens—He is God; He formed the earth and fashioned it; He established it; He did not create it for nothing, but formed it to be inhabited: “I am Jehovah, and there is no one else.
He established the earth to be inhabited.
In the beginning God created the heavens and the earth.
He created it.
So God created man in His own image; in the image of God He created him; He created them male and female.
God created the man in his image. The man is a creation, made, not a fragment of God.
And God looked upon all that He had made, and indeed, it was very good. And there was evening, and there was morning—the sixth day.
God saw everything he had made and it was very good. The finished earth was good, and it was meant to stay a place of life.

topics.label: The Bible
topics.ask: Inspired of God, not a human project

thoughts.text: All Scripture is inspired of God and beneficial for teaching, for reproving, for setting things straight, for disciplining in righteousness,

Paul does not say Scripture contains some thoughts about God. He says it is inspired of God. That is why it can teach, reprove, set things straight, and discipline. Peter’s line, that men spoke from God as they were moved by holy spirit, is the same claim from the writers’ side.

The Greek word is theopneustos, God and breath in one word, literally God-breathed. AKS does not leave that compound in English. It reads inspired of God, so the reader hears the source, not a vague feeling that the page is stirring.

AKS says all Scripture is inspired of God and beneficial for teaching, for reproving, for setting things straight, for disciplining in righteousness. Inspired of God means God is the source. It does not mean the writing is merely moving.
For prophecy was at no time brought by man’s will, but men spoke from God as they were moved by holy spirit.
Men spoke from God as they were moved by holy spirit.
Sanctify them by means of the truth; your word is truth.
Your word is truth.
For prophecy was at no time brought by man’s will, but men spoke from God as they were moved by holy spirit.
Peter denies that prophecy is a human project. The men spoke, so the books have human writers, languages, and styles. They spoke from God, moved by holy spirit, so the result is inspired of God.
The spirit here is the force that moved them, not another God dictating in his own name.

No prophecy was brought by man’s will. Men spoke from God as they were moved by holy spirit. The will that produced it is God’s. The speakers are men. The spirit is what moved them, which fits spirit as God’s active force rather than a third author sitting beside the Father.

AKS says prophecy was at no time brought by man’s will, but men spoke from God as they were moved by holy spirit. Moved keeps the sense of being carried. Holy spirit is lowercase, God’s power moving the speakers.
All Scripture is inspired of God and beneficial for teaching, for reproving, for setting things straight, for disciplining in righteousness,
All Scripture is inspired of God.
Now the earth was formless and empty, and darkness was over the surface of the deep. And God’s active force was moving over the surface of the waters.
God’s active force at work.
The green grass dries up, the blossom withers, but the word of our God endures forever.”
The word of our God endures forever. Grass withers. The word does not.
The entirety of Your word is truth, and all Your righteous judgments endure forever.
The very essence of your word is truth. The claim is about the word itself.

topics.label: Michael
topics.ask: The archangel and the Lord Jesus

thoughts.text: For the Lord Himself will descend from heaven with a loud command, with the voice of an archangel, and with the trumpet of God, and the dead in Christ will be the first to rise.
The one who descends is the Lord Jesus, and the voice of that descent is an archangel’s voice. There is one archangel in Scripture, Michael. Jesus also has angels subject to him.
The verse does not say the words “Jesus is Michael.” It puts the archangel’s voice with the Lord’s own descent, and the other verses have to be read beside it.

Archangel occurs in the singular. The Lord himself descends with a commanding call, with the voice of an archangel, and with God’s trumpet. The voice belongs to the descent of the Lord. The dead in Christ rise. An archangel is the chief angel, and the Bible never uses the word in the plural.

AKS says the Lord Himself will descend from heaven with a loud command, with the voice of an archangel, and with the trumpet of God, and the dead in Christ will be the first to rise. Voice of an archangel is kept.
It is not changed into a voice like an archangel, which would add a comparison the phrase does not require.
But even the archangel Michael, when he disputed with the devil over the body of Moses, did not presume to bring a slanderous charge against him, but said, “Jehovah rebuke you!”
Michael is the archangel. The word is singular.
Then a war broke out in heaven: Michael and his angels fought against the dragon, and the dragon and his angels fought back.
Michael and his angels.
who has gone into heaven and is at the right hand of God, with angels, authorities, and powers subject to Him.
Angels and powers are subject to Jesus.
But even the archangel Michael, when he disputed with the devil over the body of Moses, did not presume to bring a slanderous charge against him, but said, “Jehovah rebuke you!”

One person is called the archangel, and his name is Michael. He does not act as the Almighty. He asks Jehovah to rebuke the devil. That fits a chief angel who has a God over him. The Lord Jesus descends with an archangel’s voice and also has a God. The titles meet.
They are not two rival commanders of the holy angels.

Michael is called the archangel, with the article in the sense of the chief. He disputes with the devil and does not bring a judgment of his own. He says Jehovah rebuke you. The name in that rebuke is a translation decision: the Hebrew pattern of the angel’s rebuke uses the divine name, as in Zechariah 3:2.

AKS says the archangel Michael said, “Jehovah rebuke you.” Archangel is singular and is Michael’s title. Jehovah is used in the rebuke because that is the divine-name formula of the rebuke, not because every Lord in Jude becomes Jehovah.
For the Lord Himself will descend from heaven with a loud command, with the voice of an archangel, and with the trumpet of God, and the dead in Christ will be the first to rise.
The Lord descends with an archangel’s voice.
And Jehovah said to Satan: “Jehovah rebukes you, Satan! Indeed, Jehovah, who has chosen Jerusalem, rebukes you! Is not this man a firebrand snatched from the fire?”
The rebuke formula: Jehovah rebukes you, Satan.
Then a war broke out in heaven: Michael and his angels fought against the dragon, and the dragon and his angels fought back.

Michael leads the holy angels against Satan. Jesus is the one to whom angels are subject, and he is revealed with his mighty angels. If those were two commanders, the Bible would be describing two loyal hosts. It describes one.
Michael is the heavenly name of the one who also came as Jesus. The verse still does not contain a sentence that says “Michael, that is, Jesus.” The reader puts the commands side by side.

Michael and his angels fight the dragon and the dragon’s angels. His angels means he commands them. Jesus is also said to come with his angels, and angels are subject to him. Scripture does not describe two loyal angelic armies.
AKS says Michael and his angels fought against the dragon. His angels keeps the command. The dragon is the one the next verses call the devil and Satan.
For the Lord Himself will descend from heaven with a loud command, with the voice of an archangel, and with the trumpet of God, and the dead in Christ will be the first to rise.
An archangel’s voice at the Lord’s descent.
and to grant relief to you who are oppressed and to us as well. This will take place when the Lord Jesus is revealed from heaven with His mighty angels
The Lord Jesus with his mighty angels.
And the great dragon was hurled down—that ancient serpent called the devil and Satan, the deceiver of the whole world. He was hurled to the earth, and his angels with him.
The dragon he fights is Satan.

“At that time Michael, the great prince who stands watch over your people, will rise up. There will be a time of distress, the likes of which will not have occurred from the beginning of nations until that time. But at that time your people—everyone whose name is found written in the book—will be delivered.

Daniel’s protector is not a minor angel. He is the great prince, and he acts at the worst distress. That rank fits the one archangel, the one who commands the angels, the one whose voice is heard when the Lord descends. The people who are delivered are those written in the book.
The verse is about a prince acting for God’s people, not about a second savior beside the Christ.

Michael is the great prince who stands watch over Daniel’s people. He rises up in a time of distress unlike any before it. Prince is a ruler’s title. Standing watch is guardianship. The same Michael is the archangel and the leader of the angels against the dragon.

AKS says Michael, the great prince who stands watch over your people, will rise up. There will be a time of distress. Great prince keeps the rank. Rise up is the action at that distress, the distress Jesus later calls unequaled.
Then a war broke out in heaven: Michael and his angels fought against the dragon, and the dragon and his angels fought back.
Michael commands the angels in the war with the dragon.
But even the archangel Michael, when he disputed with the devil over the body of Moses, did not presume to bring a slanderous charge against him, but said, “Jehovah rebuke you!”
He is the archangel.
However, the prince of the kingdom of Persia opposed me for twenty-one days. Then Michael, one of the chief princes, came to help me, for I had been left there with the kings of Persia.
Michael, one of the foremost princes, comes to help. Foremost prince is a rank beside the angel who speaks.

topics.label: Worship
topics.ask: The Father, in spirit and truth

thoughts.text: But a time is coming and has now come when the true worshipers will worship the Father in spirit and in truth, for the Father is seeking such as these to worship Him.

The woman asks which mountain. Jesus says the Father is looking for worshipers in spirit and truth. Worship is not tied to a shrine, an image, or a city. It is aimed at the Father, which is why prayer goes to him through the Son, and why an idol cannot stand in.
True worshipers worship the Father. The place is no longer the mountain or Jerusalem, which is the argument of the conversation. Spirit and truth are the manner. The Father is seeking such people.

AKS says the true worshipers will worship the Father in spirit and in truth, for the Father is seeking such as these to worship Him. The Father is the one worshiped. Spirit is not a call to chase a feeling. Truth is the opposite of a worship built on a tradition he did not ask for.
God is a Spirit, and His worshipers must worship Him in spirit and in truth.”
God is a Spirit. Worship matches what he is.
Jesus answered, “I am the way and the truth and the life. No one comes to the Father except through Me.
The way to the Father.
God is a Spirit, and His worshipers must worship Him in spirit and in truth.”

Jesus has said the Father is seeking worshipers. Then he says why location does not matter. God is a Spirit. You do not worship a spirit by bowing to a carving or by insisting on one mountain. You worship the Father in spirit and truth. The holy spirit remains his active force.
This verse is about what God is, not about a third person replacing the Father.

Pneuma here describes God’s kind of being. He is not flesh that must be approached on one mountain. An indefinite article in English marks a classification: he is spirit in nature. It does not identify God as the holy spirit, the force he sends. The holy spirit is God’s, upon people.
God himself is the Father Jesus has just named.

AKS says “God is a Spirit, and His worshipers must worship Him in spirit and in truth.” A Spirit classifies his nature. Capitalizing Spirit does not install a personal name. Him is the Father. Worship in spirit is worship that fits a God who is not an image and not confined to a place.
But a time is coming and has now come when the true worshipers will worship the Father in spirit and in truth, for the Father is seeking such as these to worship Him.
The Father is the one who is worshiped.
I am Jehovah; that is My name! I will not yield My glory to another or My praise to idols.
He does not give his praise to idols.

On coming to the house, they saw the Child with His mother Mary, and they fell down and did obeisance to Him. Then they opened their treasures and presented Him with gifts of gold and frankincense and myrrh.

The men honor the child with a bow and with gifts. That honor is real. It is not a confession that the child is the Almighty God. Hebrews says God’s angels are told to do obeisance to the Son. Angels are servants. Their bow does not make the Son the God they serve.
Jesus himself tells Satan that worship belongs to Jehovah, and to him alone.

The Greek προσκυνέω (proskyneo) can mean a bow of honor or the worship that belongs to God. The same verb is used of people honoring Jesus, of a king’s court, and of Peter. Context decides which act it is.

AKS reads that the astrologers “fell down and did obeisance” to the child. Obeisance is a deep bow of honor. Worship is reserved for the act that belongs to Jehovah, so the two are not folded into one English word.
And again, when God brings His firstborn into the world, He says: “Let all God’s angels do obeisance to Him.”
God’s angels do obeisance to the Son. The bow is commanded, and they remain angels.
“Away from Me, Satan!” Jesus told him. “For it is written: ‘Worship Jehovah your God and serve Him only.’”
Jesus says worship belongs to Jehovah your God, and him alone.
As Peter was about to enter, Cornelius met him and fell at his feet to do obeisance to him.
Cornelius falls at Peter’s feet, and Peter refuses the honor that does not belong to a man.
“Away from Me, Satan!” Jesus told him. “For it is written: ‘Worship Jehovah your God and serve Him only.’”

This verse quotes Deuteronomy 6:13, where the divine name appears. AKS keeps Jehovah in the quotation so the reader can see who is being spoken of. One Greek verb covers more than one act. A deep bow of honor is obeisance.

The devotion that may be given only to Jehovah is worship. Jesus uses the second when Satan asks to be bowed to as God. Revelation uses worship again when an angel tells John to stop and to worship God.
The distinction is in the English so a reader can see which act the verse is talking about.

Jesus answers Satan with a line from Deuteronomy. The Hebrew passage uses the divine name. The Greek verb in his answer is προσκυνέω (proskyneō), the same verb used when people bow. In this sentence the act is the exclusive honor of God, so the English is worship, not a general bow.

AKS reads “Worship Jehovah your God and serve Him only.” Jehovah is kept because the Hebrew passage being quoted contains the divine name. Worship is kept for this act. The sentence does not say the bow given to Jesus as Son is this same exclusive worship.
Fear Jehovah your God, serve Him only, and take your oaths in His name.
The command Jesus quotes: fear Jehovah and serve him.

On coming to the house, they saw the Child with His mother Mary, and they fell down and did obeisance to Him. Then they opened their treasures and presented Him with gifts of gold and frankincense and myrrh.
The astrologers’ bow to the child is called obeisance, not this exclusive worship.
“Lord, I believe,” he said. And he did obeisance to Jesus.
The man who was healed does obeisance to Jesus after calling him Lord.

So I fell at his feet to worship him. But he told me, “Do not do that! I am a fellow servant with you and your brothers who rely on the testimony of Jesus. Worship God! For the testimony of Jesus is the spirit of prophecy.”
The angel says, Worship God. The worship offered to a fellow servant is refused.
But he said to me, “Do not do that! I am a fellow servant with you and your brothers the prophets, and with those who keep the words of this book. Worship God!”
Do not do that. Worship God. The same refusal is repeated.

topics.label: Life
topics.ask: The unborn is a life in the law

thoughts.text: But if a serious injury results, then you must require a life for a life—

The case is a pregnant woman and her child. A fine covers harm that does not end in injury. A life for a life covers the serious outcome. Jehovah’s law counts that life. Psalm 139 speaks of the unformed body already seen by God.
Taking an unborn life is not outside the command against murder. It is the case this statute already weighs.

Men strike a pregnant woman. If the child is born and there is no further injury, the law is a fine. If a serious injury results, the law is a life for a life. The unborn child is the one in view beside the woman. A fatal injury is treated as the loss of a life, not as the loss of property only.

AKS says if her child is born prematurely, but there is no further injury, the man is fined. If a serious injury results, you must require a life for a life. Born prematurely keeps a birth, not a mistranslation that erases the child into a miscarriage only. Life for a life is the penalty when the injury is fatal.
The child is a life in that law.
If men who are fighting strike a pregnant woman and her child is born prematurely, but there is no further injury, he will surely be fined as the woman’s husband demands and as the court allows.
The pregnant woman and the child, when there is no further injury.
Your eyes saw my unformed body; all my days were written in Your book and ordained for me before one of them came to be.
God saw the unformed body.

For the life of all flesh is its blood. Therefore I have told the Israelites, ‘You must not eat the blood of any living thing, because the life of all flesh is its blood; whoever eats it must be cut off.’

The law gives the reason inside the ban. Blood is the life, so it is not food. Acts 15 repeats abstain from blood for Christians. The verse is about blood as life, not about a menu. It does not, by itself, list every medical fraction of blood. Those limits are not written here.
Life and blood are identified. The prohibition is not a dietary preference. Whoever eats the blood is cut off, because he has eaten the life.
AKS says the life of all flesh is its blood, and you must not eat the blood of any living thing. Life is nephesh, the same word elsewhere rendered soul. Eating blood is eating the life.
You must abstain from food sacrificed to idols, from blood, from the meat of strangled animals, and from sexual immorality. You will do well to avoid these things. Farewell.
Abstain from blood.
Only be sure not to eat the blood, because the blood is the life, and you must not eat the life with the meat.
Do not eat the life with the meat.
Only be sure not to eat the blood, because the blood is the life, and you must not eat the life with the meat.

Moses does not say blood may be eaten if it is a small amount or if the eater is grateful. The life is in the blood, and the life is not food. That is the line behind the later Christian command to abstain from blood.
The sentence equates the blood and the life and then forbids eating the life with the meat. The ban is restated so Israel will not treat blood as a sauce.
AKS says be sure not to eat the blood, because the blood is the life, and you must not eat the life with the meat. Life and blood stay paired.

For the life of all flesh is its blood. Therefore I have told the Israelites, ‘You must not eat the blood of any living thing, because the life of all flesh is its blood; whoever eats it must be cut off.’
The life of the flesh is its blood.
But you must not eat meat with its lifeblood still in it.
The command already given to Noah.
Your eyes saw my unformed body; all my days were written in Your book and ordained for me before one of them came to be.

David speaks of himself before birth as someone God saw. The unformed body is him. That is the same life the law protects when a pregnant woman is struck and a serious injury demands a life for a life. The child is not a blank the adults may discard.
Unformed body is the embryo, not yet finished, and already seen. The days were written before one of them came to be. The person in the womb is the one God is attending to.
AKS says Your eyes saw my unformed body. Unformed body keeps a body that is not yet complete, rather than a thing with no life in view. The speaker is the person who was that unformed body.
But if a serious injury results, then you must require a life for a life—
A serious injury in that case is a life for a life.
Whoever sheds the blood of man, by man his blood will be shed; for in His own image God has made mankind.
Whoever sheds man’s blood, by man his blood will be shed, for God made man in his image.
When Elizabeth heard Mary’s greeting, the baby leaped in her womb, and Elizabeth was filled with the holy spirit.
The infant in Elizabeth leaped. An infant who leaps is a living child, not a part of the mother only.
“Before I formed you in the womb I knew you, and before you were born I set you apart and appointed you as a prophet to the nations.”
Before I formed you in the womb I knew you. The knowing is of a person not yet born.

topics.label: Sin
topics.ask: Missing the mark, and born into it

thoughts.text: for all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God,

Sin is lawlessness, a refusal of God’s standard, and it is also something we are born into. Death passed to all men through one man. A person does not start life clean of that inheritance and then only fail by personal choice. Personal sins are real.
The inherited condition is also real. The wage of sin is death, not a transfer into another kind of life.

The Greek noun ἁμαρτία (hamartia) is built from the idea of missing a mark. It is not a mood and not a private weakness only. The verb form is used of falling short. Romans pairs it with a glory no human reaches.
AKS reads “all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God.” Fall short keeps the picture of a mark that was missed. It does not say some people are born already right with God.
Everyone who practices sin practices lawlessness as well. Indeed, sin is lawlessness.
Sin is lawlessness. The word is a breach of God’s law, not a custom.
That is why, just as through one man sin entered into the world and death through sin, and so death spread to all men because they had all sinned.
Sin entered through one man, and death through sin, and death spread to all.
Surely I was brought forth in wrongdoing; I was sinful when my mother conceived me.
David says he was sinful from the time his mother conceived him. The condition is from the start.
For the wages sin pays is death, but the gift God gives is everlasting life by Christ Jesus our Lord.
The wages of sin is death. The gift is life. The two are not the same thing.
Then after desire has conceived, it gives birth to sin; and sin, when it is full-grown, gives birth to death.
Desire gives birth to sin, and full-grown sin gives birth to death.

topics.label: Faith
topics.ask: Assurance that has to act

thoughts.text: Now faith is the assurance of what we hope for and the certainty of what we do not see.

Faith takes God at his word about things not yet seen, because he has already given reason to trust him. Without it no one can please him. The one who approaches must believe that he exists and that he rewards the one who searches. Faith that never acts is dead.
It comes by hearing the word, not by deciding to feel certain.

The Greek ὑπόστασις (hypostasis) is something that stands under a hope, a basis you can rest on. ἔλεγχος (elenchos) is a proving, a conviction produced by evidence. πίστις (pistis) is that trust. It is not a wish and not a feeling with nothing behind it.
AKS reads “the assurance of what we hope for and the certainty of what we do not see.” Assurance and certainty are stronger than a guess. The verse does not say faith invents what it cannot show.
And without faith it is impossible to please God. For anyone who approaches Him must believe that He exists and that He rewards those who earnestly seek Him.
Without faith it is impossible to please God. He exists, and he rewards the searcher.
As the body without the spirit is dead, so faith without deeds is dead.
Faith without deeds is dead, as a body without breath is dead.
So faith comes from what is heard, and what is heard is through the word about Christ.
Faith comes by hearing, and hearing by the word of Christ.
For God so loved the world that He gave His only-fathered Son, that everyone exercising faith in Him must not perish but have everlasting life.
The promise is for the one exercising faith, not for a feeling that never moves.

topics.label: Angels
topics.ask: Spirits sent to serve, not the dead

thoughts.text: Are not the angels ministering spirits sent to serve those who will inherit salvation?

Angels are created persons, powerful and invisible, made through the Son along with the other invisible things. They carry out God’s word. They are not the dead under another name. Humans who are resurrected will be like the angels in that they no longer die.
That comparison only works if angels are a different kind of creature. An angel who is offered worship refuses it and says to worship God.

The Greek ἄγγελος (angelos) means a messenger. It names a spirit person who is sent. It does not name a dead human. The Hebrew מַלְאָךְ (malak) is the same idea, a messenger, whether the one sent is human or spirit. Context shows which.
AKS reads “ministering spirits sent to serve those who will inherit salvation.” Spirits, sent, to serve. The sentence does not say they were once people, and it does not tell us to pray to them.
Bless Jehovah, all His angels mighty in strength who carry out His word, who hearken to the voice of His command.
His angels are mighty and they carry out his word.

For by means of Him all other things were created in the heavens and on the earth, the things visible and the things invisible, whether thrones or lordships or governments or authorities. All other things have been created through Him and for Him.
The invisible things, thrones and lords included, were created through the Son.
In fact, they can no longer die, because they are like the angels. And since they are sons of the resurrection, they are sons of God.
Those resurrected cannot die anymore, because they are like the angels. Like is a comparison, not an identity.
And I, John, am the one who heard and saw these things. And when I had heard and seen them, I fell down to worship at the feet of the angel who had shown me these things.
John falls before an angel and is told not to. Worship belongs to God.

topics.label: Marriage
topics.ask: One man and one woman, for life

thoughts.text: For this reason a man will leave his father and mother and be united to his wife, and they will become one flesh.

Marriage is God’s arrangement from the beginning, not a later custom. One man leaves his parents and is joined to one woman. What God has yoked, a man is not to pull apart. A wife is bound as long as her husband lives.
The one ground Jesus names for divorce and remarriage is sexual immorality. A husband is to love his wife as his own body. The arrangement is a gift, and it is also a bond.

The Hebrew says a man leaves father and mother and clings to his wife, and they become one flesh. Wife is a woman. Jesus quotes the line and adds that the Creator made them male and female from the beginning. The Greek for the only ground of divorce in his next words is πορνεία (porneia), sexual immorality.
AKS reads “united to his wife, and they will become one flesh.” It does not read partner in a way that leaves the sexes unnamed. Jesus’ exception is sexual immorality, not every unhappiness.
Jesus answered, “Have you not read that from the beginning the Creator ‘made them male and female,’
From the beginning the Creator made them male and female.
So they are no longer two, but one flesh. Therefore what God has joined together, let man not separate.”
They are one flesh. What God joined, man is not to separate.
Now I tell you that whoever divorces his wife, except for sexual immorality, and marries another woman commits adultery.”
Divorce and another marriage is adultery, except for sexual immorality.
A wife is bound to her husband as long as he lives. But if her husband dies, she is free to marry anyone she wishes, as long as he belongs to the Lord.
A wife is bound while her husband lives.
In the same way, husbands ought to love their wives as their own bodies. He who loves his wife loves himself.
A husband loves his wife as his own body.

topics.label: Forgiveness
topics.ask: A debt sent away

thoughts.text: For if you forgive men their trespasses, your heavenly Father will also forgive you.

God forgives the one who confesses and turns around. He is faithful and just when he does it. The release is real. It is not owed to a person who keeps the sin and only wants the feeling of being cleared.

The same God tells his people to forgive one another, the way they have been forgiven. Peter’s question about how many times is answered with a number too large to count out as a limit. A person who will not release a brother is asking to keep a debt God has told him to cancel.

The Greek verb ἀφίημι (aphiemi) means to send away, to let go, to cancel a debt. Forgiveness is a release. It is not a shrug that the wrong never mattered. The same family of words is used when sins are wiped away after repentance.
AKS reads that if you forgive men their trespasses, your heavenly Father will also forgive you. The condition is in the sentence. It is not added by a later teacher.
Repent, then, and turn back, so that your sins may be wiped away and refreshing may come from Jehovah,
Repent and turn back, so that sins may be wiped away.
If we confess our sins, He is faithful and just to forgive us our sins and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.
If we confess, he is faithful to forgive and to cleanse.
Be kind and tenderhearted to one another, forgiving each other just as in Christ God forgave you.
Forgive each other just as God forgave you in Christ.
Then Peter came to Jesus and asked, “Lord, how many times should I forgive my brother who sins against me? Up to seven times?”
Peter asks how many times. The answer is not a small count.

topics.label: Choice
topics.ask: God sets life and death before you

thoughts.text: I call heaven and earth as witnesses against you today that I have set before you life and death, blessing and cursing. Therefore choose life, so that you and your descendants may live,

Jehovah does not tempt anyone, and he takes no pleasure in the death of the wicked. He wants the wicked one to turn and live. He is patient, not wishing for any to perish but for all to come to repentance.

A God who says “choose” is not a God who has already closed the door on the person he is speaking to. People are responsible because the choice is real. Serving him is decided, not inherited as a fate that cannot be refused.

The Hebrew verb for choose is בָּחַר (bachar). Moses tells the nation to choose life. The sentence is a command to people who can take one road or the other. A later Greek word, προορίζω (proorizo), is sometimes read as if every person were locked to heaven or to destruction before birth.
The Scriptures that use a purpose for a group or for the Christ do not erase this command to choose.
AKS reads “choose life, so that you and your offspring may live.” Choose is left as a real act. It is not rewritten as if the outcome had already been assigned to each person.

But if it is unpleasing in your sight to serve Jehovah, then choose for yourselves this day whom you will serve, whether the gods your fathers served beyond the Euphrates, or the gods of the Amorites in whose land you are living. As for me and my house, we will serve Jehovah!”
Choose today whom you will serve. The day of the choice is theirs.
When tempted, no one should say, “God is tempting me.” For God cannot be tempted by evil, nor does He tempt anyone.
God does not tempt anyone. The pull toward evil is not from him.
Do I take any pleasure in the death of the wicked? declares Sovereign Lord Jehovah. Wouldn’t I prefer that he turn from his ways and live?
He takes no pleasure in the death of the wicked. He prefers that the person turn and live.
Jehovah is not slow in keeping His promise as some understand slowness, but is patient with you, not wanting anyone to perish but everyone to come to repentance.
He is patient, not wishing any to perish, but all to come to repentance.

topics.label: The Law
topics.ask: Why Moses’ law is not the Christian rule

thoughts.text: For Christ is the end of the law, to bring righteousness to everyone who believes.

Christians are not under the Law of Moses. Its decrees that stood against us were canceled and taken away, nailed to the stake. We were released from that Law so that we serve in a new way. By calling the covenant new, God made the first one obsolete.
The weekly sabbath, the tithe, the food rules, and circumcision belonged to that covenant. They are not the terms on which a person is declared righteous now. The Law did its work. It led to Christ.

The Greek νόμος (nomos) in this argument is the Law given through Moses. Christ is its τέλος (telos), its end, the point it was leading to. The Law was a guardian until the Christ. A guardian’s work finishes when the heir comes of age. תּוֹרָה (torah) is the Hebrew word for that instruction. It was holy.
It was also a covenant with Israel, not a permanent rule for every nation.

AKS reads “Christ is the end of the law.” End is kept. The line is not softened into “Christ is the goal, so the Law continues as the way of righteousness.” Righteousness here is for the one who believes.
So the law became our guardian to lead us to Christ, that we might be declared righteous by faith.
The Law was a guardian leading to Christ, so that we might be declared righteous by faith.
having canceled the debt ascribed to us in the decrees that stood against us. He took it away, nailing it to the stake!
The decrees against us were canceled and nailed to the stake.
But now, having died to what bound us, we have been released from the law, so that we serve in the new way of the spirit, and not in the old way of the written code.
We were released from the Law and serve in a new way.
By speaking of a new covenant, He has made the first one obsolete; and what is obsolete and aging will soon disappear.
A new covenant makes the first one obsolete.

topics.label: Tongues
topics.ask: Real languages, and then they ceased

thoughts.text: How is it then that each of us hears them in his own native language?

The first occurrence of the gift is the explanation of the gift. Foreigners in Jerusalem recognized their own languages and the mighty things of God being spoken. Tongues were a sign for unbelievers, not a badge for the congregation.

A language no one in the room knows does not teach anyone. The gift was never the mark that a person had God’s spirit, and it was not promised to every believer in every century. Prophecies would cease and tongues would be restrained. What remains is faith, hope, and love.

The Greek γλῶσσα (glossa) means a tongue, and then the language that tongue speaks. On the day the spirit was poured out, each visitor heard in his own native language, a dialect he had grown up with. The gift was speech in real languages, not a private sound no human could share.
Where a congregation did not know the language, the speech did not build them up unless it was interpreted.

AKS says each one heard them “in his own native language.” Native language is a known speech. Later, where AKS says a man “speaks in a tongue” and no one understands him, the problem is the hearers, not a new kind of non-language. Love remains. The gift of tongues was to be restrained.
And they were all filled with the holy spirit and began to speak in other tongues as the spirit enabled them.
They spoke in other tongues as the spirit enabled them. Other tongues are other languages.
Tongues, then, are a sign, not for believers, but for unbelievers. Prophecy, however, is for believers, not for unbelievers.
Tongues are a sign for unbelievers, not a display for believers.
For he who speaks in a tongue does not speak to men, but to God. Indeed, no one understands him; he utters sacred secrets in the spirit.
Speech no one in the congregation understands is not speech to the congregation.
Love never fails. But where there are prophecies, they will cease; where there are tongues, they will be restrained; where there is knowledge, it will be dismissed.
Tongues will be restrained. They are not the permanent mark of worship.

topics.label: Antichrist
topics.ask: Already many, not one future man

thoughts.text: Children, it is the last hour; and just as you have heard that the antichrist is coming, so now many antichrists have appeared. This is how we know it is the last hour.

Antichrist is not a name left empty for a later villain. John says the spirit of the antichrist is already in the world. Anyone who denies the Father and the Son, or who will not confess that Jesus Christ came in the flesh, is included.
False Christs and false prophets are also foretold, and they deceive by signs. The test is the teaching about Jesus, not a headline about one ruler.

The Greek ἀντίχριστος (antichristos) uses a prefix that can mean against, and also instead of. John does not describe one political ruler still to come. He says many antichrists have already appeared, and that this is how the last hour is recognized.
The mark he gives is a teaching: denying that Jesus is the Christ, and refusing to confess that he came in the flesh.
AKS reads “many antichrists have appeared.” Many is in the text. A translation that waits for a single man at the end of history has to ignore the verb John already uses.
Who is the liar, if it is not the one who denies that Jesus is the Christ? This is the antichrist, who denies the Father and the Son.
The antichrist denies that Jesus is the Christ, and denies the Father and the Son.
and every spirit that does not confess Jesus is not from God. This is the spirit of the antichrist, which you have heard is coming and which is already in the world at this time.
Every spirit that does not confess Jesus is the spirit of the antichrist, already in the world.
For many deceivers have gone out into the world, refusing to confess the coming of Jesus Christ in the flesh. Any such person is the deceiver and the antichrist.
The deceiver refuses to confess the coming of Jesus Christ in the flesh.
For false Christs and false prophets will appear and perform great signs and wonders to deceive even the chosen ones, if that were possible.
False Christs and false prophets use signs. The danger is deception, and it is plural.

topics.label: Babylon the Great
topics.ask: Leave false religion

thoughts.text: And on her forehead a mysterious name was written: BABYLON THE GREAT, THE MOTHER OF PROSTITUTES AND OF THE Detestable things OF THE EARTH.

God’s people are told to come out of her, so that they do not share her sins or receive her plagues. Leaving is possible, which means a person can be in her and then not be. She trades in every unclean religious thing and she persecutes.
Isaiah already rejected worship that kept its festivals and still loved wrongdoing. The call is not to reform her. The call is to leave her and to worship the Father in truth.

The name on her forehead is called a mystery, a μυστήριον (mysterion), something that has to be identified rather than read as a street address. She is a prostitute, the mother of the prostitutes, drunk with blood, seated over many waters which are peoples and nations. A literal city can be a harlot in prophecy.
This figure is larger than one capital. She is the world empire of false religion, the mother of its practices.

AKS keeps the name in capitals: BABYLON THE GREAT, THE MOTHER OF PROSTITUTES AND OF THE ABOMINATIONS OF THE EARTH. Mother means she produces others. The title is not a compliment and not a single congregation.
Then I heard another voice from heaven say: “Come out of her, My people, so that you will not share in her sins or contract any of her plagues.
Come out of her, my people, so you do not share her sins.
Then one of the seven angels with the seven bowls came and said to me, “Come, I will show you the punishment of the great prostitute, who sits on many waters.
She sits on many waters. The figure is wider than one city wall.
“Therefore come out from among them and be separate, says Jehovah. Touch no unclean thing, and I will receive you.”
Come out from among them and be separate. Jehovah receives the one who leaves.
Bring your worthless offerings no more; your incense is detestable to Me. New Moons, Sabbaths, and convocations—I cannot endure wrongdoing in a solemn assembly.
Festivals and incense do not hide wrongdoing. Worship he hates is still worship, and it is refused.

topics.label: Prophecy
topics.ask: The end told from the beginning

thoughts.text: From the beginning I foretell the outcome, and from long ago the things that have not yet been done. I say, ‘My decision will stand, and I will do all that I please.’
Isaiah names Cyrus as the shepherd who would have Jerusalem rebuilt and the temple’s foundation laid. Cyrus later did that. Micah names Bethlehem as the town of the ruler whose origin is from of old.

Daniel’s God sets up a kingdom in the days of those kings that will not be passed to another people. The first promise in Eden says the seed of the woman will crush the serpent’s head. Prophecy in these books is specific. It is not a mood about the future.
Jesus said everything written about him in the Law, the Prophets, and the Psalms had to be fulfilled.

The Hebrew נָבִיא (navi) is a prophet, a speaker for God, not a person guessing from the stars. Isaiah 46 says God declares the end from the beginning. The claim can be tested. A name, a town, or a kingdom written down before the event is a different kind of sentence from a poem after the fact.
AKS reads “I declare the end from the beginning, and from ancient times what is still to come.” Still to come is future to the speaker. The verse is a claim that history will confirm.
who says of Cyrus, ‘He is my shepherd, and he will carry out all my will,’ who says of Jerusalem, ‘She will be rebuilt,’ and of the temple, ‘Your foundation will be laid.’
Cyrus is named as the one who would say Jerusalem will be rebuilt.
But you, Bethlehem Ephrathah, who are small among the clans of Judah, out of you will come forth for Me One to be ruler over Israel—One whose origin is from ancient times, from the days of long ago.
Bethlehem is named as the town the ruler comes from.

In the days of those kings, the God of heaven will set up a kingdom that will never be destroyed, nor will it be left to another people. It will shatter all these kingdoms and bring them to an end, but will itself stand forever.
God’s kingdom is set up in the days of those kings and is never destroyed.
And I will put enmity between you and the woman, and between your seed and her seed. He will crush your head, and you will strike his heel.”
The seed of the woman will crush the serpent’s head. The promise is early and specific.
Jesus said to them, “These are the words I spoke to you while I was still with you: Everything must be fulfilled that is written about Me in the Law of Moses, the Prophets, and the Psalms.”
Jesus says the Law, the Prophets, and the Psalms wrote about him, and it had to be fulfilled.

While Jesus was sitting on the Mount of Olives, the disciples came to Him privately. “Tell us,” they said, “when will these things happen, and what will be the sign of Your presence and of the conclusion of the system of things?”

The question on the Mount of Olives ties the sign to Jesus’ presence and to the conclusion of the system of things. AKS’s wording follows the word’s sense of presence so the sign is not reduced to a single flash.
Parousia means being present, not only a moment of arrival. The disciples ask for the sign of that presence.
AKS says “the sign of your presence.” Coming would suggest only an instant. Presence covers the time of his being here in kingdom power.

While Jesus was sitting on the Mount of Olives, the disciples came to Him privately. “Tell us,” they said, “when will these things happen, and what will be the sign of Your presence and of the conclusion of the system of things?”
The disciples ask for the sign in this verse.

topics.label: Flood
topics.ask: A real judgment, eight people

thoughts.text: And every living thing over the earth was destroyed—man and livestock, crawling creatures and birds of the air; they were blotted out from the earth, and only Noah and those with him in the ark remained.

Noah’s day is history. God waited while the ark was built. Eight people were brought safely through the water. Jesus speaks of that time the way he speaks of his own presence: people were eating, drinking, and marrying until the day Noah entered the ark.
He does not treat the flood as a fable used for a lesson. The world that refused the warning was wiped away. The earth itself remained, and life continued through the ones who were spared.

The Hebrew מַבּוּל (mabbul) is the flood, a cataclysm, not a seasonal river rising. Genesis says all the fountains of the great deep burst and the floodgates of the heavens were opened. Everything that had the breath of life on the earth, outside the ark, was blotted out. The wording is global.
A local story does not need an ark the size described, or a promise about all flesh.
AKS says every living thing over the earth was destroyed and blotted out. Over the earth is kept. It is not reduced to a valley.
And look! I will bring floodwaters upon the earth to destroy every creature under the heavens that has the breath of life. Everything on the earth will perish.
The waters are brought to destroy every creature under the heavens that has the breath of life.
In the six hundredth year of Noah’s life, on the seventeenth day of the second month, all the fountains of the great deep burst forth, and the floodgates of the heavens were opened.
The deep burst open and the floodgates of the heavens were opened. Both sources are named.
who disobeyed long ago when God waited patiently in the days of Noah while the ark was being built. In the ark a few people, only eight souls, were saved through water.
Eight souls were brought safely through. The number is small because the refusal was wide.
For in the days before the flood, people were eating and drinking, marrying and giving in marriage, up to the day Noah entered the ark.
Jesus uses the flood as a real day people were living through until the ark was shut.

topics.label: Morals
topics.ask: Sexual conduct belongs in marriage

thoughts.text: Flee from sexual immorality. Every other sin a man can commit is outside his body, but he who sins sexually sins against his own body.

God’s will is that his people be holy and abstain from sexual immorality. The place for sexual union is the marriage of a man and a woman. What is outside that is not a private matter God has declined to mention.
The same letter that names the sins also says people were those things and were washed. The command is to flee, not to manage the desire by giving it a smaller stage. Holiness here is concrete.

The Greek πορνεία (porneia) covers sexual immorality, not only one act. Paul says flee from it. The Hebrew of the Law already forbade a man lying with a man as with a woman, and it forbade adultery. The Christian letter does not relax that.
It says the sexually immoral, adulterers, and men who submit to or perform homosexual acts will not inherit the kingdom.

AKS says “flee from sexual immorality” and, in the verse before, names homosexual acts beside adultery and idolatry. The list is not a suggestion. Marriage is to be honored and the bed kept undefiled.
Marriage should be honored by all and the marriage bed kept undefiled, for God will judge the sexually immoral and adulterers.
Marriage is honored. God judges the sexually immoral and adulterers.
For it is God’s will that you should be holy: You must abstain from sexual immorality;
God’s will is holiness, and that means abstaining from sexual immorality.
You must not lie with a man as with a woman; that is a detestable thing.
A man lying with a man as with a woman is forbidden in the Law, and the Christian letters do not open that door.
Do you not know that the wicked will not inherit the Kingdom of God? Do not be deceived: Neither the sexually immoral, nor idolaters, nor adulterers, nor men who submit to or perform homosexual acts,
Those who practice these things will not inherit the kingdom. The warning says do not be deceived.

topics.label: Love
topics.ask: The mark of a disciple

thoughts.text: By this everyone will know that you are My disciples, if you love one another.”

The first command is to love Jehovah with the whole heart, soul, and mind. Love of neighbor stands with it, and love does no wrong to a neighbor. Love is patient and kind. It does not replace obedience, and it does not cancel justice.
A person who does not love has not known God, because God himself is love. The disciples are identified by that love, not by a title and not by a sign in the sky.

The Greek ἀγάπη (agape) is the love Jesus commands here, a love that acts for the other person. It is the same family of words John uses when he says God is love. The sentence does not say love is God, as if the feeling replaced the person. God is the one who loves.
The Hebrew חֶסֶד (chesed) is loyal love, love that keeps a covenant.
AKS reads “everyone will know that you are my disciples, if you love one another.” The test is visible. It is not a private warmth that never changes how people are treated.
Jesus declared, “‘Love Jehovah your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your mind.’
Love Jehovah your God with all your heart, soul, and mind. That command is first.
Whoever does not love does not know God, because God is love.
The one who does not love has not known God, because God is love.
Love is patient, love is kind. It does not envy, it does not boast, it is not proud.
Love is patient and kind. It is recognized by what it does and by what it refuses.
Love does no wrong to its neighbor. Therefore love is the fulfillment of the law.
Love does no wrong to a neighbor. It fulfills the law’s demand about other people.

topics.label: Preaching
topics.ask: The good news is spoken

thoughts.text: Therefore go and make disciples of all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the holy spirit,

People cannot believe in the one they have not heard of, and they cannot hear without someone preaching. The message Jesus sent his disciples with was that the kingdom of the heavens had drawn near. Paul tells Timothy to preach the word whether the season feels open or not.
The work is public. It is teaching, not a secret kept for people who already agree. Baptism follows the making of a disciple. It does not replace the speaking.

The Greek verb in the commission is to make disciples, μαθητεύσατε (matheteusate). A disciple is a learner who follows. The noun εὐαγγέλιον (euangelion) is the good news, a message with a content. It is not a feeling the believer keeps. Jesus tells them to go, to baptize, and to teach.
The witness runs from Jerusalem to the most distant part of the earth.
AKS reads “go and make disciples of all nations.” Go and make are commands. All nations leaves no people outside the assignment. The preaching of the kingdom is part of the same work.
But you will receive power when the holy spirit comes upon you, and you will be My witnesses in Jerusalem, and in all Judea and Samaria, and to the ends of the earth.”
They will be witnesses in Jerusalem, Judea, Samaria, and to the most distant part of the earth.
How then can they call on the One in whom they have not believed? And how can they believe in the One of whom they have not heard? And how can they hear without someone to preach?
How will they believe in the one they have not heard of? Hearing requires a preacher.
As you go, preach this message: ‘The Kingdom of the heavens is near.’
The message they carry is that the kingdom of the heavens has drawn near.
Preach the word; be prepared in season and out of season; reprove, rebuke, and encourage with every form of patient instruction.
Preach the word in season and out of season.

topics.label: Demons
topics.ask: Wicked spirits, not dead people

thoughts.text: For our struggle is not against flesh and blood, but against the rulers, against the authorities, against the powers of this world’s darkness, and against the spiritual forces of evil in the heavenly realms.

Jesus drove out spirits with a word. The accounts treat the spirits as someone other than the sick person. James says the demons believe there is one God, and they shudder. Belief without obedience is not faith, and their shudder shows they know the one they oppose.
The Law forbade sacrifice to demons, divination, and every attempt to get information from a spirit. The dragon, the original serpent, is the Devil, and his angels are thrown down with him.
A Christian does not consult them, fear them as if they were the dead, or treat them as a myth.

AKS says the struggle is against wicked spirit forces, not against blood and flesh. Spirit forces are real opponents. The verse is not a picture of human institutions only.

topics.label: Messiah
topics.ask: The one the Scriptures named

thoughts.text: Jesus said to them, “These are the words I spoke to you while I was still with you: Everything must be fulfilled that is written about Me in the Law of Moses, the Prophets, and the Psalms.”

Jesus says the three parts of the Hebrew Scriptures wrote about him. Micah had named Bethlehem. Zechariah had said the king would come humble, riding on a donkey. Isaiah had said the servant would be pierced for our sins, and the punishment that brought peace would be on him.

The psalm speaks of hands and feet pierced. Daniel’s count reaches Messiah the Prince and then speaks of him being cut off. The identification is a pile of details, not one vague hope that someone good would appear.

The Hebrew מָשִׁיחַ (mashiach) means anointed one. The Greek χριστός (christos) is the same title, not a family name. An anointed one is appointed, set apart for an office. Daniel counts from the word to restore Jerusalem until Messiah the Prince. The title is a person the books were already describing.

AKS reads that everything written about him in the Law of Moses, the Prophets, and the Psalms had to be fulfilled. About him is specific. The Hebrew Scriptures are treated as a witness to one person, not as a general religious library.
But you, Bethlehem Ephrathah, who are small among the clans of Judah, out of you will come forth for Me One to be ruler over Israel—One whose origin is from ancient times, from the days of long ago.
The ruler comes out of Bethlehem, and his origin is from of old.
Rejoice greatly, O Daughter of Zion! Shout in triumph, O Daughter of Jerusalem! See, your King comes to you, righteous and victorious, humble and riding on a donkey, on a colt, the foal of a donkey.
The king comes to Zion, righteous and humble, riding on a donkey.
But He was pierced for our sins, He was crushed for our wrongdoing; the punishment that brought us peace was upon Him, and by His stripes we are healed.
He is pierced for our sins. The peace is bought by his punishment.
For dogs surround me; a band of evil men encircles me; they have pierced my hands and feet.
The psalm says they pierced his hands and his feet.

Know and understand this: From the issuance of the decree to restore and rebuild Jerusalem until the Messiah, the Prince, there will be seven weeks and sixty-two weeks. It will be rebuilt with streets and a trench, but in times of distress.
From the word to rebuild Jerusalem until Messiah the Prince, the weeks are counted.

topics.label: Giving
topics.ask: Willing gifts, not a required tenth

thoughts.text: Each one should give what he has decided in his heart to give, not out of regret or compulsion. For God loves a cheerful giver.

The tithe was Israel’s law. Malachi’s charge that the nation was robbing God was a charge against people still under that law. Christians were not placed under it. Jesus told the ones he sent to give freely what they had received freely.

Paul tells the elders that it is more blessed to give than to receive, and he points them to work so they can help the weak. Giving is real. The amount is decided by the person, in view of what he has, without a collector standing over a percentage.

The Hebrew מַעֲשֵׂר (maaser) is a tenth. The Law told Israel to set aside a tenth of the produce of the field. That command belongs to the covenant that ended in Christ. The Greek of Paul’s instruction is about a decision in the heart, not a rate. God loves a ἱλαρὸν δότην (hilaron doten), a cheerful giver.
AKS reads “not out of regret or compulsion. For God loves a cheerful giver.” Compulsion is named in order to be refused. A fixed tenth enforced on Christians would be that compulsion.
You must be sure to set aside a tenth of all the produce brought forth each year from your fields.
The tenth is a command about the produce of Israel’s fields.
Will a man rob God? Yet you are robbing Me! But you ask, ‘How do we rob You?’ In tithes and offerings.
The rebuke about tithes is spoken to the nation still under that law.
Heal the sick, raise the dead, cleanse the lepers, drive out demons. Freely you have received; freely give.
Freely you received, freely give. The pattern for the disciples is not a tax.
In everything, I showed you that by this kind of hard work we must help the weak, remembering the words of the Lord Jesus Himself: ‘It is more blessed to give than to receive.’”
It is more blessed to give than to receive. The giving helps the weak.

topics.ask: Why the English reads this way

thoughts.text: In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was a god.

John opens by introducing a person called the Word, already existing in the beginning, beside God, and himself divine. The Word is not a saying or a plan. The title with the article presents someone who can be with God and also be spoken of as godlike.

The next lines continue that distinction: the Word was with God, and through him creation took place. Later John says the Word became flesh. The verse is therefore about identity and origin, not only about a message.
AKS’s “a god” is meant to preserve both truths the Greek holds together: the Word is not the Almighty God he was with, and the Word is not a mere creature without divine status.

The Greek wording is built from en arche (“in the beginning”), ho logos (“the Word,” with the article), the verb en (“was”), pros ton theon (“with the God”), and a closing clause, theos en ho logos, where theos has no article and stands before the verb.

The article on the first theos identifies the one the Word was with. The second theos, without the article in this position, describes a quality of the Word. It does not say the Word is the same person as that God.

AKS reads “the Word was a god.” The indefinite article is required by English, not by a Greek article that is missing. The clause keeps the Word distinct from God, which the verse has already said the Word was with, and it still calls the Word divine.
Other renderings say “divine” or “the Word was God.” AKS does not treat those as the same statement. “God” with a capital, in this sentence, would identify the Word as the God he was with.
He was with God in the beginning.

The Word became flesh and made His dwelling among us. We have seen His glory, the glory of the only-fathered Son from the Father, full of undeserved kindness and truth.
