Parousia means being present, not only a moment of arrival. The disciples ask for the sign of that presence.
AKS says “the sign of your presence.” Coming would suggest only an instant. Presence covers the time of his being here in kingdom power.

While Jesus was sitting on the Mount of Olives, the disciples came to Him privately. “Tell us,” they said, “when will these things happen, and what will be the sign of Your presence and of the conclusion of the system of things?”
The disciples ask for the sign in this verse.
All things came into existence through him, and apart from him not even one thing came into existence.

John has already said the Word was with God. This line says creation happened through him. He is the agent, not the God he was with, and not one of the things that came into existence apart from him. The later letter to the Colossians makes that limit explicit.
The verb describes things coming into existence, not the Word creating himself. He is already present with God in the lines before this one.

AKS says all things came into existence through him, and apart from him not even one thing came into existence. Colossians says the same work with the words all other things, so the Word is not counted among the things made through him.
In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was a god.
The Word was with God before anything is said to have come into existence through him.

For by means of Him all other things were created in the heavens and on the earth, the things visible and the things invisible, whether thrones or lordships or governments or authorities. All other things have been created through Him and for Him.
All other things were created by means of him.
No one has ever seen God. The only-fathered god, who is at the Father's side, is the one who has made Him known.

John has already called the Word a god and said that the Word was with God. This line uses god again for the Son, and it keeps the Father as the God no human has seen. The Son is not a second Almighty. He is the only one who came directly from the Father and then made him known.
The title uses theos, god. The earliest copies read only-begotten god. Some later copies read only-begotten Son. The word only-begotten marks a unique origin, the one produced directly by God.
AKS says the only-begotten god, who is at the Father’s side, is the one who has made God known. No one has seen God. The Son can explain him because he was with him.
In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was a god.
The Word was with God, and the Word was a god.
Now this is everlasting life, that they may know You, the only true God, and Jesus Christ, whom You have sent.
The Father is the only true God, and Jesus is the one he sent.
The Son is the image of the invisible God, the firstborn of all creation.
The Son is the firstborn of all creation.
“Most truly I say to you,” Jesus said, “before Abraham came into existence, I have been.”

The crowd said Jesus was not yet fifty and asked how he had seen Abraham. His answer is about existence before Abraham’s birth. He has just said that the Father is the one who glorifies him, and that the Father is their God. The sentence distinguishes him from that God.

The Greek verb is present in form, but the action started before Abraham came into existence and was still going on. That is why AKS uses I have been. The same verb is rendered I have been when Jesus tells Philip that he has been with them for a long time.
AKS does not turn this sentence into a claim that Jesus is the one who spoke to Moses. It keeps a life that began before Abraham and had not ended.
Jesus answered, “If I glorify Myself, My glory means nothing. The One who glorifies Me is My Father, of whom you say, ‘He is our God.’
The Father, whom they call God, is the one who glorifies Jesus.
Jesus replied, “Philip, I have been with you all this time, and still you do not know Me? Anyone who has seen Me has seen the Father. How can you say, ‘Show us the Father’?
The same verb is rendered I have been with you all this time.
God said to Moses: “I Will Become What I Choose to Become.” And he added: “This is what you are to say to the Israelites, ‘I Will Become has sent me to you.’”
What was spoken to Moses is a different statement, about the one who sent Moses.
And Jesus said to him: “Truly I tell you today, you will be with me in Paradise.”

Jesus had said he would be killed and raised on the third day. On the day he was raised he said he had not yet ascended to the Father. The criminal could not be with him in Paradise on the day of the execution.

Today belongs with the moment Jesus gave his word, the way solemn promises in the Hebrew Scriptures use today. The Paradise he promised is the restored earth, the home of the great crowd, not heaven that afternoon.
The Greek word for today can stand with the promise or with the day the promise was spoken. The written text had no comma. AKS places the pause after today.
AKS reads, Truly I tell you today, you will be with me in Paradise. The man was not told that he would be in Paradise that same afternoon.
“The Son of man must suffer many things,” He said. “He must be rejected by the elders, chief priests, and scribes, and He must be killed and on the third day be raised to life.”
Jesus said he would be raised on the third day.
“Do not cling to Me,” Jesus said, “for I have not yet ascended to the Father. But go and tell My brothers, ‘I am ascending to My Father and your Father, to My God and your God.’”
After his death he had not yet ascended to the Father.
For the living know that they will die, but the dead know nothing. They have no further reward, because the memory of them is forgotten.
The dead know nothing, so the man was not alive in Paradise that day.
who, although he was existing in God’s form, gave no consideration to trying to be equal to God.

Paul is teaching humility. The example is someone who had a high place and did not grasp for a higher one. Equality with God was not his to keep. He emptied himself, became a man, and died on a torture stake. God afterward exalted him.
The order is downward obedience, then a gift of honor from God.

The Greek noun means something to be seized or snatched. It is not a word for holding on to a thing already possessed. If he gave no consideration to seizing equality with God, he was not already that equal.
AKS says that although he was existing in God’s form, he gave no consideration to trying to be equal to God. God’s form means a spirit existence with God, not identity as the Almighty.
More than that, when he came as a man, he humbled himself and became obedient to the point of death, yes, death on a torture stake.
He became obedient as far as death on a torture stake.
For this very reason God exalted him to a superior position and kindly gave him the name that is above every other name,
God exalted him. The higher name was given, not already his as Almighty.
You heard Me say, ‘I am going away, and I am coming back to you.’ If you loved Me, you would rejoice that I am going to the Father, because the Father is greater than I.
Jesus says the Father is greater than he is.
Keep watch over yourselves and the entire flock of which the holy spirit has made you overseers. Be shepherds of the congregation of God, which He purchased with the blood of His own Son.

The overseers shepherd a congregation that God purchased. The price is the blood of his own Son. That keeps the Father as the buyer and the Son as the one who died. The same distinction is in the ransom sayings, where the Son gives his life.

The Greek says through the blood of the own one. It can be read as his own blood or as the blood of his own. The verse has already called the flock God’s. The blood that purchased it is the blood of the Son who belongs to God.
AKS says the congregation of God, which he purchased with the blood of his own Son. It does not say that God himself died.
just as the Son of man did not come to be served, but to serve, and to give his life as a ransom in exchange for many.”
The Son of man gives his life as a ransom.
For God so loved the world that He gave His only-fathered Son, that everyone exercising faith in Him must not perish but have everlasting life.
God gave his only-begotten Son.

For by means of Him all other things were created in the heavens and on the earth, the things visible and the things invisible, whether thrones or lordships or governments or authorities. All other things have been created through Him and for Him.

The Son is the first creation, the agent through whom the rest were made. He is before those other things, and they hold together by means of him. He is also the firstborn from the dead, first of another group.
Firstborn in both places is about being first, not about being the uncreated God.

A bare rendering of the Greek is all things. Left alone, that wording can be heard as if the Son created every thing including himself. The verse before it has already called him the firstborn of all creation.
AKS says by means of him all other things were created, and he is before all other things. Other is required by the context, not by an extra Greek word sitting in the line.
The Son is the image of the invisible God, the firstborn of all creation.
He is the firstborn of all creation.
Also, He is before all other things, and by means of Him all other things were made to exist.
He is before all other things.
All things came into existence through him, and apart from him not even one thing came into existence.
All things came into existence through him.
To the angel of the congregation in Laodicea write: These are the words of the Amen, the faithful and true Witness, the beginning of the creation by God.
He is the beginning of the creation by God.
To the angel of the congregation in Laodicea write: These are the words of the Amen, the faithful and true Witness, the beginning of the creation by God.

Jesus is the Amen, the faithful witness, and the beginning of what God created. That title fits a first creation, not a second Almighty. Proverbs speaks of wisdom produced as the beginning of Jehovah’s way. Colossians calls the Son the firstborn of all creation.
The three lines belong together.
The title is beginning, the start of what God created. AKS does not call him the Originator in the sense of the one who created all things including himself.
AKS reads the beginning of the creation by God. The same person is the firstborn of all creation, and wisdom is described as produced at the start of Jehovah’s way.
The Son is the image of the invisible God, the firstborn of all creation.
The firstborn of all creation.
Jehovah produced me as the beginning of his way, the earliest of his achievements of long ago.
Jehovah produced wisdom as the beginning of his way.
In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was a god.
The Word was with God in the beginning.
Jehovah produced me as the beginning of his way, the earliest of his achievements of long ago.

Wisdom was there before the rest of Jehovah’s works because Jehovah produced wisdom first. That is the same pattern as a Son who is the beginning of the creation by God and the agent of what came after. The speaker is not the everlasting God. Jehovah is the one who produced him.
The Hebrew verb is one the Scriptures also use when a person is brought into existence. Wisdom is speaking as someone Jehovah produced, not as Jehovah himself.
AKS says Jehovah produced me as the beginning of his way, the earliest of his achievements of long ago. Produced replaces a vague first course. The line is about origin.
To the angel of the congregation in Laodicea write: These are the words of the Amen, the faithful and true Witness, the beginning of the creation by God.
The beginning of the creation by God.
The Son is the image of the invisible God, the firstborn of all creation.
The firstborn of all creation.
God said to Moses: “I Will Become What I Choose to Become.” And he added: “This is what you are to say to the Israelites, ‘I Will Become has sent me to you.’”

Moses asked what he should say when Israel asked for the name of the God of their fathers. The answer is first a statement about what God will become toward them, and then the personal name by which he is to be remembered. The verb and the name belong together.
One describes his activity. The other identifies him.
The Hebrew expression is a verb of becoming, spoken as something God will be or will prove to be. It is not a static I am. AKS also allows the sense I Will Prove to Be What I Will Prove to Be.
AKS reads I Will Become What I Choose to Become, and then I Will Become has sent me to you. The memorial name in the next verse is Jehovah.

God also told Moses, “Say to the Israelites, ‘Jehovah, the God of your fathers—the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob—has sent me to you.’ This is My name forever, and this is how I am to be remembered in every generation.
Jehovah is the name to be remembered for all generations.
“Happy are those conscious of their spiritual need, for theirs is the Kingdom of the heavens.
The same word describes the beggar Lazarus. Here it describes people who know their spiritual poverty and look to God. The Kingdom belongs to them because they know they cannot supply themselves.
The next happiness in this sermon promises the meek that they will inherit the earth.
The Greek word is the one used of a beggar, a person who knows he has nothing. With spirit, it is not a compliment for being empty of life. It is the painful awareness of needing God.
AKS says Happy are those conscious of their spiritual need, for the Kingdom of the heavens belongs to them. Poor in spirit would hide the need.
Happy are the gentle, for they will inherit the earth.
The meek inherit the earth.
And a beggar named Lazarus lay at his gate, covered with sores
The same word for poor is used of the beggar.
who gave himself as a corresponding ransom for all—this is to be witnessed to at the proper time.

There is one God, and one mediator, the man Christ Jesus. The ransom is not God paying himself. It is the man Jesus giving a life that corresponds to what was lost. That is why the mediator is called a man, and why the one God and the mediator are not the same person.
The word appears only here. It joins ransom with a prefix meaning in exchange for, or corresponding to. Jesus’ perfect life answers the perfect life Adam lost.
AKS says he gave himself as a corresponding ransom for all. Where Jesus speaks of a ransom in exchange for many, the simpler word for ransom is used. Here Paul uses the fuller word.
For there is one God, and there is one mediator between God and men, a man, Christ Jesus,
One God, and one mediator, the man Christ Jesus.
just as the Son of man did not come to be served, but to serve, and to give his life as a ransom in exchange for many.”
The simpler word, a ransom for many.
So it is written: “The first man Adam became a living soul”; the last Adam a life-giving spirit.
Adam became a living soul. The last Adam is a life-giving spirit.

And we know that the Son of God has come, and he has given us understanding so that we may know the one who is true. And we are in union with the one who is true by means of his Son, Jesus Christ. This is the true God and everlasting life.

An earlier wording could be heard as if the Son were the true God. The line does the opposite. The Son came to make the true one known. Jesus himself called the Father the only true God. This verse agrees with that.

The sentence names the Son, then the one who is true, then says we are in union with that one by means of his Son. This is the true God points back to the one who is true, not to the Son who is the means.
AKS says the Son has given us understanding so that we may know the one who is true, and that we are in union with the one who is true by means of his Son. This is the true God and everlasting life.
Now this is everlasting life, that they may know You, the only true God, and Jesus Christ, whom You have sent.
The Father is the only true God, and Jesus is the one he sent.
But about the Son he says: “God is your throne forever and ever, and the scepter of your kingdom is the scepter of uprightness.”

The psalm was first spoken to a human king whom God appointed. As a prophecy it points to the Messiah, whom God also appoints. Calling the Son God in the sense of addressing the Almighty would ignore the next breath, where his God anoints him above his companions.
The Greek can be read as your throne, O God, or as God is your throne. The next line says God, your God, anointed you. The one addressed has a God. He is not the Almighty.
AKS reads God is your throne forever and ever. Jehovah is the source of the Son’s royal authority. The same decision is used in the psalm being quoted.
You have loved righteousness and hated wickedness; therefore God, Your God, has anointed You above Your companions with the oil of joy.”
God, your God, anointed you.
God is your throne forever and ever, and justice is the scepter of your kingdom.
The psalm says God is your throne.
He will be great and will be called the Son of the Most High. Jehovah God will give Him the throne of His father David,
The throne is given by God.
And these will go away into everlasting cutting-off, but the righteous into everlasting life.

The goats go to a cutting-off from which there is no resurrection. The sheep receive life that does not end. The verse is not a picture of an immortal soul suffering forever. Death is the loss. Life is the gift.
The Greek word is used of pruning, cutting off what is taken away. It is not a word for keeping a person alive in pain. Everlasting describes the result. The person is cut off from life.
AKS says everlasting cutting-off, and everlasting life for the righteous. The two outcomes are opposites. One ends life. The other continues it.
For God so loved the world that He gave His only-fathered Son, that everyone exercising faith in Him must not perish but have everlasting life.
The alternative to perishing is everlasting life.
For the wages sin pays is death, but the gift God gives is everlasting life by Christ Jesus our Lord.
The wages of sin is death. The gift is everlasting life.
Now the earth was formless and empty, and darkness was over the surface of the deep. And God’s active force was moving over the surface of the waters.

Scripture speaks of this spirit as God’s breath, his hands, or his fingers, and compares it to water poured out. A craftsman’s hands do not act apart from him. Stephen, full of holy spirit, saw God’s glory and Jesus at God’s right hand, two persons, not three.
The spirit has no personal name.
The Hebrew word can mean breath, wind, or spirit. Here it is God’s own force at work over the waters, not a third person beside him.
AKS says God’s active force was moving over the surface of the waters. Spirit remains a true sense of the word. Person is not.
So if you who are evil know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more will your Father in heaven give the holy spirit to those who ask Him!”
The Father gives holy spirit to those who ask.
But Stephen, full of the holy spirit, looked intently into heaven and saw the glory of God and Jesus standing at the right hand of God.
Stephen saw God and Jesus, not a third person.

“The spirit of Jehovah is on Me, because He has anointed Me to preach good news to the poor. He has sent Me to proclaim liberty to the captives and recovery of sight to the blind, to release the oppressed,
The spirit of Jehovah is Jehovah’s power on the one he sends.
It was now the third hour, and they nailed him to the stake.

The accounts are not two clocks in contradiction. One can include the start of the execution, including the whipping. The other can mark when he was nailed to the stake. Both round the hour. AKS uses stake for the instrument they nailed him to.
The third hour is about nine in the morning, counting from sunrise in three-hour parts of the day. Writers often gave the time in those blocks, so the hour can be approximate.

AKS says it was now the third hour, and they nailed him to the stake. John speaks of about the sixth hour when Pilate handed him over. Scourging was part of the execution and could stand between the sentence and the nailing.
Carrying His own stake, He went out to The Place of the Skull, which in Hebrew is called Golgotha.
He went out carrying his own stake.
More than that, when he came as a man, he humbled himself and became obedient to the point of death, yes, death on a torture stake.
Death on a torture stake.
“We are not stoning you for a fine work,” the Jews answered, “but for blasphemy, because you, although being a man, make yourself a god.”

The crowd’s accusation is not that Jesus said “I and the Father are the same person.” They heard a man speaking as a god. Jesus answers from Psalm 82, where human judges are called gods, and then says the Father sanctified him and sent him.
His own words for the claim are “I am God’s Son.” The verse distinguishes a god from the God who sent him.
The Greek theos here has no article. In this sentence it is “a god,” not “the God,” the Father. Capitalizing God turns the charge into a claim Jesus did not make.
AKS reads that they wanted to stone him because he, although a man, made himself a god. It does not say he made himself God.
I and the Father are one.”
The line that prompted the charge.
then what about the One whom the Father made holy and sent into the world? How then can you accuse Me of blasphemy for stating that I am God’s Son?
He identifies the claim as “I am God’s Son.”
In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was a god.
The Word was a god, and the Word was with God.
I have said, ‘You are gods; you are all sons of the Most High.’
The scripture he quotes, where men are called gods.
For there are three that testify:

A line that sounds like a definition of the Trinity was written into some later manuscripts of this letter and then into older English Bibles. It is not part of the letter. AKS follows the text that does not contain it.
Nothing in the real sentence says the Father, the Son, and the spirit are one God. The witnesses agree. Witnesses that agree are not one person.

Some later copies insert a sentence about the Father, the Word, and the holy spirit, and about those three being one. Those words are not in the early text. The three that testify in this passage are the spirit, the water, and the blood.
AKS reads “there are three that testify,” and the next verse names the spirit, the water, and the blood. It does not print a Trinity formula here.
the spirit, the water, and the blood—and these three are in agreement.
The three are the spirit, the water, and the blood.
Now this is everlasting life, that they may know You, the only true God, and Jesus Christ, whom You have sent.
The only true God is the Father.
Along the way they found a man from Cyrene, named Simon, and they forced him to carry the stake of Jesus.

Simon of Cyrene carries the instrument Jesus had been carrying. The accounts call it the same thing they later nail him to. AKS keeps stake so the reader does not import a shaped symbol the Greek noun does not specify.

The Greek word is stauros, a stake or upright pole. The verse says Simon was forced to carry it. The instrument is something one man can carry, and AKS does not turn the word into the later church emblem.
AKS says they forced him to carry the stake of Jesus. Stake translates stauros. Cross would decide a shape the word itself does not draw.
Carrying His own stake, He went out to The Place of the Skull, which in Hebrew is called Golgotha.
He went out carrying his own stake.
If a man has committed a sin worthy of death, and he is executed, and you hang his body on a stake,
The law speaks of a body hung on a stake.
Carrying His own stake, He went out to The Place of the Skull, which in Hebrew is called Golgotha.

John and Matthew are describing one walk to the same place. One moment he carries it. Later Simon is compelled to carry it. Both verses use the word AKS renders stake. The place-name is given in Hebrew so the reader can see this is a report, not a symbol being explained.
He carried it, and the place has a Hebrew name, Golgotha. The instrument is stauros again. AKS does not add a crossbeam the sentence does not mention.
AKS says “Carrying His own stake, He went out.” Stake is the same decision as in the other accounts of the execution.
Along the way they found a man from Cyrene, named Simon, and they forced him to carry the stake of Jesus.
Simon is forced to carry the same stake.
Christ redeemed us from the curse of the law by becoming a curse for us. For it is written: “Cursed is everyone who is hung on a stake.”
The curse is on the one hung on a stake.
The God of our fathers raised up Jesus, whom you had killed by hanging Him on a stake.

Peter’s charge to the court uses the language of the curse text. The Greek can be heard as wood or tree. AKS chooses stake because that is how the law being echoed is rendered, and because the execution accounts use stauros for the same death.
One English word keeps the law and the event together.

The phrase is hanging him on a tree or a timber, the word also used for wood. Peter is echoing the law in Deuteronomy about the one whose body is hung on a stake. AKS follows that Hebrew law’s word rather than a later emblem.
AKS says you killed him by hanging Him on a stake. It does not say tree, and it does not say cross. The matching law in Deuteronomy 21:22 uses stake.
If a man has committed a sin worthy of death, and he is executed, and you hang his body on a stake,
The law: hang his body on a stake.
Christ redeemed us from the curse of the law by becoming a curse for us. For it is written: “Cursed is everyone who is hung on a stake.”
Paul quotes that curse.
If a man has committed a sin worthy of death, and he is executed, and you hang his body on a stake,

This is the law Paul quotes when he says the one hung on a stake is under a curse. If this verse said tree and Galatians said stake, the quotation would look broken. AKS uses stake in both so the reader can see they are one statute.
The Hebrew word is the ordinary word for a tree or a piece of timber set up so a body can be hung on it. It is not the name of a shaped religious symbol.
AKS says you hang his body on a stake. Stake keeps the legal instrument. Tree would be possible English and is not used here, so the later quotations can say stake as well.
Christ redeemed us from the curse of the law by becoming a curse for us. For it is written: “Cursed is everyone who is hung on a stake.”
Paul quotes this curse.
The God of our fathers raised up Jesus, whom you had killed by hanging Him on a stake.
Peter uses the same charge.
The angel appeared to her and said, “Greetings, you who are highly favored! Jehovah is with you.”

The angel tells Mary she has been shown favor. He does not say she is the source of grace or a mediator. The greeting “Jehovah is with you” is the greeting Gideon heard. AKS uses the name there so the reader can see which Lord is meant, and it does not call her full of grace.

The Greek verb means to show favor, to treat graciously. It does not say Mary is a store of grace for other people to draw on. An older Latin line, full of grace, turned the favor she received into a title.

AKS says “Greetings, you who are highly favored! Jehovah is with you.” Highly favored keeps the verb as favor shown to her. Jehovah in the greeting follows the Hebrew form of this angelic hello, as in Judges 6:12. The note does not claim a surviving Greek copy of this verse still prints the four letters.
And the angel of Jehovah appeared to Gideon and said, “Jehovah is with you, O mighty man of valor.”
The same greeting: Jehovah is with you.
For there is one God, and there is one mediator between God and men, a man, Christ Jesus,
One mediator, the man Christ Jesus.
He arrested him and put him in prison, handing him over to be guarded by four squads of four soldiers each. Herod intended to bring him out to the people after the Passover.

Luke is dating Herod’s plan by the Passover. Putting a spring festival’s later name into the sentence makes the Bible sound as if that festival belonged to the apostles. AKS keeps Passover so the verse stays inside the feast it is actually naming.

The Greek word is pascha, the Passover. It is the same word Paul uses when he says Christ our Passover lamb has been sacrificed. An older English Bible put Easter in this verse. That is a later festival name, not the word Luke wrote.
AKS says Herod intended to bring him out after the Passover. It does not say Easter. The word is the Jewish feast already under way in the chapter.
Get rid of the old leaven, that you may be a new unleavened batch, as you really are. For Christ, our Passover lamb, has been sacrificed.
Christ, our Passover lamb.
And He took the bread, gave thanks and broke it, and gave it to them, saying, “This is My body, given for you; do this in remembrance of Me.”
The meal Jesus gave is tied to that Passover night, not to a later holiday.
Who then is the faithful and discreet slave, whom the master has put in charge of his household servants, to give them their food at the proper time?

Jesus asks who the slave is. The master puts him over the household. The slave does not take the title for himself, and the disciples were just told not to be called leaders. His assigned work is food at the right time, meaning what the household needs in order to keep living.
The verse is about being found doing that when the master comes, not about wearing a rank.

The Greek for slave is doulos, a slave, not a dignified office. Discreet renders the word for sensible, thoughtful judgment. The master does the appointing. The work is to give the household its food at the proper time.

AKS says the faithful and discreet slave, whom the master has put in charge of his household servants, to give them their food at the proper time. Slave is kept. Servant would soften doulos into a volunteer. Discreet keeps the good sense the master is looking for, rather than a vague wise.
Nor are you to be called leaders, for your Leader is one, the Christ.
They are not to be called leaders. Their Leader is the Christ.
And this good news of the Kingdom will be preached in all the inhabited earth for a witness to all the nations, and then the end will come.
The good news of the Kingdom is preached in all the earth before the end.
just as the Son of man did not come to be served, but to serve, and to give his life as a ransom in exchange for many.”

A ransom corresponds to the loss. Adam’s perfect life was lost, and death passed to his children. Jesus gives his life, a corresponding one, for many. The giver is the Son of Man, a man. The one God and the ransom are not the same person spending himself on himself.
Ransom is the price that releases. For many means the price covers more than one, not that the Son was paying himself. He gives his life. The life is the payment.
AKS says the Son of man came to give his life as a ransom in exchange for many. Ransom is the release-price. Life is what he gives. The verse does not say God died.
who gave himself as a corresponding ransom for all—this is to be witnessed to at the proper time.
The corresponding ransom, the fuller Greek word.
For just as through the disobedience of the one man the many were made sinners, so also through the obedience of the one man the many will be made righteous.
Through one man’s obedience the many are made righteous.

While Jesus was sitting on the Mount of Olives, the disciples came to Him privately. “Tell us,” they said, “when will these things happen, and what will be the sign of Your presence and of the conclusion of the system of things?”

The question is double: when, and what is the sign of your presence and of the close of this system. Presence covers a period. Jesus compares the days of Noah to the presence of the Son of man, days in which people ate and drank and did not notice.
A single lightning arrival cannot be those days. AKS keeps presence here so the sign can be a season, and it keeps come where the Greek word is come.

The disciples ask for the sign of his parousia and of the conclusion of the system of things. Parousia is being alongside. Paul uses the same word for his own presence as the opposite of his absence, and for his physical presence in contrast with his letters. It names a stay, not only an arrival.
A different verb, come, appears later in the chapter and in Acts 1:11. Those lines are not this word.

AKS reads “the sign of Your presence and of the conclusion of the system of things.” Presence translates parousia because the word means being alongside, as it does when AKS says Paul’s presence and his physical presence. Coming would hide that. Where the Greek verb is come, AKS says come.
Verse 30 says coming on the clouds. Acts 1:11 says he will come back. Those are not rewritten as presence.
Therefore, my beloved, just as you have always obeyed, not only in my presence, but now even more in my absence, continue to work out your salvation with fear and trembling.
Paul’s presence, set over against his absence. The same Greek word.
For some say, “His letters are weighty and forceful, but his physical presence is unimpressive, and his speaking is of no account.”
His physical presence. The same Greek word.
At that time the sign of the Son of man will appear in heaven, and all the tribes of the earth will mourn. They will see the Son of man coming on the clouds of heaven with power and great glory.
A different word: coming on the clouds. AKS does not force presence onto it.
“Men of Galilee,” they said, “why do you stand here looking into the sky? This same Jesus, who has been taken from you into heaven, will come back in the same way you have seen Him go into heaven.”
He will come back in the same way. That verb is come, and AKS says come.
And He took the bread, gave thanks and broke it, and gave it to them, saying, “This is My body, given for you; do this in remembrance of Me.”

Jesus hands them bread on the night of the Passover and tells them to do it as a remembrance. A remembrance points back to a body given once. It is not a priest making the body present again. The emblem is bread. The command is to remember him.

The bread is given with a meaning: this is my body, given for you. Do this is a command to repeat the meal in remembrance. Remembrance is a memorial of a death, not a new sacrifice. The verb is remember, not re-offer.
AKS says “This is My body, given for you; do this in remembrance of Me.” Remembrance keeps the memorial sense. The loaf is not said to turn into flesh.
In the same way, after supper He took the cup, saying, “This cup is the new covenant in My blood, which is poured out for you.
The cup is the new covenant in his blood.
For as often as you eat this bread and drink this cup, you proclaim the Lord’s death until He comes.
You proclaim his death until he comes.
He gave orders to stop the chariot. Then both Philip and the eunuch went down into the water, and Philip baptized him.

The eunuch sees water and asks what prevents him from being baptized. They go down into it. That is immersion of a believer who has heard the good news, not a rite performed on an infant who cannot ask. Jesus himself came up out of the water when he was baptized.

Both Philip and the eunuch go down into the water, and Philip baptizes him. Baptize is immerse. Going down into the water is what the verb looks like in a narrative. A sprinkle does not require both men to go down into the water.
AKS says both went down into the water, and Philip baptized him. Down into the water is kept. Baptized is not changed into christened or sprinkled.
As soon as Jesus came up out of the water, He saw the heavens breaking open and the spirit descending on Him like a dove.
Jesus came up out of the water.
But when they believed Philip as he preached the good news of the Kingdom of God and the name of Jesus Christ, they were baptized, both men and women.
Men and women who believed were baptized.
As soon as Jesus came up out of the water, He saw the heavens breaking open and the spirit descending on Him like a dove.

Jesus’ own baptism was in the Jordan, and he came up out of the water. That is the act later commanded for disciples. The spirit descends on him. The Father is the one who speaks in the matching account. Two persons, and the spirit as what comes upon the Son.

Came up out of the water means he had been in it. Immediately the spirit descends like a dove. The baptism of Jesus is the pattern of immersion, and the spirit is again compared to a bird resting, not introduced as a third speaker.
AKS says as soon as Jesus came up out of the water, he saw the heavens breaking open and the spirit descending on Him like a dove. Out of the water is the immersion. Spirit is lowercase.
As soon as Jesus was baptized, He went up out of the water. Suddenly the heavens were opened, and He saw the spirit of God descending like a dove and resting on Him.
He went up out of the water, and the spirit descended like a dove.
He gave orders to stop the chariot. Then both Philip and the eunuch went down into the water, and Philip baptized him.
Philip and the eunuch go down into the water.
And they assembled the kings in the place that in Hebrew is called Armageddon.

The only use of the name is this gathering. It is not a local battle near an old town that happens to exhaust the prophecy, because the kings of the entire earth were the ones summoned. It is God’s war.
The promises that the meek inherit the earth still stand after human rulership ends.

Armageddon is a Hebrew place-name in a vision. It occurs once. The gathering of the kings is to that symbolic place for the war just described. A single valley cannot hold every king of the earth, and the verse does not say the planet is what gets destroyed.
AKS says they assembled the kings in the place that in Hebrew is called Armageddon. Hebrew is noted so the name stays a name. Kings are the ones assembled, which matches the war of God’s great day.
These are demonic spirits that perform signs and go out to all the kings of the earth, to assemble them for battle on the great day of God the Almighty.
The battle on the great day of God.
Then I saw heaven standing open, and there before me was a white horse. And its rider is called Faithful and True. With righteousness He judges and wages war.
The rider judges and wages war.
The righteous will inherit the earth and dwell in it forever.
The earth remains the home of the righteous.
Then God said, “Let the earth bring forth vegetation: seed-bearing plants and fruit trees, each bearing fruit with seed according to its kind.” And it was so.

God tells the earth to bring forth vegetation by kinds, and later the living creatures by kinds. The wording is reproduction within a kind, seed according to its kind. AKS does not translate that as an open process in which every kind is a stage of another.
The maker is still God, speaking.

Kind is the Hebrew grouping, min. Each plant bears fruit with seed according to its kind. The phrase is repeated for animals. The text sorts living things into kinds that reproduce as those kinds. It does not describe one kind turning into another.

AKS says seed-bearing plants and fruit trees, each bearing fruit with seed according to its kind. Kind is kept. Species would pretend the Hebrew word is a modern taxonomic rank. According to its kind is the boundary the verse actually draws.
So God created the great sea creatures and every living thing that moves, with which the waters teemed according to their kinds, and every winged bird after its kind. And God saw that it was good.
Sea creatures and birds, according to their kinds.
In the beginning God created the heavens and the earth.
God created. The kinds are his work.
All Scripture is inspired of God and beneficial for teaching, for reproving, for setting things straight, for disciplining in righteousness,

Paul does not say Scripture contains some thoughts about God. He says it is inspired of God. That is why it can teach, reprove, set things straight, and discipline. Peter’s line, that men spoke from God as they were moved by holy spirit, is the same claim from the writers’ side.

The Greek word is theopneustos, God and breath in one word, literally God-breathed. AKS does not leave that compound in English. It reads inspired of God, so the reader hears the source, not a vague feeling that the page is stirring.

AKS says all Scripture is inspired of God and beneficial for teaching, for reproving, for setting things straight, for disciplining in righteousness. Inspired of God means God is the source. It does not mean the writing is merely moving.
For prophecy was at no time brought by man’s will, but men spoke from God as they were moved by holy spirit.
Men spoke from God as they were moved by holy spirit.
Sanctify them by means of the truth; your word is truth.
Your word is truth.
For the Lord Himself will descend from heaven with a loud command, with the voice of an archangel, and with the trumpet of God, and the dead in Christ will be the first to rise.
The one who descends is the Lord Jesus, and the voice of that descent is an archangel’s voice. There is one archangel in Scripture, Michael. Jesus also has angels subject to him.
The verse does not say the words “Jesus is Michael.” It puts the archangel’s voice with the Lord’s own descent, and the other verses have to be read beside it.

Archangel occurs in the singular. The Lord himself descends with a commanding call, with the voice of an archangel, and with God’s trumpet. The voice belongs to the descent of the Lord. The dead in Christ rise. An archangel is the chief angel, and the Bible never uses the word in the plural.

AKS says the Lord Himself will descend from heaven with a loud command, with the voice of an archangel, and with the trumpet of God, and the dead in Christ will be the first to rise. Voice of an archangel is kept.
It is not changed into a voice like an archangel, which would add a comparison the phrase does not require.
But even the archangel Michael, when he disputed with the devil over the body of Moses, did not presume to bring a slanderous charge against him, but said, “Jehovah rebuke you!”
Michael is the archangel. The word is singular.
Then a war broke out in heaven: Michael and his angels fought against the dragon, and the dragon and his angels fought back.
Michael and his angels.
who has gone into heaven and is at the right hand of God, with angels, authorities, and powers subject to Him.
Angels and powers are subject to Jesus.
God is a Spirit, and His worshipers must worship Him in spirit and in truth.”

Jesus has said the Father is seeking worshipers. Then he says why location does not matter. God is a Spirit. You do not worship a spirit by bowing to a carving or by insisting on one mountain. You worship the Father in spirit and truth. The holy spirit remains his active force.
This verse is about what God is, not about a third person replacing the Father.

Pneuma here describes God’s kind of being. He is not flesh that must be approached on one mountain. An indefinite article in English marks a classification: he is spirit in nature. It does not identify God as the holy spirit, the force he sends. The holy spirit is God’s, upon people.
God himself is the Father Jesus has just named.

AKS says “God is a Spirit, and His worshipers must worship Him in spirit and in truth.” A Spirit classifies his nature. Capitalizing Spirit does not install a personal name. Him is the Father. Worship in spirit is worship that fits a God who is not an image and not confined to a place.
But a time is coming and has now come when the true worshipers will worship the Father in spirit and in truth, for the Father is seeking such as these to worship Him.
The Father is the one who is worshiped.
I am Jehovah; that is My name! I will not yield My glory to another or My praise to idols.
He does not give his praise to idols.
But if a serious injury results, then you must require a life for a life—

The case is a pregnant woman and her child. A fine covers harm that does not end in injury. A life for a life covers the serious outcome. Jehovah’s law counts that life. Psalm 139 speaks of the unformed body already seen by God.
Taking an unborn life is not outside the command against murder. It is the case this statute already weighs.

Men strike a pregnant woman. If the child is born and there is no further injury, the law is a fine. If a serious injury results, the law is a life for a life. The unborn child is the one in view beside the woman. A fatal injury is treated as the loss of a life, not as the loss of property only.

AKS says if her child is born prematurely, but there is no further injury, the man is fined. If a serious injury results, you must require a life for a life. Born prematurely keeps a birth, not a mistranslation that erases the child into a miscarriage only. Life for a life is the penalty when the injury is fatal.
The child is a life in that law.
If men who are fighting strike a pregnant woman and her child is born prematurely, but there is no further injury, he will surely be fined as the woman’s husband demands and as the court allows.
The pregnant woman and the child, when there is no further injury.
Your eyes saw my unformed body; all my days were written in Your book and ordained for me before one of them came to be.
God saw the unformed body.
Jesus said to them, “These are the words I spoke to you while I was still with you: Everything must be fulfilled that is written about Me in the Law of Moses, the Prophets, and the Psalms.”

Jesus says the three parts of the Hebrew Scriptures wrote about him. Micah had named Bethlehem. Zechariah had said the king would come humble, riding on a donkey. Isaiah had said the servant would be pierced for our sins, and the punishment that brought peace would be on him.

The psalm speaks of hands and feet pierced. Daniel’s count reaches Messiah the Prince and then speaks of him being cut off. The identification is a pile of details, not one vague hope that someone good would appear.

The Hebrew מָשִׁיחַ (mashiach) means anointed one. The Greek χριστός (christos) is the same title, not a family name. An anointed one is appointed, set apart for an office. Daniel counts from the word to restore Jerusalem until Messiah the Prince. The title is a person the books were already describing.

AKS reads that everything written about him in the Law of Moses, the Prophets, and the Psalms had to be fulfilled. About him is specific. The Hebrew Scriptures are treated as a witness to one person, not as a general religious library.
But you, Bethlehem Ephrathah, who are small among the clans of Judah, out of you will come forth for Me One to be ruler over Israel—One whose origin is from ancient times, from the days of long ago.
The ruler comes out of Bethlehem, and his origin is from of old.
Rejoice greatly, O Daughter of Zion! Shout in triumph, O Daughter of Jerusalem! See, your King comes to you, righteous and victorious, humble and riding on a donkey, on a colt, the foal of a donkey.
The king comes to Zion, righteous and humble, riding on a donkey.
But He was pierced for our sins, He was crushed for our wrongdoing; the punishment that brought us peace was upon Him, and by His stripes we are healed.
He is pierced for our sins. The peace is bought by his punishment.
For dogs surround me; a band of evil men encircles me; they have pierced my hands and feet.
The psalm says they pierced his hands and his feet.

Know and understand this: From the issuance of the decree to restore and rebuild Jerusalem until the Messiah, the Prince, there will be seven weeks and sixty-two weeks. It will be rebuilt with streets and a trench, but in times of distress.
From the word to rebuild Jerusalem until Messiah the Prince, the weeks are counted.
And I tell you that you are Peter, and on this rock I will build My congregation, and the gates of the Grave will not prevail against it.

Jesus is speaking about people he will gather, and about the Grave not overpowering that body. Peter has just identified him as the Christ, the Son of the living God. The rock the congregation is built on is that identification, not a later religious office.
The word stays an assembly because that is what the Greek names.
The Greek ἐκκλησία (ekklesia) is a called-out assembly of people. It is the same kind of word used for a gathered body of persons. It does not name a building, and it does not name a denomination.
AKS reads “I will build My congregation.” Congregation keeps the people. Church would import a later institution and a building the sentence does not mention.
Keep watch over yourselves and the entire flock of which the holy spirit has made you overseers. Be shepherds of the congregation of God, which He purchased with the blood of His own Son.
The overseers are told to shepherd the congregation of God, a flock of people.

To the congregation of God in Corinth, to those made holy in union with Christ Jesus and called to be holy, together with all those everywhere who call on the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, their Lord and ours:
Paul writes to the congregation of God in Corinth, the people called to be holy.
Husbands, love your wives, just as Christ loved the congregation and gave Himself up for her
Christ loved the congregation and gave himself for it. The object of his love is people.
For it is by undeserved kindness you have been saved through faith, and this not from yourselves; it is the gift of God,

The rescue is a gift of God. It is not from yourselves, so no one may boast. Faith receives it. Faith does not turn the gift into something the person produced. The next line still says we are created for good works. The kindness is undeserved. The life that follows is not idle.
The Greek χάρις (charis) is a gift, favor shown to someone who has not earned it. It is kindness with the debt left unpaid by the receiver.

AKS reads “by undeserved kindness you have been saved through faith.” Undeserved keeps the point that the gift is not a wage. Kindness keeps the warmth of the word. Grace, left alone, has become a church term that no longer says this.
To all in Rome who are loved by God and called to be holy ones: Undeserved kindness and peace to you from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
Undeserved kindness and peace come from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
For the wages sin pays is death, but the gift God gives is everlasting life by Christ Jesus our Lord.
The wages of sin is death. The gift is everlasting life.
not by works, so that no one can boast.
The salvation is not from works, so that no one may boast.
To all in Rome who are loved by God and called to be holy ones: Undeserved kindness and peace to you from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.

Paul greets people who are loved by God and called to be set apart while they live. The same word is used of the congregation in Philippi, together with its overseers and ministerial servants. Holiness here is a calling, not a title granted after a person dies.
The Greek ἅγιοι (hagioi) means holy ones, people set apart. It describes the living congregation Paul is writing to, not a class of the dead.
AKS reads “called to be holy ones.” Saints would sound like a special rank after death. Holy ones says what the Greek says about people still in Rome.
Paul and Timothy, slaves of Christ Jesus, To all the holy ones in union with Christ Jesus at Philippi, together with the overseers and ministerial servants:
The letter is to the holy ones, with the overseers and ministerial servants.
the sacred secret that was hidden for ages and generations but is now revealed to His holy ones.
The sacred secret is revealed to his holy ones, people who can be told it.

To the congregation of God in Corinth, to those made holy in union with Christ Jesus and called to be holy, together with all those everywhere who call on the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, their Lord and ours:
Those sanctified in Christ are called to be holy ones.
and to illuminate for everyone the stewardship of this sacred secret, which for ages past was kept hidden in God, who created all things.

Paul says he was given a stewardship of something God had kept back and has now illuminated. A secret that is revealed can be told. Colossians says the same secret was hidden for ages and is now revealed to his holy ones.
The word is not an invitation to treat Christian teaching as permanently obscure.
The Greek μυστήριον (mysterion) is something kept hidden and then made known. In these books it is not a puzzle the reader is meant to leave unsolved.

AKS reads “this sacred secret, which for ages past was kept hidden in God.” Sacred secret keeps both parts: it was hidden, and it belongs to God. Mystery, in later religion, often means something that stays dark.
the sacred secret that was hidden for ages and generations but is now revealed to His holy ones.
The sacred secret was hidden and is now revealed to his holy ones.
Now to Him who is able to strengthen you by my good news and by the proclamation of Jesus Christ, according to the revelation of the sacred secret concealed for ages past
The sacred secret was kept silent for long ages and then made known.
He replied, “The knowledge of the sacred secrets of the Kingdom of the heavens has been given to you, but not to them.
Jesus says the sacred secrets of the kingdom are given to the disciples to know.
This is a trustworthy saying: If anyone aspires to be an overseer, he desires a noble task.

The desire is for a task: watching over a flock. Paul tells the elders in Ephesus that the holy spirit made them overseers to shepherd the congregation. The qualifications that follow are about character, family, and teaching, not about a chain of ordination invented later.
No one in the congregation is to be called Father as a religious title. One is their Father in heaven.
The Greek ἐπίσκοπος (episkopos) is one who watches over. διάκονος (diakonos) is one who serves. Both words describe work. They do not describe a later rank with a special robe or title of Father.

AKS reads “if anyone aspires to be an overseer, he desires a noble task.” Task keeps the work in view. Bishop would import a later office the sentence does not name. The paired workers in Philippi are ministerial servants, not deacons of a denomination.
Paul and Timothy, slaves of Christ Jesus, To all the holy ones in union with Christ Jesus at Philippi, together with the overseers and ministerial servants:
Overseers and ministerial servants are named beside the holy ones, as workers among them.
Keep watch over yourselves and the entire flock of which the holy spirit has made you overseers. Be shepherds of the congregation of God, which He purchased with the blood of His own Son.
Overseers are to shepherd the congregation of God.
And do not call anyone on earth your father, for you have one Father, who is in heaven.
Do not call anyone on earth your father. The title belongs to the Father in heaven.
After this I heard a sound like the roar of a great crowd in heaven, shouting: “Praise Jah! Salvation and glory and power belong to our God!

The great crowd shouts that salvation, glory, and power belong to our God. The first word of the shout already contains a form of his name. A translation that wants the name known does not hide that form inside a borrowed cheer.
The same short name is why the English form Jehovah is used wherever the four letters of the name stand in the Hebrew Scriptures.
The Hebrew הַלְלוּ־יָהּ (hallelu-Yah) is a command to praise, joined to Yah, a short form of the divine name. The shout is not a word with the name buried inside it.
AKS reads “Praise Jah!” The two parts stay visible: praise, and the name. Hallelujah would leave a reader hearing a cheer and missing whose name is in it.
May people know that you, whose name is Jehovah, You alone are the Most High over all the earth.
People are to know that Jehovah alone is the Most High.

God also told Moses, “Say to the Israelites, ‘Jehovah, the God of your fathers—the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob—has sent me to you.’ This is My name forever, and this is how I am to be remembered in every generation.
The name Jehovah is how he is to be remembered for all generations.
And I heard a sound like the roar of a great crowd, like the rushing of many waters, and like a mighty rumbling of thunder, crying out: “Praise Jah! For Jehovah our God the Almighty reigns.
The crowd shouts Praise Jah again as Jehovah begins to rule.

On coming to the house, they saw the Child with His mother Mary, and they fell down and did obeisance to Him. Then they opened their treasures and presented Him with gifts of gold and frankincense and myrrh.

The men honor the child with a bow and with gifts. That honor is real. It is not a confession that the child is the Almighty God. Hebrews says God’s angels are told to do obeisance to the Son. Angels are servants. Their bow does not make the Son the God they serve.
Jesus himself tells Satan that worship belongs to Jehovah, and to him alone.

The Greek προσκυνέω (proskyneo) can mean a bow of honor or the worship that belongs to God. The same verb is used of people honoring Jesus, of a king’s court, and of Peter. Context decides which act it is.

AKS reads that the astrologers “fell down and did obeisance” to the child. Obeisance is a deep bow of honor. Worship is reserved for the act that belongs to Jehovah, so the two are not folded into one English word.
And again, when God brings His firstborn into the world, He says: “Let all God’s angels do obeisance to Him.”
God’s angels do obeisance to the Son. The bow is commanded, and they remain angels.
“Away from Me, Satan!” Jesus told him. “For it is written: ‘Worship Jehovah your God and serve Him only.’”
Jesus says worship belongs to Jehovah your God, and him alone.
As Peter was about to enter, Cornelius met him and fell at his feet to do obeisance to him.
Cornelius falls at Peter’s feet, and Peter refuses the honor that does not belong to a man.
Then Jehovah God formed the man from the dust of the ground and blew the breath of life into his nostrils, and the man became a living soul.

A soul can die. Ezekiel says the soul who sins is the one who will die. A translation that says “immortal soul” adds a doctrine the words do not carry. You are a soul. You do not possess a second self that leaves at death and keeps on living.
The Hebrew נֶפֶשׁ (nephesh) is a living person or a life that can die. The Greek ψυχή (psyche) carries the same range. Neither word names an immortal wisp living inside a body.
AKS reads “the man became a living soul.” Became is the sentence. It does not say the man was given a soul. He is the soul, formed from dust, made alive by breath.
Look, every soul belongs to Me; both father and son are Mine. The soul who sins is the one who will die.
The soul who sins is the one who will die. The soul is not deathless.
For the living know that they will die, but the dead know nothing. They have no further reward, because the memory of them is forgotten.
The dead know nothing. A soul that has died is not awake somewhere else.
Do not be afraid of those who kill the body but cannot kill the soul. Instead, fear the One who can destroy both soul and body in Gehenna.
God can destroy both soul and body in Gehenna.
“Away from Me, Satan!” Jesus told him. “For it is written: ‘Worship Jehovah your God and serve Him only.’”

This verse quotes Deuteronomy 6:13, where the divine name appears. AKS keeps Jehovah in the quotation so the reader can see who is being spoken of. One Greek verb covers more than one act. A deep bow of honor is obeisance.

The devotion that may be given only to Jehovah is worship. Jesus uses the second when Satan asks to be bowed to as God. Revelation uses worship again when an angel tells John to stop and to worship God.
The distinction is in the English so a reader can see which act the verse is talking about.

Jesus answers Satan with a line from Deuteronomy. The Hebrew passage uses the divine name. The Greek verb in his answer is προσκυνέω (proskyneō), the same verb used when people bow. In this sentence the act is the exclusive honor of God, so the English is worship, not a general bow.

AKS reads “Worship Jehovah your God and serve Him only.” Jehovah is kept because the Hebrew passage being quoted contains the divine name. Worship is kept for this act. The sentence does not say the bow given to Jesus as Son is this same exclusive worship.
Fear Jehovah your God, serve Him only, and take your oaths in His name.
The command Jesus quotes: fear Jehovah and serve him.

On coming to the house, they saw the Child with His mother Mary, and they fell down and did obeisance to Him. Then they opened their treasures and presented Him with gifts of gold and frankincense and myrrh.
The astrologers’ bow to the child is called obeisance, not this exclusive worship.
“Lord, I believe,” he said. And he did obeisance to Jesus.
The man who was healed does obeisance to Jesus after calling him Lord.

topics.label: Obeisance
topics.ask: A bow of honor, not the worship due to God

thoughts.text: On coming to the house, they saw the Child with His mother Mary, and they fell down and did obeisance to Him. Then they opened their treasures and presented Him with gifts of gold and frankincense and myrrh.

The men honor the child with a bow and with gifts. That honor is real. It is not a confession that the child is the Almighty God. Hebrews says God’s angels are told to do obeisance to the Son. Angels are servants. Their bow does not make the Son the God they serve.
Jesus himself tells Satan that worship belongs to Jehovah, and to him alone.

The Greek προσκυνέω (proskyneo) can mean a bow of honor or the worship that belongs to God. The same verb is used of people honoring Jesus, of a king’s court, and of Peter. Context decides which act it is.

AKS reads that the astrologers “fell down and did obeisance” to the child. Obeisance is a deep bow of honor. Worship is reserved for the act that belongs to Jehovah, so the two are not folded into one English word.
And again, when God brings His firstborn into the world, He says: “Let all God’s angels do obeisance to Him.”
God’s angels do obeisance to the Son. The bow is commanded, and they remain angels.
“Away from Me, Satan!” Jesus told him. “For it is written: ‘Worship Jehovah your God and serve Him only.’”
Jesus says worship belongs to Jehovah your God, and him alone.
As Peter was about to enter, Cornelius met him and fell at his feet to do obeisance to him.
Cornelius falls at Peter’s feet, and Peter refuses the honor that does not belong to a man.
And again, when God brings His firstborn into the world, He says: “Let all God’s angels do obeisance to Him.”

A bow can be commanded without making the one who is honored into the Almighty. Angels remain servants. The Son is honored above them. The next lines of the chapter keep that order: the Son has a God, and the angels are spirits sent to serve.
The verb is again προσκυνέω (proskyneō). Here God commands it of angels toward his firstborn. The word is a directed act of honor. It does not rename the Son as the God who gives the command.
AKS reads “Let all God’s angels do obeisance to Him.” Obeisance is the bow. The sentence still calls the one who speaks God, and the one who receives the bow his firstborn.
But about the Son he says: “God is your throne forever and ever, and the scepter of your kingdom is the scepter of uprightness.”
The Son is spoken of as having a throne that lasts forever.
Are not the angels ministering spirits sent to serve those who will inherit salvation?
Angels are spirits sent to serve. Their bow does not make them, or the Son, into Jehovah.
so that in the name of Jesus every knee should bend—of those in heaven and those on earth and those under the ground—
Every knee bends at the name of Jesus.
As Peter was about to enter, Cornelius met him and fell at his feet to do obeisance to him.

Obeisance is not automatically right just because it is a bow. Peter will not let a man treat him as more than a man. The honor Cornelius meant to give is stopped. That is why the word has to be read with the person it is aimed at. A bow to the Son is accepted in the Gospels.
A bow that lifts a man into God’s place is not.
Cornelius uses the same kind of bow, προσκυνέω (proskyneō), toward Peter. Peter’s answer shows the act can be too much when it is aimed at a man.
AKS reads that Cornelius fell at Peter’s feet to do obeisance to him. The next verse has Peter say, “I am only a man myself.” The English keeps the bow, and it keeps the refusal.
But Peter helped him up. “Stand up,” he said, “I am only a man myself.”
Peter says he is only a man and will not receive the bow.

So I fell at his feet to worship him. But he told me, “Do not do that! I am a fellow servant with you and your brothers who rely on the testimony of Jesus. Worship God! For the testimony of Jesus is the spirit of prophecy.”
John falls before an angel and is told, Worship God.
But he said to me, “Do not do that! I am a fellow servant with you and your brothers the prophets, and with those who keep the words of this book. Worship God!”
The angel refuses the bow again and says, Worship God.
“Away from Me, Satan!” Jesus told him. “For it is written: ‘Worship Jehovah your God and serve Him only.’”

This verse quotes Deuteronomy 6:13, where the divine name appears. AKS keeps Jehovah in the quotation so the reader can see who is being spoken of. One Greek verb covers more than one act. A deep bow of honor is obeisance.

The devotion that may be given only to Jehovah is worship. Jesus uses the second when Satan asks to be bowed to as God. Revelation uses worship again when an angel tells John to stop and to worship God.
The distinction is in the English so a reader can see which act the verse is talking about.

Jesus answers Satan with a line from Deuteronomy. The Hebrew passage uses the divine name. The Greek verb in his answer is προσκυνέω (proskyneō), the same verb used when people bow. In this sentence the act is the exclusive honor of God, so the English is worship, not a general bow.

AKS reads “Worship Jehovah your God and serve Him only.” Jehovah is kept because the Hebrew passage being quoted contains the divine name. Worship is kept for this act. The sentence does not say the bow given to Jesus as Son is this same exclusive worship.
Fear Jehovah your God, serve Him only, and take your oaths in His name.
The command Jesus quotes: fear Jehovah and serve him.

On coming to the house, they saw the Child with His mother Mary, and they fell down and did obeisance to Him. Then they opened their treasures and presented Him with gifts of gold and frankincense and myrrh.
The astrologers’ bow to the child is called obeisance, not this exclusive worship.
“Lord, I believe,” he said. And he did obeisance to Jesus.
The man who was healed does obeisance to Jesus after calling him Lord.
